title: P11.20.A RETROSPECTIVE ANALYSIS OF LEPTOMENINGEAL METASTASES FROM SOLID TUMORS: A DIAGNOSTIC STRATIFICATION
authors: A Shah; N Pandey; K Bhattacharya; N Menon; P Bhargava; A Sahay; R Kaushal; O Shetty; S Pathuthara; A Choudhari; A Sahu; A Puranik; I Dev; A Moiyadi; P Shetty; V Singh; A Chatterjee; A Dasgupta; T Gupta; S Epari
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Leptomeningeal metastasis (LM) is the spread of tumor cells to the arachnoid mater, pia mater or subarachnoid space by either hematogenous spread, direct extension from a contiguous intraparenchymal brain metastasis, or through systemic involvement along the perineural or perivascular spaces. LM has a poor prognosis and is characterized by non-specific neurological symptoms which require early diagnosis by neuroimaging and CSF analysis. Presence of malignant cells on CSF cytology provides the gold standard for diagnosing LM. The 2017 EANO-ESMO guidelines proposed diagnostic criteria with levels of certainty for diagnosing LM to guide treatment decisions. With this background, we aim to classify LM into Type I (confirmed) and Type II (Probable, Possible) categories by capturing the broad spectrum of LM presentations.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
This is a retrospective observational study of a four-year period (2020-2023). Cases for which CSF analysis was performed due to neurological symptoms suspected to be caused by metastasis or with some radiological suspicion of LM were included. Primary central nervous system tumors, hematolymphoid neoplasms, head and neck neoplasms (direct extension) were excluded. The Pathology search engine was used to retrieve CSF positive, negative and equivocal cases. The clinico-pathology and radiology details were accessioned from the Electronic Medical Record. Furthermore, subtyping was done on Radiology into linear (type A); nodular (type B); both linear and nodular (type C); hydrocephalus only (type D-hydrocephalus) or no neuroimaging evidence of LM (type D-normal). Based on the level of evidence, cases were categorized as Confirmed LM (Positive CSF cytology), Probable LM (Equivocal/ Negative CSF cytology with presence of typical MRI features of LM and typical clinical features) and Possible LM (Equivocal/ Negative CSF cytology with absence of typical MRI features but with typical clinical features).
RESULTS
Of the 265 cases, 95 were CSF cytology positive (Type I, confirmed LM; Type IA=37, IB=23, IC=15, ID-Hydrocephalus=4 and ID-Normal=16). In 170 cases, CSF cytology was Negative/ equivocal (Type II; Type IIA=19, IIB=13, IIC=4, IID-Hydrocephalus=None and IID-Normal=134) which in conjunction with clinical characteristics were further characterized as probable (n=36) or possibly (n=134) due to LM. The primary sites were lung (n=160), breast (n=80), gastro-intestinal tract (GIT) (n=23), urogenital (n=1) and soft-tissue(n=1).
CONCLUSION
In all, there were 95 Type I (confirmed cases) and 170 Type II (36 probable, 134 possibly due to LM) cases. Lung was the most common primary site followed by breast and GIT. Rare sites included urogenital and soft tissues.

title: P11.21.B CLINICAL CHARACTERISTICS AND TREATMENT STRATEGIES FOR CANCER CASES PRESENTING WITH CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM SYMPTOMS AS THE INITIAL MANIFESTATION
authors: N Hirai; T Tsukamoto; M Takeda; Y Koyahara; Y Hiramoto; S Fujita; H Nakayama; M Hayashi; K Ito; N Saito
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Historically, metastatic brain tumors have been associated with a poor prognosis, with median survival reported at approximately six months. Accordingly, brain metastases have often been regarded as a terminal-stage manifestation of cancer, limiting the consideration of aggressive treatment. However, advances in imaging and systemic therapies have significantly improved the prognosis for various cancers, leading to prolonged survival even in advanced stages. In cases where metastatic brain tumors are discovered as the initial manifestation through neurological symptoms, determining the appropriate treatment strategy remains a clinical challenge. We hypothesize that controlling brain metastases could facilitate subsequent treatment of the primary malignancy and potentially prolong survival. Here, we retrospectively analyzed cancer cases presenting with central nervous system symptoms as the initial presentation treated at our institution over the past 10 years.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
We retrospectively reviewed 13 cases diagnosed between 2013 and 2022, in which central nervous system symptoms were the initial manifestation of cancer. Clinical data, including age, sex, neurological symptoms, tumor size and number, Karnofsky Performance Status, primary tumor site, presence of extracranial metastases, treatment approaches for brain metastases and primary tumors, and GPA/Lung-mol GPA scores, were collected. Overall survival (OS) was defined as the interval from the diagnosis of brain metastases to death or last follow-up.
RESULTS
Thirteen cases were identified, with primary tumors originating from lung cancer (n=11), breast cancer (n=1), and esophageal cancer (n=1). Among lung cancer cases, nine were non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and two were small cell lung cancer (SCLC). In NSCLC cases, the median predicted OS based on the Lung-mol GPA was 6.9 months, whereas the actual observed median OS was 53 months. Even among NSCLC cases without driver mutations, the median OS was 24.5 months, exceeding the predicted survival. In SCLC cases, the predicted and observed OS were consistent.
CONCLUSION
This study demonstrates that NSCLC cases presenting with central nervous system symptoms as the initial manifestation achieved markedly longer survival than predicted by the Lung-mol GPA. Treatment-naïve status at diagnosis and subsequent aggressive therapy targeting the primary tumor may have contributed to the favorable outcomes. These findings suggest that aggressive treatment should still be considered in NSCLC patients without genetic mutations. GPA/Lung-mol GPA scores, which are designed for cases with brain metastases arising after cancer diagnosis, may not accurately predict prognosis in cases where brain metastases are the initial presentation. Multimodal treatment strategies may greatly extend survival in this unique patient population.

title: P11.22.A ABC EFFLUX TRANSPORTERS ARE EXPRESSED AT THE BLOOD-BRAIN TUMOR BARRIER IN HUMAN BRAIN METASTASES
authors: D M Fedorushkova; C C Flohil; O van Tellingen; M C de Gooijer
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Brain metastases (BM) are a common complication of many solid cancers, and their incidence is expected to rise as systemic treatments continue to improve and prolong patient survival. The efficacy of systemic therapies against BM is often hindered by the blood-brain barrier (BBB). The BBB restricts the brain entry of many drugs, in part due to active efflux by ABCB1 (P-glycoprotein) and ABCG2 (breast cancer resistance protein). The expression and functionality of these drug-transporting proteins at the BBB can vary. Previous work in mouse models has demonstrated that ABC transporters can restrict chemotherapy efficacy against glioblastoma (GBM) and melanoma BM, even when the BBB is compromised. However, while their expression has been clearly established in GBM patients, their presence in the various types of human BM is less well documented. We therefore set out to comprehensively assess the expression of ABCB1 and ABCG2 in human tissue of the most common BM.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
A retrospective pathology study has been conducted through PALGA, the nationwide network and registry of histopathology and cytopathology in the Netherlands. Data provided by PALGA were year of birth, age at diagnosis, localization of the lesion, and diagnosis, as made by the local pathologist. Tissue of the nine most common origins of brain metastases was requested: non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC), small-cell lung carcinoma (SCLC), Her2 positive-, Her2 negative- and triple-negative breast cancer, melanoma, renal clear cell carcinoma, colon carcinoma, and ovarian carcinoma. Per origin, 10 pairs of the primary tumor and matched BM of the same patient were requested for comparison. Whenever possible, tissue was selected to be treatment-naïve to avoid potential confounding effects of systemic therapy on ABC transporter expression. Using immunohistochemistry, tissues were stained for ABCB1, ABCG2, IgG - as a proxy for barrier leakage - and the endothelial cell marker CD31.
RESULTS
In general, we find expression of ABCB1 and ABCG2 in the vasculature associated with brain metastases of all investigated primary origins. Expression levels did vary within and across different lesions. Interestingly, in some cases, we observed expression in the tumor-associated vasculature of primary tumors but not in the adjacent tumor-free tissue, suggesting a local tumor-induced expression of drug efflux transporters.
CONCLUSION
The brain metastasis associated vasculature expresses ABCB1 and ABCG2, which can impede the delivery of systemic therapies to brain metastases. Supported by Dutch Cancer Society (KWF) project grant 14736.

title: P11.23.B PSYCHO-ONCOLOGICAL BURDEN IS REDUCED FOLLOWING NEUROSURGICAL RESECTION OF BRAIN METASTASES
authors: T Araceli; A Haj; C Doenitz; E Stoerr; L Winkler; A Fischl; K Rosengarth; P Hau; E Bumes; N Schmidt; M Proescholdt
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Most patients with brain metastases (BM) have a high psycho-oncological burden. This aspect may negatively affect the course of the disease and treatment outcome. Neurosurgical and neurooncological departments treat increasing numbers of patients with BM. So far, no data on the efficacy of surgical treatment on psycho-oncological distress exist. Therefore, we analyzed the extent of psycho-oncological burden in a patient population with BM before and after neurosurgical resection, comparing pre- and postsurgical screening results. The study aims to establish whether neurosurgical therapy may reduce psycho-oncological distress in our patient cohort.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
We included 103 patients (45 female, 58 male) with a median age of 59.8 years, who were planned to receive a microsurgical resection of BM between January 2016 and January 2024. The most frequent primary tumors were lung (40.8%), melanoma (27.2%) and breast cancer (7.8%). Psycho-oncological screening was performed using the Hornheider Screening Instrument (HSI) in 84.5% and the distress thermometer (DT) in 15.5% of all cases. Postsurgical screening was performed after a median duration of 4.5 days (range: 2 - 42 days). The postsurgical Karnofsky score (KPS) was 90% (range: 50 - 100%), surgical complications occurred in 26 patients (25.2%), with worsening of a preexisting neurological deficit (13.6%) and wound complications (6.8%) as the most frequent forms of complications.
RESULTS
16.00 Comparing pre- and postsurgical screening results, 17 patients (16.5%) stayed stable, 47 patients (45.6%) improved, and 39 patients (37.9%) showed an increased psycho-oncological distress. The improvement rate of patients with a progressive disease, both intracranially and systemically, was significantly inferior to that of patients with a stable disease (16.6% vs. 47.4%, p = 0.033). From the population screened presurgically, 46 patients (44.7%) reached a score beyond the predefined threshold and required psycho-oncological treatment. Postsurgically, the fraction of patients requiring intervention dropped significantly to 41.8% (p = 0.020). The postsurgical HSI score was significantly reduced from a median of 4 (range: 1 - 10) to 3 (range: 1 - 10; p = 0.036). In contrast, the DT values did not show a significant change postsurgically (p = 0.431).
CONCLUSION
Neurosurgical resection may significantly reduce the psycho-oncological burden in patients with brain metastases. Psycho-oncological improvement is more evident in patients with stable intracranial and extracranial disease.

16.00 Comparing pre- and postsurgical screening results, 17 patients (16.5%) stayed stable, 47 patients (45.6%) improved, and 39 patients (37.9%) showed an increased psycho-oncological distress. title: P11.24.A DEEP LEARNING RADIOMIC MODEL PREDICTS INTRATUMORAL TERTIARY LYMPHOID STRUCTURES IN BREAST CANCER BRAIN METASTASIS
authors: Z Fan; Y Zhao; G Wu; Z Shi; Z Qin
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Intratumoral tertiary lymphoid structures (iTLS) in breast cancer brain metastases (BCBM) are associated with improved survival and may influence treatment decision-making. However, their non-invasive detection remains challenging in BCBM. We aim to develop a non-invasive model using baseline 3d contrast-enhanced MRI to predict the iTLS status and the prognosis.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
A total of 120 patients with BCBM who underwent surgery were retrospectively recruited from our centre between Decermber 2015 and April 2024 and divided into training and validation sets. TLSs were evaluated, differences in progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) between groups were calculated using the Kaplan-Meier method. Immunohistochemistry and multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF) were used to assess TLSs heterogeneity. After feature dimensionality and selection, corresponding features were used to construct deep learning radiomic (DLR) models for diagnosing iTLS based on preoperative MR. The performances of models were assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). The log-rank test was used to evaluate the prognostic value of the DLR model.
RESULTS
The presence of iTLS was identified in 46.7% (n=120) patients. TLS was positively associated with OS (p=0.0172) and PFS (p=0.0161) in the human epidermal growth factor receptor type 2-positive subtype, and with prolonged OS (p=0.0482) in the triple-negative breast cancer subtype. The DLR model demonstrated excellent performance in predicting the presence of iTLS in training (AUC=0.92, 95% CI: 0.88, 0.95) and validation set (AUC=0.86, 95% CI: 0.82, 0.91). The DLR model-predicted iTLS group has favourable overall survival (HR=0.67; 95% CI: 0.47, 0.91; p=0.01) and progression-free survival (HR=0.65; 95% CI: 0.49, 0.87; p=0.009) in the validation set.
CONCLUSION
The DLR model has indicated accurate prediction of iTLS status, which may assist in the risk stratification and immunotherapy candidate selection for patients with BCBM in clinical practice.

title: P11.25.B CARCINOMATOUS ENCEPHALITIS (CE) AS FIRST MANIFESTATION OF OCCULT EGFR-MUTATED LUNG ADENOCARCINOMA MIMICKING LEUKOENCEPHALOPATHY ON MRI.
authors: D Machado-Sampedro; J García-Domínguez; A Contreras-Chicote; F Arias; N Gutierrez-Alonso; G Lafuente-Gómez
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Leptomeningeal carcinomatosis is an uncommon complication of solid tumors, occurring in a minority of patients with advanced malignancies. However, carcinomatous encephalitis—defined as perivascular (Virchow-Robin space) infiltration of malignant cells without mass formation—is even more rare. The simultaneous presence of both leptomeningeal and perivascular parenchymal involvement is exceptional and described only in isolated case reports. These manifestations usually occur in patients with known systemic cancer, particularly lung adenocarcinoma. Here, we present a unique case of dual central nervous system (CNS) involvement as the initial and only manifestation of an occult EGFR-mutated lung carcinoma, with an atypical leukoencephalopathy-like magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) pattern.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
A 60-year-old female, light smoker with no other significant medical history presented with a 3-month course of headache, disorientation and weight loss. Neurological examination was unremarkable.
RESULTS
Brain MRI demonstrated symmetrical hyperintensities in the periventricular white matter and brainstem on FLAIR sequences, resembling a leukoencephalopathy pattern. Diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) revealed multiple millimetric foci of restricted diffusion with a peripheral distribution, while no abnormal enhancement was observed on post-gadolinium T1-weighted images. Thoracic-abdominal-pelvic computerized tomography (CT) showed a 12 millimeters subsolid lesion in the right upper lobe without pathological enhancement on positron emission tomography (PET). CSF analysis demonstrated mononuclear-predominant pleocytosis and undetectable glucose. Cytology detected malignant cells consistent with lung adenocarcinoma, and molecular testing confirmed an epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) exon 19 deletion. Brain biopsy confirmed malignant infiltration of subarachnoid space and Virchow-Robin space consistent with simultaneous leptomeningeal carcinomatosis and carcinomatous encephalitis. A diagnosis of CE was established and target therapy was initiated with a daily dose of osimertinib but it was unsuccessful, as she developed seizures and rapidly progressive altered mental state. The clinical evolution was not favorable and unfortunately, she died two months after admission.
CONCLUSION
This case illustrates the diagnostic challenges of early CNS-only metastatic dissemination. The absence of mass lesions, lack of contrast enhancement, and atypical imaging can mimic non-oncological conditions. Carcinomatous encephalitis, though rare, should be considered in the differential diagnosis of rapidly progressive neurological syndromes—even in patients without a known malignancy.

title: P11.26.A IS BREAST CANCER HISTOLOGICAL SUBTYPE CORRELATED WITH OUTCOMES IN STEREOTACTIC RADIOSURGERY FOR BRAIN METASTASES?
authors: C Ingram; E Johnson; J Ching; E Clarke; E Simpson; T Sauramba; M Chandrasekaran; J Ninan; R Barlow; S Main
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Breast cancer is the most common form of cancer worldwide with an estimated incidence of 2.26 million per year. Brain metastasis affects 10-16 % of these. Stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) is frequently used to provide local control of brain metastases. It is important to review this in the context of tumour biology and evolving systemic therapies which may have CNS activity.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
Retrospective single centre observational study of breast cancer patients with brain metastases treated with SRS between January 2020 and June 2024. Overall survival (OS) was calculated from the start of SRS to death. Progression free survival was calculated from the start of each individual treatment to CNS progression on imaging (PFS-CNS). Survival analysis was conducted using Kaplan Meier plots and multivariate analysis (MVA) in the “R” statistical language.
RESULTS
85 patients were treated of which 72 were included for analysis due to missing data. There were 81 episodes of SRS treatment. KPS in all patients was >70. Stratification by Luminal A (n=11), Luminal B (n=13), HER2 positive (n=29), and Basal (n=19). Median overall survival was 26.0 months (95%CI: 13.7-32.6). PFS-CNS was 16.2 months (95%CI: 11.3-33.0) in all patients. There was a statistically significant difference in OS dependent on tumour histology with basal type performing the worst (p= 0.047; Basal type 13.7 months, 95%CI: 4.1-n/a; Her2 33.5, 95%CI: 25.1-n/a) There was no difference in CNS-PFS between histological groups (p=0.88). MVA showed that KPS (HR0.60, p=0.002) and receiving systemic therapy (SACT) after SRS (HR0.25, p<0.001) are associated with improved OS. In addition, receiving SACT after SRS is associated with improved PFS-CNS on MVA (HR 0.21, p<0.001)
CONCLUSION
SRS is an effective intervention for local disease control regardless of breast cancer histological subtype. Receiving SACT after SRS is associated with both improved local control and survival. OS differences between subgroups are likely due to factors such as biological variations, patient selection, and the availability of CNS-penetrant/active SACT. This data is consistent with other published work. Further work into the scheduling of SRS in the context of CNS penetrant/effective SACT is required for optimal patient care.

title: P11.27.B EXPLORATORY STUDY ON INTRAVENTRICULAR ADMINISTRATION OF NIVOLUMAB VIA OMMAYA RESERVOIR FOR LEPTOMENINGEAL METASTASES FROM LUNG CANCER: A RETROSPECTIVE ANALYSIS OF 12 CASES
authors: C Zhou; Y Cao
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Leptomeningeal metastases (LM) from lung cancer carry a dismal prognosis, particularly in patients who develop resistance to standard intraventricular chemotherapy with pemetrexed. Although intraventricular pemetrexed via an Ommaya reservoir has demonstrated clinical benefit, its efficacy is limited in cases of primary or acquired resistance. This exploratory study aims to assess the safety and preliminary efficacy of intraventricular nivolumab (40 mg) in patients with LM from lung cancer who are refractory to pemetrexed.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
From October 2022 to December 2025, 12 patients with LM secondary to lung cancer were retrospectively reviewed at the Department of Neurosurgery, Fudan University. All patients had demonstrated resistance to intraventricular pemetrexed: 3 with primary resistance (disease progression within 1 month of initiation) and 9 with acquired resistance (progression after more than 1 month of therapy). Each patient received 40 mg of nivolumab via intraventricular injection through an Ommaya reservoir. For patients showing initial clinical benefit, treatment was continued every 3 weeks. Efficacy was evaluated based on neurological symptom improvement, thin-slice cranial MRI (including black-blood sequences), cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) cytology, and biochemical parameters. The intraventricular administration protocol was approved by the institutional ethics committee, and all patients receiving treatment provided written informed consent.
RESULTS
Among the 3 patients with primary resistance, 1 patient exhibited a meaningful clinical response, with progression-free survival (PFS) of 6 months and ongoing disease control. Of the 9 patients with acquired resistance, 4 demonstrated a favorable response: 2 patients with PFS of 4 months and 2 with PFS of 1 month. The remaining 7 patients (2 with primary and 5 with acquired resistance) experienced no significant symptomatic improvement and were classified as treatment non-responders. No serious adverse events related to intraventricular nivolumab administration were observed.
CONCLUSION
Intraventricular administration of nivolumab via an Ommaya reservoir appears to be a feasible and potentially effective salvage therapy for lung cancer patients with leptomeningeal metastases refractory to pemetrexed. These preliminary findings warrant further validation in prospective studies with larger patient cohorts to better define its clinical utility and appropriate patient selection.

title: P11.28.A HELPING THE DEAD TO TEACH THE LIVING: ADVICE FROM FOUR DECADES OF LEPTOMENINGEAL DISEASE RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIALS
authors: A Franklin; D Aregawi; S Hofer; A Mansouri; M Glantz
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Despite 50 years of intensive clinical and laboratory research, the prognosis for patients with leptomeningeal disease (LMD) remains dismal. Recently, potentially paradigm-changing insights into the cellular and molecular anatomy of the leptomeningeal space, and the genomic underpinnings of tumors metastasizing to the cerebrospinal fluid, coupled with novel therapeutic strategies have fueled a renaissance of interest in this disease. Examining the study design, patient-level data, and challenges from all prior randomized controlled trials (RCTs) may help maximize the efficiency and impact of future trials.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
Using a PRISMA-compliant search with multiple databases, 8 qualifying phase III RCTs were identified. Information regarding study design, patient demographics, eligibility, follow-up, treatment, and outcomes were recorded. Patient-level data was acquired from study sponsors or published Kaplan Meier curves. Summary statistics and sample size calculations were computed using Cox Proportional Hazards and random effects models and an inverse variance technique.
RESULTS
The 8 randomized phase III studies (1987 -2019) enrolled 429 patients and analyzed 412 (51.5 [25.9] patients/study) from 169 institutions (2.5 patients/institution) over an average of 5.1 years/trial. Two patients were screened for each patient enrolled. Only 1 study achieved its accrual goal; only 2 provided a sample size calculation. Treatment arms included, MTX (4), DepoCyt (4), cytarabine (3), Thiotepa (1), systemic therapy plus DepoCyt or MTX (2) or systemic therapy alone (2). Two studies (52 patients) included only lymphoma LMD patients and 2 (108 patients) only breast cancer LMD patients. Overall, 87% of patients had solid tumors and 13% had lymphoma. Primary endpoints included OS (1 study, 34 patients), neurologic PFS (2 studies, 124 patients), LMD-related PFS (1 study, 73 patients), cytologic response (2 studies, 87 patients), and a composite response measure (2 studies, 94 patients). Median OS was 101 (86,124) days for all patients, 85.2 (63,156) for lymphoma, and 103 (87.6, 142) for solid tumor patients. Only 1 study (outcome measure cytologic response) provided class I evidence. All other studies and endpoints provided class III or IV evidence. Sample size modeling suggests that only NM-related PFS is a practical endpoint for future studies in light of accrual challenges.
CONCLUSION
The study design of RCTs for LM has been inadequate, outcome measures suboptimal, patient selection and treatment comparisons extremely narrow, there are no pediatric or leukemia randomized trials, and substantial accrual challenges have dramatically limited study size. All of these shortcomings are potentially remediable, and should be addressed in the next generation of RCTs.

title: P11.29.B WHOLE-BRAIN RADIATION THERAPY WITH DOSE ESCALATION ON MULTIPLE METASTASES, WITH AND WITHOUT HIPPOCAMPAL AVOIDANCE (HIPPORAD TRIAL)
authors: A Grosu; C Schmoor; E Graf; L Frings; T Rothe; S Schneider-Fuchs; O Oehlke; U Nestle; F Würschmidt; M Niyazi; R Bodensohn; F Paulsen; V Lewitzki; J Dunst; E Fokas; S Wetzel; I F Ciernik; C Dietzel; M Ott; L Agolli; C Nieder; K Egger; J Beck; H Urbach; C Lahmann; I Popp
abstract:
BACKGROUND
The HIPPORAD trial investigated a novel method of whole brain radiotherapy (WBRT) with a simultaneous integrated boost (SIB) with and without hippocampal avoidance in patients with multiple brain metastases.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
This was a prospective, multicenter, randomized, double-blind phase II clinical trial (DRKS00004598), conducted across 13 German centers. Patients with 4 to 10 brain metastases (≥5 mm in size) were randomly assigned (1: 1) to receive either hippocampal avoidance WBRT with SIB (HA-WBRT+SIB, Arm A) or standard WBRT with SIB without hippocampal sparing (Arm B). Treatment comprised WBRT with 30 Gy combined with SIB of 51 Gy directed at the metastases (42 Gy for lesions in the brainstem or surgical cavities), administered over 12 daily fractions. The primary outcome was the change in neurocognitive performance in the Verbal Learning and Memory Test (VLMT), assessed three months post-therapy. Secondary endpoints included neurocognitive function at 9 and 18 months, emotional wellbeing, quality of life, and oncological efficacy.
RESULTS
Between 02.08.2016-07.09.2021, 170 patients were enrolled and 136 randomized: 67 to HA-WBRT+SIB and 69 to WBRT+SIB. At the three-month evaluation, 38 patients in Arm A and 42 in Arm B were alive, treated per protocol, and included in the primary analysis. No significant difference in overall learning ability was observed between groups (p = 0.83). Both arms experienced a decline in VLMT scores at three months. At the nine-month mark, cognitive scores improved, with Arm A trending more favorably than Arm B. Notably, depression rates were significantly lower in the HA-WBRT+SIB group at both 3 (p = 0.047) and 18 months (p = 0.048). Arm A also exhibited a trend towards lower anxiety and higher emotional functioning. One year after treatment, the rate of distant intracranial progression was 22% in both groups, whereas local progression occurred in 4% of patients in Arm A and 12% in Arm B. Time to hippocampal metastases did not differ significantly (p = 0.98). Median overall survival was 9.1 months in the HA-WBRT+SIB arm und 6.6 months in the WBRT+SIB arm (p = 0.44). Neurological mortality at one year was 4% in arm A and 12% in arm B. Serious adverse events related to treatment were observed in 3% of Arm A patients and 6% of Arm B patients.
CONCLUSION
This is the first randomized trial to prove feasibility of HA-WBRT+SIB and suggest that it may reduce depressive symptoms in patients with multiple brain metastases. Verbal memory performance showed no significant difference, although patients receiving HA-WBRT+SIB exhibited a trend toward better recovery. HA-WBRT+SIB was well tolerated, maintained strong intracranial control, and was associated with very low neurological mortality.

title: P11.30.A IMMUNOMODULATORY EFFECTS OF PREOPERATIVE STEREOTACTIC RADIOSURGERY IN BRAIN METASTASES: PROSPECTIVE INTEGRATION OF TISSUE AND CEREBROSPINAL FLUID PROFILING

abstract:
BACKGROUND
Brain metastases (BM) are among the most common malignant brain tumors in adults, associated with poor prognosis and limited therapeutic options. Preoperative stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) is emerging as a novel local treatment strategy, promising advantages in reducing perioperative tumor cell dissemination, radiation necrosis, and facilitating corticosteroid tapering. Beyond local control, SRS may also modulate the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME), and potentially synergize with CNS-active systemic therapies. However, the immunomodulatory mechanisms of SRS and its impact on the TIME and neurovascular niche of BM remain poorly understood. Liquid biopsy approaches, particularly from cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), may provide a minimally invasive window into treatment-induced changes and biomarker discovery.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
This study leverages tissue and serial CSF samples from the prospective biomarker study BMX-Rad (Immunomodulatory effects of preoperative radiosurgery in patients with brain metastases; n=20 patients). Analyses include histological and immunohistochemical assessment (e.g., necrosis, hypoxia, immune infiltrates), spatial tissue profiling via multiplex immunofluorescence, and single-cell RNA sequencing on selected cases. Longitudinal CSF samples are analyzed for immune cell phenotypes, cytokine profiling, and circulating tumor DNA. A comprehensive integration of scRNA-seq with tissue and CSF-derived data aims to delineate key SRS-induced alterations in the TIME. All findings are correlated with clinical outcomes.
RESULTS
Preliminary BM tissue analyses after SRS demonstrate entity-specific differences of the TIME, with melanoma BMs showing highest T-cell infiltration. Particularly dense lymphocytic infiltrates are observed after simultaneous SRS and immune checkpoint inhibition suggest synergistic effects. Spatial tissue profiling and scRNA-seq are currently being integrated to resolve spatial and functional immune cell distributions. In parallel, immune response dynamics in the CSF are being analyzed in corresponding serial CSF samples.
CONCLUSION
This study aims to unravel the immunomodulatory effects of SRS on BM, bridging local tissue responses with minimally invasive CSF-based profiling. This may inform biomarker-driven patient stratification and pave the way for rationally designed, personalized combination therapies integrating SRS and systemic treatments in BM.

title: P11.31.B NEUTROPHIL-TO-LYMPHOCYTE RATIO AS AN INDEPENDENT PROGNOSTIC MARKER FOR BRAIN METASTASIS: A RETROSPECTIVE COHORT STUDY
authors: R G Malueka; R A Hartanto; S Safitri; K Dananjoyo
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Brain metastases (BM) remain the most common intracranial tumors with dismal prognosis despite advances in therapy. Identifying accessible prognostic markers is crucial for optimizing patient management. The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), a simple systemic inflammation marker, has shown promise in predicting cancer outcomes. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of NLR in patients with brain metastases.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
A retrospective analysis was conducted on 338 patients with histopathologically confirmed brain metastases from January 2019 to December 2023. Clinical parameters, including gender, age, onset of symptoms, and Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS), were collected. NLR was calculated from routine blood samples with cut-off points of 4 for subgroup analysis. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, bivariate correlation, and multivariate Cox regression were performed to identify independent prognostic factors for overall survival (OS).
RESULTS
Male gender (61.2%) and age <60 years (65.1%) predominated. A higher NLR (>4) was associated with worse survival outcomes. Multivariate analysis identified acute onset (HR 0.670, p=0.015) and NLR >4 (HR 3.465, p=0.008) as independent predictors of mortality. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated significantly better survival in patients with NLR <4 (p=0.004). Patients with NLR <4 also had a notably higher 2-year survival rate (66% vs 32%).
CONCLUSION
Elevated NLR is significantly associated with poorer survival in brain metastasis patients, with a cut-off value of 4 providing the strongest prognostic stratification. Routine NLR assessment offers a practical and cost-effective tool for prognosis estimation and treatment planning in neuro-oncology practice.

title: P11.32.A IDENTIFICATION OF PROGNOSTICALLY RELEVANT IMMUNE ECOTYPES IN LUNG ADENOCARCINOMA BRAIN METASTASES
authors: L Jassowicz; F Heinicke; L Zhu; M Barthel; J Hunger; A Unterberg; S M Krieg; A von Deimling; R Warta; M Zucknick; C Herold-Mende
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Brain metastases are a severe complication for lung adenocarcinoma patients. Immunotherapies build a promising treatment option, but there is still a limited understanding of the patient-individual immune cell composition within these brain metastases and its prognostic and predictive implications.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
We studied a clinically annotated cohort of n = 76 neurosurgically resected lung adenocarcinoma brain metastases for their infiltration by various immune cells, including T cells, B cells, plasmablasts, macrophages, and granulocytes, applying multiplexed imaging of whole slides and cell quantification by tissue cytometry. In addition, broad clinical data, matched bulk transcriptomes, and serum cytokine levels of patients were assessed for integrative analyses with the tissue immune cell quantities.
RESULTS
Our analyses revealed the grouping of brain metastases into four cell-type integrative immune ecotypes, each characterized by a unique immune cell composition and infiltration rate. The immune ecotypes were associated with a distinct overall survival, independent of clinical prognostic variables in a multivariate model. Interestingly, a subgroup of brain metastases enriched for B cells, often spatially arranged with T cells and other specialized cell types in tertiary lymphoid structures, was especially linked to a favorable prognosis. Integrative analyses of bulk transcriptome data further enabled the identification of related gene expression signatures. Our current analyses assess the suitability of serum cytokines as surrogate markers for the brain metastases immune ecotypes, evaluating patient-matched samples.
CONCLUSION
Together, our analyses advance the knowledge of lung adenocarcinoma immune landscapes in the brain metastatic niche and suggest characteristics that could translate to clinically applicable biomarkers in the future.

title: P11.33.B CHARACTERISTICS OF LONG-TERM SURVIVORS AMONG PATIENTS WITH BRAIN METASTASES TREATED WITH RADIOTHERAPY
authors: J Baremans; F Cialdella; C C Hinkert; J J Verhoeff; M J van Zandvoort; M E Philippens; E E van Grinsven
abstract:
BACKGROUND
The incidence of brain metastases in the adult cancer population is rising. Thanks to advances in systemic therapies and evolving radiotherapy strategies, survival rates continue to improve. However, little is known about who these long-term surviving patients are and what their clinical course or outcomes are following treatment. In this study we describe the clinical characteristics of long-term survivors (LTS).
MATERIAL AND METHODS
Data were obtained from the Cohort for patient-reported Outcomes, Imaging and trail inclusion in Metastatic BRAin disease (COIMBRA) from May 2019 until December 2023. Clinical information on survival, disease progression, and cancer treatments during the year following radiotherapy was collected from hospital medical records. Patients were classified as long-term survivors (LTS; >1 year survival) or short-term survivors (STS; ≤1 year survival) after radiotherapy for brain metastases.
PRELIMINARY RESULTS
Within this time period, 481 patients were included in the COIMBRA study. Of these, 258 individuals (54%) were LTS. The median survival time among LTS was 553 days (approximately 18 months and 5 days), compared to 155 days (5 months and 3 days) in STS. The majority of patients received SRS (88% of STS and 98% of LTS). Lung cancer, breast cancer, and melanoma were the most common primary tumors among both the LTS and STS. The distribution of pre-radiotherapy characteristics among LTS—such as primary tumor type, number of brain metastases, and KPS—was largely comparable to that of the overall cohort, with the exception of melanoma, which was more prevalent among LTS. This suggests no clear survival advantage for most subgroups, apart from a possible association with melanoma. Notably, 60% of LTS developed new brain metastases during the first year following radiotherapy, of whom 68% underwent re-irradiation.
CONCLUSION
Over half of the patients treated with radiotherapy for brain metastases survived longer than one year - challenging the historically poor survival reported in this population. Long-term survivors showed no distinct pre-radiotherapy characteristics compared to the overall cohort, except for a higher prevalence of melanoma, suggesting that extended survival is generally not limited to specific clinical subgroups. These findings underscore the importance of recognizing the substantial proportion of long-term survivors and the growing need to critically assess the long-term impact of treatments and optimize follow-up care.

title: P11.34.A LEPTOMENINGEAL SPREAD IN OLIGODENDROGLIOMAS: INSIGHTS FROM A CASE REPORT AND SYSTEMATIC LITERATURE REVIEW
authors: H V Salvotti; P C Cecchi; F Erdini; A Schwarz; P Berti
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Oligodendrogliomas are a subtype of IDH-mutated gliomas defined by 1p/19q codeletion and generally associated with a more favorable prognosis than astrocytomas. Symptomatic leptomeningeal dissemination in oligodendrogliomas is exceptionally rare. At present, limited information is available regarding incidence and risk factors.
METHODS
We present the case of a 37-year-old patient diagnosed in 2010 with a right parietal oligodendroglioma, IDH-mutant, and 1p/19q codeleted; Grade 2. In 2014, due to local recurrence and anaplastic transformation, a second surgery was performed, followed by chemo-radiotherapy. In 2022, a growing contrast-enhanced lesion in the hypothalamic region led to a biopsy, which revealed distal recurrence with TERT promoter mutation. Further molecular alterations (CDKN2A/B, MYC) were not found. The patient was treated with proton therapy (total dose: 59,4 Gy), achieving complete radiological resolution. 14 years after the initial diagnosis, in March 2024, the patient developed lumbago and dysesthesia in the lower extremities. Brain MRI was negative; however, spinal MRI revealed extensive leptomeningeal contrast enhancement along the spinal canal, suggesting metastatic spread. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis confirmed the radiological suspicion. Rapid clinical deterioration led to the discontinuation of palliative treatment, and the patient passed away in April 2024. Based on this case, we conducted a systematic literature review on PubMed on leptomeningeal spread in oligodendroglioma following PRISMA guidelines We included studies published from 2016 onwards and excluded non-human studies and publications on primary leptomeningeal oligodendroglioma.
RESULTS
Following the removal of duplicates and studies that did not meet the inclusion criteria, we identified 13 publications reporting cases of leptomeningeal dissemination in oligodendroglioma. Male predominance was observed among the reported cases (ratio 2.33: 1). in 7 cases, the localization of the primitive oligodendroglioma was available. Among those, a high incidence (87.5%) of tumors located adjacent to the ventricular system was found. Of 6 cases with available proliferation index, an elevated Ki 67/MIB-1 index (≥ 15 %) was reported in 83.88 %. It can be speculated that the proximity to the ventricular system and, thus, to CSF pathway, may increase the risk of dissemination. At present, the prognostic value of molecular factors in leptomeningeal seeding remains elusive.
CONCLUSIONS
The identification of radiological, molecular, and clinical predictive markers is essential for optimizing surveillance strategies and guiding therapeutic decision-making. In patients with oligodendrogliomas located near the ventricular system and exhibiting an elevated Ki-67 proliferation index, MRI screening of the entire neuroaxis may be warranted during follow-up.

title: P11.35.B SURVIVAL OF PATIENTS WITH LD-SCLC FOLLOWED WITH BRAIN-MRI INSTEAD OF THE PROPHYLACTIC CRANIAL IRRADIATION (PCI) - RESULTS OF A PROSPECTIVE ONE-ARM STUDY
authors: S Nawrocki; E Wasilewska-Teśluk; A Sugajska; A Sopel; A Badzio
abstract:
BACKGROUND
The primary end-point was the assessment of patients’ overall survival at 24 months after starting chest chemoradiotherapy. We assumed that follow-up with brain-MRI (every 3-months) and the use of stereotactic radiotherapy(SRT) for early brain metastases will not worsen survival in LD-SCLC patients without PCI. The other endpoints were intracranial tumor control at 12 and 24 months; the risk of brain metastases without PCI; the feasibility and efficacy of SRT (stereotactic radiotherapy).
MATERIAL AND METHODS
It was a prospective, two-center one-arm study (NCT04168281). We included 87 patients who responded to radical chest chemoradiotherapy and had no brain involvment on brain MRI and any progression after completion of chemoradiotherapy. The group included 46 females and 41 males aged 52-84 (median=67). PS of 80% patients was very good of good (WHO 0 or 1), in 20% WHO=2. The first patient was enrolled 03.09.2019, the last 20.09.2024. The median and the average follow-up was 545 days and 650 days (range: 960-2097). The patients had brain MRI and chest-abdomen CT every 3 months. The brain metastases were treated with SRT or WBRT or chemotherapy.
RESULTS
29 (33%) of patients progressed in the brain. 61 (70%) had any progression. The median OS was 22 months, 2-y OS was 44% (95% CI= 32%-55%); the median OS of pts with brain metastases was 19 months and 2-y OS was 24%; for patients without brain metastases median OS was 27 months and 2-y OS 56%. 14 (48%) patients with brain progression were treated with SRT, 11 (38%) patients with WBRT, 3 (10%) patients with chemotherapy and one (3%) with surgery as the first treatment. The median PFS was 10 months for all patients, 8 months for brain metastases vs 15 months for progression outside the brain.
CONCLUSION
The progresssion rate in the brain was lower than expected. It confirms than most patients with LD-SCLC do not need PCI. The OS of the whole group was close to the pre-study assumption and comparable to published results in PCI-treated cohorts, however the OS of brain metastases patients was significantly shorter. The progression in the brain was observed early -most patients progressed during the first 12 months and almost all in 18 months. A MRI (not CT) before starting radical chemoradiotherapy should be done in all patients. The significant proportion of patients with brain progression can be treated with SRT instead of WBRT. Better ways to identify patients with high risk of brain involvement are urgently needed to offer them PCI instead of treating the whole LD-SCLC population as per current clinical guidelines.

title: P11.36.A BARRIER DISRUPTING FIELDS, INDUCING BLOOD-ARACHNOID BARRIER DISRUPTION, ENABLE NON-INVASIVE/EFFICIENT DELIVERY OF ANTIBODIES INTO THE CSF FOR THE TREATMENT OF LEPTOMENINGEAL DISEASE
authors: Y Mardor; D Last; S liraz zaltsman; I Cooper; S Sharabi
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Leptomeningeal diseases remain exceptionally challenging to treat, primarily due to poor drug penetration across the blood-CSF-barrier, specifically the blood-arachnoid barrier (BAB). We previously demonstrated that barrier disrupting fields (BDF), based on pulsed electric fields (PEFs), can be applied non-invasively to induce blood-brain barrier opening and enable efficient drug delivery into mice brains. Here we demonstrate BDF application for transient BAB opening (BABo) in rats leading to a FIH study.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
An in silico model of electric fields distribution in the rat brain was constructed using MRI data, enabling the assessment of BABo levels as a function of exposure to PEFs. The model predicted CSF antibody concentrations based on brain MRI, serum concentration and BDF treatment parameters. To validate the simulation electrodes were attached to the heads of rats and increasing voltages were applied while measuring resulting currents. Voltage-current plots were then compared to the simulation predictions. Subsequently, Nivolumab or Trastuzumab was administered IV before BDF, and CSF samples were collected before and periodically after BDF (15 min to 4 hours post treatment). Various BDF protocols were tested (100-200 50 µs pulses, 0-700 V, 4 Hz, 25-60 sec total). CSF antibody concentrations were used to calculate the amount of drug crossing the BAB per mm2 as a function of local PEFs exposure. These findings were than translated into a human in silico model to plan personalized BDF treatments - including electrode configuration and PEFs parameters - based on individual brain MRI data, for the FIH study.
RESULTS
The voltage-current plots demonstrated a strong linear correlation (r2>0.99) between predicted and measured currents, validating the simulation’s accuracy. The threshold for BABo was determined to be 20 V/cm, consistent with our prior in vitro results. BABo was found to increase linearly with the number of pulses and exponentially with the pulse amplitudes. CSF analysis confirmed significant penetration of both antibodies under all tested conditions, with peak CSF concentrations in the range of 150 ng/ml in the rats CSF following BDF. These results supported the initiation of a FIH study combining BDF with monoclonal antibody therapy for the treatment of leptomeningeal diseases.
CONCLUSION
This study demonstrates the feasibility of achieving therapeutic antibody concentrations in the CSF through transient and safe BABo using short duration (minutes) non-invasive BDF treatment in rats. These findings lay the groundwork for a novel and efficient treatment modality for leptomeningeal diseases.
SUPPORT
Grants from the Israel Cancer Research Fund, Israel Science Foundation and Israeli Ministry of Sciences.

title: P11.37.B NOVEL PATIENT-DERIVED BREAST CANCER BRAIN METASTASES MODELS CHARACTERIZED BY LARGE-SCALE DRUG SCREENING AND INTEGRATIVE MULTI-OMICS PROFILING
authors: C Park; L Jassowicz; R Warta; A M Lenkiewicz; P Dao Trong; C Hong; V Thewes; C Wagner; L Michel; G Jungwirth; A Nohman; A Abdollahi; A Unterberg; A Schneeweiss; S M Krieg; B Kaminska; M Zapatka; P Lichter; C C Herold-Mende
abstract:
BACKGROUND
The development brain metastases is among the most critical predictive factors for breast cancer patient survival. At the same time, personalized selection of effective drugs against BCBM is particularly challenging due to various reasons, including tumor evolution and clonal selection throughout pre-treatments, and novelty and/or multiplicity of driver alterations at this prognostically leading metastatic site.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
To better understand individual BCBM biology and drug sensitivity, we generated novel patient-derived BCBM cell lines from three individuals with triple-negative and three with HER2-enriched breast cancer and tested their suitability as ex vivo and in vivo model systems. We performed a large-scale drug screening evaluating responses to 276 drugs and testing more than 10 dosage points. Both, the cell lines and their parental BCBM tissues, were further characterized by whole genome and RNA-sequencing. Integrative analyses of drug response and multi-omics data was performed together with the patients´ molecular tumor board as part of the Heidelberg CATCH study, a metastatic breast cancer precision oncology program, and clinical data.
RESULTS
Multi-omics analyses revealed that the novel cell lines maintained key molecular characteristics, including major predictive alterations, of the originating BCBM. Further, the cell lines proofed tumor growth in mice supporting their suitability for potential in vivo studies. Overall, the newly established BCBM cell lines exhibited drug responses that closely reflected the individual patient and breast cancer subtype. In addition to the validation of predicted drug sensitivities based on multi-omics data, functional drug response data exhibited the potential to further aid in target prioritization within therapeutic approaches. Of note, individual ex vivo drug responses and resistances overall broadly matched the retrospectively assessed real-life drug response and clinical courses.
CONCLUSION
Taken together, our findings emphasize the critical importance of personalized therapeutic strategies for BCBM patients and demonstrate the value of integrating functional drug screening with multi-omics data. Ultimately, the newly developed and characterized BCBM cell lines serve as a valuable resource for future research.

title: P11.38.A PROGNOSTIC VALUE OF DYNAMIC BRAIN METASTASIS METRICS IN PATIENTS RECEIVING MULTIPLE COURSES OF STEREOTACTIC RADIOTHERAPY
authors: L Horne; D Dehelean; S H Maier; A Nitschmann; D F Fleischmann; N Oberwegner; P Rogowski; J Rübenthaler; S Corradini; C Belka; S Schönecker; S N Marschner
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Optimizing the timing of repeat focal radiosurgery versus transition to whole-brain radiotherapy (WBRT) in patients with brain metastases remains unresolved. Traditional static indices like the Diagnosis-Specific Graded Prognostic Assessment (DS-GPA) may not fully capture evolving intracranial disease burden. We investigated whether dynamic growth metrics—cumulative Brain Metastasis Velocity (cBMV), volumetric Brain Metastasis Velocity (vBMV), and initial BMV (iBMV)—could better guide treatment sequencing.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
In this single-center, retrospective cohort (2018-2024), 122 patients with a total of 817 brain metastases underwent ≥2 courses of stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS), hypofractionated SRS (HFSRT), or WBRT. We calculated cBMV (metastases/year), vBMV (cm³/year), and iBMV (first-interval growth rate) for each patient. Associations with overall survival (OS), intracranial progression-free survival (iPFS), and time to WBRT (WBFS) were assessed via Kaplan-Meier estimates, Cox proportional hazards, and competing-risks models. Discrimination was quantified using Harrell’s C-index, and clinical thresholds (<4, 4-13, >13 metastases/year) were applied to cBMV.
RESULTS
Patients received a median of two radiotherapy courses (range 2-6). Low cBMV (<4/year) was linked to prolonged OS (median 35.4 months) compared with intermediate (16.2 months) and high (>13/year; 13.3 months) groups (p<0.001 for OS, iPFS, WBFS). vBMV similarly stratified outcomes (OS p<0.001; iPFS p=0.001; WBFS p=0.009). In contrast, iBMV did not predict any endpoint (all p>0.7). DS-GPA achieved modest discrimination for OS (C-index 0.552), whereas cBMV and vBMV outperformed it (C-index 0.742 and 0.731, respectively).
CONCLUSION
Dynamic velocity metrics, particularly cBMV and vBMV, offer robust prognostic stratification in patients undergoing repeated SRS. These measures can identify those with slow progression who may safely continue focal treatments and those with rapid lesion accrual warranting earlier WBRT, thereby enabling more personalized radiotherapeutic decision-making.

title: P11.39.B IMPORTANCE OF THE HISTOLOGICAL GROWTH PATTERN IN BRAIN METASTASES. A PROSPECTIVE IMAGING-GUIDED BIOPSY TRIAL
authors: T Araceli; M Proescholdt; K Schebesch; C Doenitz; C Wendl; K Evert; E Noeva; J Hoene; M J Riemenschneider; D Hirsch; D Sparrer; F Lueke; D Heudobler; T Pukrop; N Schmidt; R Blazquez
abstract:
BACKGROUND
The histological growth pattern (HGP) of liver metastases is frequently evaluated, while the same attention is often absent for brain metastases despite evidence suggesting its prognostic significance. This oversight may stem from the lack of a standardized method for assessing the HGP at the macro-metastasis/brain parenchyma interface (MMPIbrain). This is the first prospective, image-guided trial aimed at standardizing the collection and analysis of HGP at the MMPIbrain.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
We recruited 50 patients (21 female, 29 male, median age 62.2 years) undergoing microsurgical resection of a lesion suspicious for a BM. The most frequent primary tumor was lung cancer (n = 23; 46%). Based on the previous trials, our protocol consisted of 4 elements: determination of target areas on the preoperative MRI scan, which appeared suspicious for tumor cell infiltration; identification of these target areas using the neuronavigation system; employment of fluorescein sodium (FL) as a tracer to detect tumor borders; use of laser confocal endomicroscopy for direct visualization of the MMPI intraoperatively. A minimum of at least 70% successful MMPI-specific tissue acquisition was determined as a primary endpoint.
RESULTS
The protocol achieved successful tissue acquisition from the MMPIbrain in 93.2% of patients, meeting the study’s primary endpoint. Exploratory analyses indicated that patients with infiltrative HGPs had a significantly worse survival outcome compared to those with non-infiltrative patterns. Notably, all patients who developed meningeal metastasis had infiltrative HGPs. Pre-operative MRI patterns strongly correlated with infiltrative HGPs, and the laser confocal endomicroscopy accurately visualized the MMPIbrain intraoperatively.
CONCLUSION
Our neurosurgical protocol was feasible and confirmed the clinical impact of infiltration at the MMPIbrain, supporting the necessity to include it in routine pathological reports for the benefit of patients with BM. In addition, this highlights the potential importance of supramarginal resection in brain metastases with an infiltrative HGP.

title: P11.40.A ANALYSIS OF THE ROLE OF SUPRAMARGINAL RESECTION IN INFILTRATIVE BRAIN METASTASES. A RANO-RESECT BASED STUDY
authors: T Araceli; R Blazquez; A Haj; C Doenitz; E Stoerr; T Pukrop; N Schmidt; M Proescholdt
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Surgery is a key element in brain metastases (BM) treatment. While gross total resection (GTR) appears beneficial, little evidence is available on supramarginal resection and its role in BM management. Moreover, given the recent advances in the study of infiltrative histological growth patterns (HGP) in brain metastases, a study regarding supramarginal resection of brain metastases becomes necessary. We, therefore, aimed to analyze the impact of supramarginal resection on BM patient’s outcomes.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
16.00 We analyzed 353 patients (162 female, 191 male) with a median age of 62.8 years (range: 23.4 - 86.2 years) who underwent surgical resection of one or several BM. Patients presented with multiple metastases in 45.5%, singular in 36.7%, and solitary in 17.8%. Fluorescence guidance (FG) was used in 207 patients (58.6%). Supramarginal resection was determined by volumetry of the pre-and postsurgical FLAIR- or non-contrast enhancing (non-CE) tumor volume as previously defined by the RANO resect group for primary brain tumors. In addition, we divided “infiltrative metastasis (IN)” from “non-infiltrative metastasis (NIN)”, according to a previously established radiological classification. Outcome analysis included progression-free (PFS) and overall survival (OS).
RESULTS
264 (74.8%) patients underwent a complete CE resection. In 52.4% of these patients, we could identify an additional supramarginal resection. The extent of supramarginal resection was significantly higher in the FG group (p=0.004). Preoperative non-CE volume was significantly higher in the IN group compared to NIN group (p=0.022). Supramarginal resection improved OS in patients with multiple metastases (p=0.023); PFS was prolonged in younger patients (p=0.020) and in those who did not receive adjuvant systemic treatment (p=0.008). PFS was negatively influenced by residual FLAIR volume in patients without disease control (p=0.035), no adjuvant systemic (p=0.009), or radiotherapy (p=0.027). Multivariate Cox regression analysis revealed age (p=0.013) and the extent of supramarginal resection (p=0.020) as independent positive prognostic factors for OS in patients with multiple metastases.
CONCLUSION
Supramarginal resection was beneficial for both, PFS and OS in specific subgroups of BM patients. Fluorescence guidance greatly increased the extent of supramarginal resection. Preoperative non-CE volume was significant higher in metastases with an infiltrative HGP, highlighting the importance of supramarginal resection in this group of patients.

title: P12.01.B GLIOBLASTOMA RECURRENCE GROWTH PATTERNS - PROGNOSTIC IMPACT AND POTENTIAL PREDICTORS
authors: J A Feldheim; J Grieger; T Schmidt; C Oster; F Julia; E Hattingen; C Hagemann; U Sure; U Herrlinger; M Stuschke; B Scheffler; C Deuschl; C Kleinschnitz; L Lazaridis; S Kebir; N Schäfer; M Glas
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Glioblastoma (GBM) recurrences usually occur locally, but can also develop at a distance from the initial lesion or several sites simultaneously. Although a fundamental influence of growth patterns on prognosis in GBM recurrence is known, there is little preliminary data on prognostic effects and associations of defined stratified growth patterns. Furthermore, possible predictive factors influencing the development of specific growth patterns cannot yet be evaluated with certainty. With this project, we aimed to answer the following questions: (1) Can a more precise analysis of GBM growth patterns in recurrence help with stratification into subgroups? (2) Do GBM growth patterns in relapse correlate with patient prognosis? (3) Can we identify predictors of defined growth patterns?
METHODS
As part of a retrospective study of two neuro-oncological centers, 251 patients were included, and their demographic data, therapy, tumor, and patient characteristics were retrospectively collected. In addition, the MRI images after initial biopsy/resection and at the time of the first recurrence were evaluated and assigned to defined growth patterns, which were then analyzed for statistical associations with a focus on prediction and prognosis with the previously collected characteristics.
RESULTS & CONCLUSIONS
We observed apparent differences in progression-free and overall survival between multicentric and multifocal recurrences. This further supports the hypothesis that these are different growth patterns from other origins. Several of the investigated growth patterns in recurrence showed significant associations with longer or shorter progression-free and overall survival compared to the overall collective (e.g. unifocal local and multicentric recurrences, p<0.05). These observations were also confirmed in multivariable survival analyses in which known prognosis-associated factors were included. Patients treated with TumorTreatingFields after subtotal tumor resection presented a significantly prolonged progression-free survival (mPFS 7.2 months vs. 4.8 months; p=0.03), which was due to a longer time to development of local recurrence. This can be interpreted as an indication of improved local tumor control (mPFS 11.1 months vs. 5.2. months; p=0.01). In the collective after subtotal resection, treatment with TumorTreatingFields was accordingly also predictive for the development of non-local tumor recurrence (OR 0.16; p=0.02).

title: P12.02.A UNRAVELLING THE CROSSTALK BETWEEN GLIOMA AND OLIGODENDROCYTES IN THE HUMAN BRAIN
authors: L Baudouin; M van Lingen; P de Witt Hamer; N Verburg; P Wesseling; j hugnot; B Nait-Oumesmar; L Douw; D A Maas
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Gliomas are primary brain tumors that carry glial characteristics and that maintain an intricate relationship with surrounding brain tissue facilitating both tumor cell proliferation and migration. The infiltrative nature of adult-type diffuse gliomas makes tumor recurrence after treatment inevitable, necessitating novel insights into the interaction of glioma cells with their surroundings to facilitate the development of more effective anti-tumor treatments. Tumor cells migrate over white matter tracts and are thought to cause a loss of white matter integrity. Accordingly, myelin protein has been identified in glioma patients’ cerebral spinal fluid indicating myelin breakdown. Myelin is produced by oligodendrocytes and the oligodendrocyte lineage comprises oligodendrocyte precursor cells (OPCs), pre-myelinating oligodendrocytes (pre-OLs) and mature myelinating oligodendrocytes (OLs) and has remarkable regenerative capacities. It is therefore likely that cells in the oligodendrocyte lineage play a key role in the response of the brain to glioma. Yet, it remains unknown how the tumor microenvironment of various glioma subtypes affects cells in the oligodendrocyte lineage.
METHODS
To investigate this, we have employed resected brain tissue from 12 glioma patients to perform histological assessment of the oligodendroglial lineage in tumoral, peritumoral and normal-appearing brain tissue. Next to this, we also performed cultures of primary human OPCs extracted from glioma peritumoral tissue from 9 glioma patients to investigate whether the glioma microenvironment affects the innate proliferation, differentiation and myelination capacity of OPCs.
RESULTS
Preliminary results indicate possibly higher numbers of oligodendroglial lineage cells (OPCs, preOLs and OLs combined) in the peritumoral tissue of IDH-mutant astrocytomas as compared to IDH-wildtype glioblastomas, while the population of preOLs and myelinating OLs was increased in peritumoral tissue of IDH-wildtype glioblastomas. In line with this, in culture, astrocytoma-derived OPCs exhibit a higher proliferative capacity, while a larger percentage of glioblastoma-derived OPCs reach a mature myelinating stage.
CONCLUSION
These findings suggest that IDH-mutant astrocytomas and IDH-wildtype glioblastomas may differentially affect the oligodendroglial population. To understand the molecular mechanisms underlying these differences, we are currently culturing OPCs with conditioned medium from patient-derived glioma cells. As such, our project will contribute to an enhanced understanding of the interactions between glioma subtypes and oligodendrocytes and may eventually help uncover novel treatment strategies to halt tumor recurrence. title: P12.03.B TRACKING GLIOMA PROGRESSION: BLOOD-BASED METABOLIC MARKERS FROM PRE-DIAGNOSIS TO SURGERY
authors: S Jonsson; C Wibom; H Antti; B Melin; B Björkblom
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Gliomas are highly invasive brain tumors with poor prognosis, particularly glioblastoma, the most aggressive subtype. Late detection significantly worsens prognosis, underscoring the need for early diagnostic markers.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
This study investigates metabolic alterations in blood samples collected at surgery and up to 20 years before diagnosis to identify potential markers for early glioma detection. We analyzed blood samples from 52 glioma patients using untargeted UHPLC-MS/MS. Metabolite profiling targeted 773 annotated metabolites and 164 unknown compounds, capturing both established and novel metabolic alterations. Multivariate data analysis, including OPLS Effect Projection and Discriminant Analysis, was applied to compare pre-diagnostic and surgery samples. Subtype-specific (glioblastoma vs. lower grade glioma) and sex-specific analyses were conducted.
RESULTS
Our study reveals significant metabolic shifts over time, with 518 detected metabolites showing substantial changes. Amino acid metabolism, particularly N-lactoyl amino acids, was notably elevated at surgery. Glioblastoma patients exhibited distinct metabolic profiles, including reduced long-chain acylcarnitine levels, compared to non-glioblastoma cases. While metabolic changes were largely consistent between sexes, some sex-specific differences emerged. Notably, a panel of eight metabolites demonstrated strong potential for early glioma detection, with levels rising well before diagnosis.
CONCLUSION
These preliminary findings highlight the promise of blood-based metabolic markers for earlier glioma detection. Further validation in larger cohorts could pave the way for a non-invasive tool, improving early diagnosis and patient survival.

title: P12.04.A PERSONALIZED TARGETED GLIOBLASTOMA THERAPIES BY EX VIVO DRUG SCREENING: ADVANCED BRAIN TUMOR THERAPY CLINICAL TRIAL (ATTRACT)
authors: A S Berghoff; M J Mair; C Abdel Malak; Z Spiro; A El-Heliebi; F Eckert; J Furtner; F Koenig; A Leibetseder; M Nowosielski; S Oberndorfer; B Prietl; J Pichler; T R Pieber; S Spiegl-Kreinecker; T Urbanic Purkart; A Woehrer; G Widhalm; M Preusser
abstract:
BACKGROUND
When applied within a personalized treatment framework, targeted therapies have revolutionized the management of several solid cancers. So far, various clinical trials aiming to introduce the concept of personalized targeted therapies in glioblastoma have not been successful, as no clinically meaningful responses have been observed. Importantly, most clinical trials investigating molecular targeted therapies included all-comers and concentrated on genetic biomarkers predicting treatment response. Given the biological complexity of glioblastoma, genetic biomarkers alone are insufficient predictors of response in a given patient, and multidimensional personalized treatment approaches are warranted. title: P12.05.B GLIOMAS IN ADOLESCENTS AND YOUNG ADULTS: INSTITUTIONAL EXPERIENCE FROM A UNIVERSITY CENTER IN ARGENTINA
authors: E J Ortega Chahla; M Atencio
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Gliomas are the most common primary brain tumors, characterized by high morbidity and mortality. In adolescents and young adults (AYA), their behavior is intermediate between pediatric and older adult gliomas. However, this population is underrepresented in clinical studies. This study analyzes the clinical, molecular, and therapeutic characteristics of AYA patients with gliomas at our institution.
MATERIALS AND METHODS
A descriptive, observational, and retrospective study was conducted on AYA patients with gliomas treated at the Ángel H. Roffo Oncology Institute (2018-2025), diagnosed according to the 2021 WHO classification. Clinical, histopathological, and molecular data were collected. Chi-square tests, non-parametric tests (p<0.05), Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, and Cox regression were used to assess associations and overall survival.
RESULTS

title: P12.06.A A PHASE 1 STUDY OF TINOSTAMUSTINE, A NOVEL ALKYLATING DEACETYLASE INHIBITOR, AS ADJUVANT TREATMENT IN NEWLY DIAGNOSED MGMT PROMOTER-UNMETHYLATED GLIOBLASTOMA
authors: P Roth; I Moreno Candilejo; M A Vaz Salgado; T Hundsberger; T Janik; M Vieito
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Treatment with temozolomide (TMZ) offers limited benefit in patients with MGMT promoter-unmethylated (uMGMT) glioblastoma (GBM). Tinostamustine, a novel multi-action alkylating deacetylase inhibitor, improves DNA accessibility and impairs repair mechanisms. Tinostamustine following chemoradiation with TMZ (RT/TMZ) in 5 uMGMT GBM patients has shown promising results.
METHODS
We conducted a Phase 1, open-label, dose-escalation study to determine the MTD and RP2D of tinostamustine following RT/TMZ in newly diagnosed uMGMT GBM patients (NCT05432375). Secondary objectives included tolerability, PFS and OS. Adults aged >18 years with uMGMT GBM were enrolled within 5 weeks of completing RT/TMZ without tumor progression. Tinostamustine was administered intravenously over 60 min on Day 1 of each 21-Day cycle starting at 80 mg/m2 escalating to 100 mg/m2 using a “3 + 3” design. Tumor response was assessed by MRI using mRANO criteria every two cycles.
RESULTS
Of the 10 patients enrolled, nine were evaluable. Median age was 63 years, 77.8% were male, median time from diagnosis to screening was 108 days. Three patients completed the 80 mg/m2 dose without DLT. Six patients were enrolled at 100mg/m2; one DLT (low-grade thrombocytopenia with prolonged recovery) was noted. Ten grade ≥3 related TEAEs occurred in 2 patients at 80 mg/m2 and five in 4 patients at 100 mg/m2, including one severe anemia case in each group. When measured from tinostamustine initiation (per-protocol), mPFS and mOS were 4.9 and 13.5 months at 80 mg/m2 and 2.9 and 9.5 months at 100 mg/m2. Measured from diagnosis, mPFS and mOS were 8.5 and 18 months at 80 mg/m2 and 7 and 12.8 months at 100 mg/m2.
CONCLUSION
Tinostamustine following RT/TMZ was associated with manageable toxicities in newly diagnosed uMGMT GBM patients at a MTD of 100 mg/m2 with encouraging efficacy signals. A planned future trial will further evaluate the RP2D of tinostamustine and impact on survival outcomes.

title: P12.07.B RARE GERMLINE VARIANTS CONTRIBUTE TO GLIOMA PREDISPOSITION
authors: A Rosenbaum; C Wibom; A H Suger; R Pensch; A Roy; T Brännström; M Rentoft; K Forsberg-Nilsson; K Lindblad-Toh; S Lindström; A M Dahlin; B Melin
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Gliomas are the most common malignant primary brain tumors in adults and are associated with high mortality, particularly at higher grades. While familial syndromes and common genetic risk factors are relevant in glioma susceptibility, the role of rare germline variants in individuals without a known family history remains poorly defined. Identifying such variants could enhance our understanding of glioma predisposition
MATERIAL AND METHODS
We conducted whole-genome sequencing (WGS) on a cohort of 113 glioma patients from a biobank in Northern Sweden. Rare variants were evaluated within a predefined gene set relevant to cancer and glioma biology. To contextualize our findings, we compared variant frequencies with multiple independent control datasets, including local population controls and publicly available genomic resources. External validation was performed using several independent glioma datasets.
RESULTS
A notable proportion of glioma patients carried rare germline variants classified as pathogenic or likely pathogenic. Burden analyses indicated a significant enrichment of rare variants in genes not previously implicated in glioma predisposition. These findings suggest the presence of underlying genetic susceptibility factors beyond known familial syndromes, potentially affecting a subset of glioma patients with sporadic disease presentation.
CONCLUSION
Our findings support the contribution of rare germline variants to glioma risk in a non-familial context. While specific gene associations still need evaluation, the results underscore the potential for integrating germline genomic profiling in future glioma risk assessment.

title: P12.08.A DECIPHERING WNT6-DRIVEN MECHANISMS OF AGGRESSIVENESS AND RESISTANCE TO CHEMOTHERAPY IN HUMAN GLIOBLASTOMA
authors: J M Ferreira; C S Gonçalves; E P Martins; B M Costa
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Glioblastoma (GBM) is among the deadliest human cancers, characterized by high heterogeneity that renders standardized treatments largely ineffective. The identification of biomarkers predictive of therapy response, and elucidating their underlying mechanisms, could unveil novel therapeutic opportunities and advance precision medicine strategies. We recently demonstrated that WNT6, a key WNT signaling activator, acts as an oncogenic driver and has prognostic value in GBM, but the molecular mechanisms by which WNT6 influences GBM aggressiveness and its impact on therapy response remain elusive.
METHODS
RNA sequencing of two matched GBM in vitro models with differential WNT6 expression provided a comprehensive transcriptomic profile. Bioinformatics analyses, including functional annotation, gene-set enrichment, and ingenuity pathways analysis, identified WNT6-driven biological processes. Functional and molecular assays, along with an in vivo orthotopic experiment, evaluated WNT6’s impact on temozolomide (TMZ) sensitivity, the standard GBM chemotherapy. Clinical data analyses assessed the prognostic significance of WNT6 in TMZ-treated GBM patients.
RESULTS
The WNT6 transcriptome was enriched in processes and pathways that suggest a potential role for WNT6 in therapy resistance. In vitro, WNT6 expression reduced TMZ efficacy across multiple oncogenic features, which was further supported in vivo, where WNT6-high tumors showed decreased responsiveness to TMZ in comparison to WNT6-low tumors. WNT6 expression was also associated with the differential activation of DNA repair pathways critical for TMZ response, including base excision repair, mismatch repair, and MGMT-mediated repair. Among TMZ-treated GBM patients, WNT6 was found to be an independent predictor of reduced survival.
CONCLUSION
This study suggests that WNT6 is predictive of TMZ response in GBM, and sheds light on the molecular mechanisms by which WNT6 may be operating. Collectively, these findings position WNT6 as a promising candidate for future therapeutic strategies in precision medicine, including combination therapies targeting WNT6 and its associated resistance pathways to improve TMZ efficacy.

title: P12.09.B ROLE OF CARBOHYDRATE-BINDING PROTEINS IN CONTROLLING GLIOBLASTOMA STEM CELL FATE AND TUMORIGENESIS
authors: M Sliusar; W Souleyreau; L Guedon; A Burban; A Sharanek; A Bikfalvi
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Galectins (GALs, LGALS) are a family of proteins recognized for their β-galactoside-binding activity, which underlies their diverse intra- and extracellular functions. Some members of the GAL family are associated with tumor development, including glioblastoma (GB). However, their precise role in tumorigenesis remains insufficiently explored.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
SUMO software was used to analyze publicly available TCGA and CCGA datasets. The scRNA-seq data analysis was conducted using the R toolkit Seurat and the SingleR package. As cellular models, we used patient-derived glioblastoma stem cells (GSCs) - BTSC73 and BTSC12. Genetic depletion was achieved using siRNA-mediated silencing and CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing. Pharmacological GAL-3 inhibition was achieved with the selective inhibitor GB1107. Cells were starved in DMEM containing penicillin-streptomycin. Cell viability was assessed by flow cytometry (FACS) using propidium iodide (PI) staining. Cell death was quantified using the Annexin/PI double staining assay. Cell cycle analysis was performed using PI staining followed by FACS. Proliferation was assessed by EDU staining.
RESULTS
We first conducted an in silico analysis for LGALS1, -3, -8, and -9 expression in GB. We found that a combination of high expression of these GALs is associated with the poorest prognosis in GB patients compared to other combinations. The scRNASeq analysis has revealed that GALs are distributed heterogeneously in GB, where GAL-3 is highly expressed in tumor cells, macrophages, and T-cells. We then conducted in vitro experiments to assess the role of GAL-3. Our results revealed that genetic silencing and pharmacological inhibition of Gal-3 lead to a decrease in BTSC12 and BTSC73 numbers, which is related to an effect on proliferation but not apoptosis. Cell cycle analysis demonstrated that CRISPR knockout cells may exhibit an accumulation in the G1 phase 22 hours after seeding. Notably, starvation of these cells resulted in the opposite phenotype, characterized by increased proliferation and a decreased G1-phase cell fraction. We suggest that these effects may be linked to a less effective G1 checkpoint, as indicated by elevated levels of γH2AX in knockout cells detected by Western blot analysis. Furthermore, TMZ treatment of BTSC73 following GAL-3 knockout resulted in a bigger decrease in cell viability compared to the control condition.
CONCLUSION
Our findings indicate that GAL-3 may contribute to GB development by regulating GSC proliferation, cell cycle progression, response to nutrient deprivation and TMZ treatment.

title: P12.10.A RETHINKING TREATMENT DE-ESCALATION IN ELDERLY GLIOBLASTOMA: LESSONS FROM A MULTI-CENTER REAL WORLD COHORT
authors: O Furman; E Falach; I Dvir; O Satra-Shenes; A Bittan; F Bokstein; D T Blumenthal; A Taliansky; L Zach
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Glioblastoma (GBM) in elderly patients (≥65 years) is associated with increased frailty, treatment toxicity, and poor prognosis. Consequently, many elderly patients receive de-escalated treatment regimens, often guided by MGMT promoter methylation status. However, real-world data comparing outcomes across different treatment modalities remain limited.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
We conducted a retrospective cohort study including 573 elderly GBM patients treated between 2009 and 2023 at two tertiary medical centers in Israel. Patients were categorized according to postoperative treatment: (1) chemoradiotherapy (CRT; 60 Gy/30 fractions or 40.05 Gy/15 fractions), (2) upfront temozolomide (TMZ) alone, (3) radiotherapy (RT) alone, or (4) best supportive care. MGMT methylation status and Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) were analyzed when available. Survival outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier and Mantel-Cox tests.
RESULTS
Median overall survival (mOS) was significantly longer for patients treated with chemoradiotherapy (14 months) compared to TMZ alone (8 months) or RT alone (8 months). Among MGMT-methylated patients, combined therapy resulted in an mOS of 23 months, versus 8 months for TMZ alone. In TMZ-only patients, salvage treatment upon disease progression was associated with improved survival (10 vs. 5 months). TMZ-related toxicity was manageable, with grade 3/4 hematologic and non-hematologic toxicities occurring in 6% and 12% of patients, respectively. Lower KPS at diagnosis correlated with reduced treatment benefit.
CONCLUSION
Fit elderly patients benefit significantly from standard-of-care therapy, particularly in the presence of MGMT methylation. Age alone should not determine treatment intensity. Our findings underscore the importance of integrating clinical, molecular, and functional assessments into treatment planning, emphasizing the need for real-world validation of geriatric oncology algorithms.
