title: P13.09.B MOLECULAR CYTOGENETIC ANALYSIS OF CHROMOSOME 17 AND EXPRESSION OF MIR-22, MIR-657 AND MIR-4737 REGARDING AGGRESSIVENESS AND RECURRENCE IN MENINGIOMAS OF DIFFERENT WHO-GRADES
authors: S Urbschat; A Evangelou; W Schulz-Schaeffer; J Oertel; R Ketter
abstract:
BACKGROUND
The investigation of aberrations of 17p and 17q in meningiomas is of clinical interest, as various tumor suppressor genes such as TP53 (17p13) or the serine/threonine kinases RPSK6KB1 (17q23) are encoded here. In addition, previous studies have shown that loss of 17q22 in recurrent meningiomas has prognostic value for the risk of recurrence. Concerning miR-expression, this study focuses on the expression of miR-22, miR-657 and miR-4737 in meningioma tumor tissues and blood samples of the patients.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
Between August 2023 and October 2024, tumor samples from 37 patients who underwent surgical treatment were collected, including 31 primary and 10 recurrent meningiomas. Patients’ blood was taken preoperatively. Using fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), the tumor samples were analyzed for numerical aberrations of 17p13 and 17q22. Real-time PCR was performed to measure the miR-expression in blood and tumor tissues. To evaluate the blood miR-expression, 20 healthy volunteers were included to this study.
RESULTS
However, losses of 17p13 and 17q22 were rare in the investigated meningiomas of all WHO-grades (average: 3.7%, range: 0%-15%), regarding the losses of 17p13 and the radiologically measured tumor volume, a significant correlation was found (r=0.477; p=0.002) and described by linear regression: 14.092 + 3.51*x (p=0.006). Apart of the losses, chromosomal gains were also detected (average: 8.8%, range: 0%-75%). The miR-expression showed that of the three candidates, only miR-22 correlated strongly negative with the WHO-grades (r=-0.669; p= <0.001). The interpaired comparison of miR-22 within WHO-grades I and III differed highly significant (p= <0.001). When comparing miR-22 expression levels in primary and recurrent meningiomas, significant lower expression was found in the recurrent meningioma group (p= 0.042). Regarding miR-blood- levels, the expression of all three candidates differed significantly from those of healthy individuals (miR-22: p=<0.001; miR-657: p=0.012; miR-4737: p=0.047).
CONCLUSION
Gains and losses of chromosome 17p13 and 17q22 were rarely detected in the meningiomas investigated, confirming the literature. However, chromosomal abnormalities were not only observed in high-grade tumors, as often described in the literature, but also as sporadic aberrations in benign meningiomas. With regard to miR-expressions, only miR-22 correlated significantly negatively with WHO-grades. The different expression in meningiomas of different WHO-grades indicates the influence of miR-22 in the tumor metabolism of meningiomas and could be a potential marker for high-grade meningiomas. The expression of miRNAs in patients` blood samples show evidence as potential biomarkers in liquid biopsy.

title: P13.10.A THE EPIDEMIOLOGICAL AND CLINICAL CHARACTERISTICS OF MENINGIOMAS IN AYA PATIENTS.
authors: A Taliansky; O Haisraely; R Spiegelmann; O Nissim; T Kaisman-Elbaz; A Wohl; M Attia; N Atar; E Jan; Z Cohen; L Zach
abstract:
INTRODUCTION
Central nervous system tumors are the third cause of morbidity and the fifth cause of mortality in Adolescent Young Adults (AYA) patients. The incidence of meningioma in this age group is low, 1.5-2.38 /100000 and little is known regarding the characteristics of meningioma in this age group. METHODS

title: P13.11.B INTRATUMORAL LACTOBACILLUS INTESTINALIS-DERIVED METABOLITE ATTENUATES MENINGIOMA MALIGNANCY BY SUPPRESSING ONCOGENIC PATHWAYS AND REPROGRAMMING THE IMMUNE MICROENVIRONMENT
authors: G Shang; s Jiang; H Zhang
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Emerging evidence implicates intratumoral microbiota in cancer progression, yet their role in meningiomas—the most common primary intracranial tumors—remains unexplored. This study investigates the immunomodulatory and antitumor effects of intratumoral Lactobacillus intestinalis (L. intestinalis), a commensal gut bacterium, and its metabolite indole-3-lactic acid (ILA) and naicin in meningioma.
METHODS
We analyzed 80 meningioma tissues (44 benign, 36 non-benign) using 16S rRNA sequencing, validated bacterial presence via fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and isolated Lactobacillus intestinalis. Dual FISH/immunofluorescence (IF) co-localization analysis was performed using a Lactobacillus intestinalis-specific FISH probe combined with immune cell markers (CD8, iNOS, CD163) to map bacterial spatial distribution. Non-targeted metabolomics identified key metabolites (indole-3-lactic acid [ILA], niacin). Functional assays included cell proliferation/scratch/Transwell migration tests, RNA sequencing, and PBMC/THP-1-derived macrophage co-culture systems to evaluate tumor-immune crosstalk.
RESULTS
Meningiomas harbored diverse intratumoral microbiota dominated by Firmicutes and Bacteroidota, with distinct community structures between benign and non-benign groups. Non-benign tumors exhibited reduced Lactobacillus intestinalis (L. intestinalis) abundance. Dual FISH/IF confirmed L. intestinalis co-localization with cytotoxic T cells (CD8+) and macrophages (CD80+/CD163+) in tumor tissues. L. intestinalis metabolite suppressed IOMM-Lee cell proliferation and migration. In PBMC co-culture systems mimicking human TME, ILA /niacin skewed macrophages toward M1 polarization and transcriptomics revealed ILA+TME mediated suppression of cell proliferation, DNA damage repair, and migration-related pathways, coupled with activation of tumor-suppressive stress responses.
CONCLUSION
This study identifies L. intestinalis-derived ILA as a microbial effector that reprograms the meningioma immune microenvironment and directly suppresses oncogenic signaling. Our findings highlight the therapeutic potential of targeting intratumoral microbiota-metabolite axes in central nervous system tumors.

title: P13.12.A WHICH MENINGIOMA MANAGEMENT TO PLAN A PREGNANCY? PER PREGNANCY MENINGIOMA GROWTH STUDY AND NEUROPATHOLOGICAL CONSIDERATIONS
authors: T Graillon; J D’Artigues; R Appay; A Mansourt; M Meyer; K Farah; S Fuentes; T Passeri; H Dufour
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Meningiomas are the most frequent intracranial tumors in adult particularly in woman. They are known to potentially increase in size during pregnancy occasionally requiring surgical removal mostly when located close to the optic pathways. Nevertheless, meningioma increase in size during pregnancy remains poorly studied and poorly predictable. Literature data on meningioma growth during pregnancy are particularly scarce. High progesterone blood level during pregnancy combined with high progesterone receptor (PR) expression of the tumor are strongly suspected to be involved in meningioma growth during pregnancy. In the present study, we first aimed to analyze meningiomas neuropathology and PR expression in the general population of young women, then we measured meningioma growth during pregnancy with neuropathological implication.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
We retrospectively analyzed the neuropathology of 112 operated on meningiomas in women from 18 to 45 years old. Then, we retrospectively perfomed volumetric analyses of meningiomas before, during and after pregnancy.
RESULTS
Among 112 analyzed meningiomas, 100% (39/39) skull base meningiomas strongly express PR. PR expression was more variable for convexity and posterior fossa meningiomas. 86% (96/112) were WHO grade 1. Nine volume measurements were performed during pregnancy in 6 women with a 3D volume increase varying from +68%, +204%, +467%, +61% and +75% in one patient with 2 pregnancies,,+244% and +498% in another patient with 2 pregnancies, +593% and + 0% in one patient who underwent a radiosurgery before the second pregnancy. Despite various per pregnancy growth, all were WHO grade 1 meningiomas. Four were located in the skull base, one in the convexity and one in the posterior fossa. All these meningiomas highly expressed progesterone receptors. Moderate decrease in tumor volume after delivery was observed in one case.
CONCLUSION
These results highlight the very important meningioma growth during pregnancy, which was not clearly reported in the literature. Based on these data, radical treatment is clearly required before pregnancy for meningiomas located close to fragile structures, particularly optic nerves. Most meningiomas strongly express progesterone receptors, including 100% of the skull base ones, suggesting that meningioma increase in size during pregnancy is highly probable for each case. These results suggest a multidisciplinary meningioma management in order to plan safely a pregnancy.

title: P13.13.B IMPACT OF PREOPERATIVE SOMATOSTATIN-RECEPTOR-TARGETED PET IMAGING ON RESECTION PLANNING AND SURGICAL DECISION-MAKING IN MENINGIOMAS
authors: N C Teske; E Barci; M J Mair; E Istrefi; A Biczok; C Schichor; N Albert; T Greve
abstract:
BACKGROUND
In meningiomas, preoperative MRI remains the primary imaging modality for resection planning, often complemented by CT imaging for skull base or intraosseous tumors. However, the advent of somatostatin-receptor (SSTR)-targeted PET promises significant advantages for delineating tumor boundaries. This study aims to investigate if inclusion of preoperative PET information to conventional MRI/CT influences resection planning in patients with meningioma.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
We retrospectively analyzed resection boundaries and parameters relevant for surgical planning including osseous resection in patients with meningioma who underwent preoperative PET imaging, based on suspicion of skull base and/or intraosseous involvement. Initially, the parameters were determined only on preoperative MRI/CT. Subsequently, resection planning was re-evaluated using the additional information provided by PET imaging. Imaging analyses were conducted using Brainlab Elements software.
RESULTS
50 patients met the inclusion criteria: 29 skull base, 12 convexity and 9 parafalcine meningiomas were identified. The extent of planned tumor resection was modified in the majority of cases (30/50, 60%) after re-evaluating surgical planning with PET imaging. In these patients, planned tumor volumes were mainly altered in meningiomas located at the skull base (19/30, 63.3%), and in tumors with intraosseous involvement (27/30, 90.0%). In detail, in 25/30 patients (83.3%) planned tumor volume increased while it decreased in 5/30 cases (16.6%). Across all patients, median tumor volumes showed an increase after reviewing PET imaging of 0.35 cm³ (p = 0.0001). PET imaging identified the need for further tumor resection to achieve complete resection (Simpson grade 1) in 6/50 patients (12%), who were initially considered completely resectable using MRI/CT-based planning.
CONCLUSION
Our study shows that preoperative PET imaging may significantly adjust and extend resection boundaries in meningiomas, particularly in cases of skull base and intraosseous meningiomas. Our data highlights the potential limitation of MRI/CT-based planning alone, which may result in an incomplete resection plan. These findings suggest that PET imaging serves as a promising preoperative diagnostic tool that could enhance surgical precision in meningioma surgery, particularly in complex meningioma cases. Whether integrating PET into the standard preoperative evaluation improves patient outcomes should be addressed in future studies.

title: P13.14.A REGORAFENIB VERSUS LOCAL STANDARD OF CARE IN PATIENTS WITH GRADE 2-3 MENINGIOMA NO LONGER ELIGIBLE FOR LOCO-REGIONAL TREATMENTS: THE MIRAGE TRIAL
authors: A Bosio; G Cerretti; M Padovan; P Del Bianco; M Polano; S Mandruzzato; S Indraccolo; R Manara; G Librizzi; M Caccese; M Corra’; M Maccari; S Lonardi; G De Salvo; G Lombardi
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Meningiomas are the most common intracranial tumors. Standard treatment involves surgical resection with curative intent. When gross total resection is not achievable, or in case of recurrence, RT is frequently utilized. On the other hand, the role of systemic treatments remains poorly supported by evidence. Regorafenib is an oral multi-tyrosine kinase (RTK) inhibitor. It exhibits high selectivity for VEGFR1/2/3, while also inhibiting PDGFRβ, FGFR1, and c-RAF/RAF1 and BRAF pathways, highly expressed in high-grade meningiomas.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
The MIRAGE Trial (NCT06275919) is a multicenter, open-label, randomized phase 2 clinical trial evaluating grade 2/3 meningioma pts who have progressed following surgery and RT. A total of 94 pts are being randomized (1: 1) to receive either regorafenib (160 mg orally for 3 weeks on, 1 week off) or local standard-of-care therapies (e.g., bevacizumab, hydroxyurea, somatostatin analogues). Major inclusion criteria include histological confirmation of WHO 2021 grade 2-3 meningioma, radiologically documented progression at least 24 weeks from RT (estimated planar growth >25% in two dimensional tumor areas within the prior 12 months or development of a new lesion) with at least 1 measurable lesion (minimum 10 x 10 mm) on baseline MRI, ineligibility for further surgery and/or radiotherapy, absence of extracranial lesions and a WHO performance status of 0-1. The primary endpoint is 6-month PFS (6m-PFS). Assuming a 6m-PFS of 20% in the control arm and 40% in the regorafenib arm (corresponding to a HR=0.57) with α=5%, β=85%, 104 patients are needed to assess the targeted efficacy. Response to treatment will be assessed by using RANO criteria. Secondary endpoints include OS, ORR, DCR, volumetric analysis of the target lesions, safety and health-related quality of life. Multi-omics exploratory analysis will also be performed to investigate possible prognostic and predictive biomarkers. Radiomics analysis will also be performed. MIRAGE, initiated in September 2024, is an academic trial promoted by the Istituto Oncologico Veneto, IOV-IRCCS and will recruit patients across 15 neuro-oncology Centers in Italy with an estimated study duration of 18 months. To date, 20 pts have been enrolled across all currently active Centers.
CONCLUSIONS
MIRAGE is the first randomized phase 2 trial analyzing the role of a RTK inhibitor (regorafenib) in prolonging PFS in pts with grade 2-3 meningioma who are ineligible for further surgery and/or radiotherapy.

title: P13.15.B STRONG EVIDENCES TO TARGET YAP1/TAZ-TEAD IN MENINGIOMA: PRECLINICAL STUDY.
authors: G Mondielli; S Delaporte; R Appay; A Mansourt; T Charnay; A Querdray; M Lagarde; C Roche; E Tabouret; T Graillon; A Soude; A Barlier
abstract:
BACKGROUND
the therapeutic management for recurrent meningioma remains an unmet need. Accumulating evidences over few years highlight the interest of targeting HIPPO pathway in cancers and more specifically the final effector complex: YAP1/TAZ-TEAD transcription factors. Biallelic inactivation of NF2 is the initiating event in the around 60 % of sporadic meningiomas. NF2/Merlin loss is associated also to an inactivation of the HIPPO repressor pathway inducing a YAP1/TAZ-TEAD transcriptional activity.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
using 3 different meningioma cell lines and a large series of fresh meningiomas, the role of the Hippo pathway was studied on 91 meningiomas, well characterized at clinical, histological and molecular level. The genomic profile, target transcripts of the complex YAP1/TAZ-TEADs, cell viability, and cell proliferation were analyzed after i) siRNA transfection targeting YAP1, TAZ, YAP1+TAZ and TEADs and ii) after treatment with six YAP1/TAZ-TEADs inhibitors (IV1 to IV6) or combined with MAPKinase (Trametinib) or Pi3K-AKT-mTOR (Everolimus) inhibitors.
RESULTS
inactivation of the YAP1/TAZ-TEAD by siRNA or by IV3 and IV6 who bind to the TEAD Ω-loop pocket inhibits cell proliferation and weakly affects cell viability. The transcriptional inhibition of CTGF and CYR61 targeted genes by these siRNA or by IV3 or IV6 demonstrate the engagement of YAP1/TAZ-TEAD complex in this effect. These effects were observed in NF2 deficient (def) and in NF2 wild type (wt) tumors. The higher expression of TEAD target genes CTGF and CYR61 in NF2def tumors vs NF2wt ones, supported the higher activity of YAP1/TAZ-TEAD transcriptional activity in NF2def tumors. However more that NF2 mutation, the NF2 protein level seems crucial since an inverse correlation between NF2 protein level and CTGF mRNA was observed. Combination of YAP1/TAZ-TEADs inhibitors with MAPKinase or Pi3K-AKT-mTOR inhibitors induced a significant stronger decrease in cell proliferation than each drug alone. An additive effect was observed between IV3 and IV6 and Everolimus or Trametinib.
CONCLUSION
Conclusion: our study highlights the potential therapeutic interest of targeting YAP1/TAZ-TEAD activity to control tumor growth of meningiomas, and to set up a clinical trial not only in NF2def tumors but in all meningiomas and suggests the potential interest of a co-targeting therapy with MAPKinase or Pi3K-AKT-mTOR inhibitors. This work was supported by Inventiva.

title: P13.16.A MENINGIOMAS IN ADOLESCENTS AND YOUNG ADULTS: CLINICAL, HISTOPATHOLOGICAL, AND MOLECULAR CHARACTERIZATION.
authors: I Bartolomé-Asensio; I Manzano-Benito; K Carrasco; G Yunge del Pozo; E Martínez-Zamorano; M Mollejo; Á Rodríguez de Lope; B Meléndez
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Meningiomas are the most common type of primary intracranial tumor, characterized by slow growth and predominantly benign nature. Although typically diagnosed in older adults (median age 66 years), their occurrence in younger patients is rare and poorly characterized. Limited studies in Adolescents and Young Adults (AYAs) have raised questions about potential differences in clinical behavior and histopathological features. Moreover, molecular drivers in this population remain insufficiently explored. We aimed to comprehensively characterize a cohort of young patients with meningiomas and compare their profiles to those of older adults.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
We retrospectively analyzed meningioma cases treated at our hospital between 2018-2025. Out of 201 patients, 15 were aged 15-40 years at diagnosis. Clinical data (age, sex, symptoms, status, tumor location, recurrence, overall survival [OS], recurrence-free survival [RFS]) and histopathological variables (WHO grade, subtype) were obtained from electronic medical records. Molecular analyses were conducted using targeted next-generation sequencing for mutations (SNVs, indels) and copy number variations (CNVs), and FISH for chromosomal/gene alterations (CDKN2A homozygous deletion). Results were compared with published data on older adults.
RESULTS
The mean age at diagnosis was 36.1 years (range 14-40), with a female-to-male ratio of 4: 1. Headache (40%) and seizures (33%) were the most common symptoms. Tumors were located in the skull base (40%), convexity (33%), midline (20%), and intraventricular region (7%). Median follow-up was 2.75 years. No deaths occurred, and two patients (13%) had recurrences, one with histological progression. OS at five years was 100%, with a mean RFS of 2.6 years; 87% of patients were disease-free at last follow-up. Histologically, 86% of tumors were WHO grade 1, 7% grade 2, and 7% grade 3. NF2 mutations were found in 45% of patients, all with 22q loss; four also showed 1p loss. AKT1 mutations were detected in two cases, and one tumor showed co-mutations in TRAF7 and KLF4. Variants of uncertain significance were detected in EGFR, ATRX, and SUFU. CNVs showed loss of 22q (64%), 1p (45%), and 19q (18%). One tumor initially grade 1 recurred with CDKN2A homozygous deletion and progressed to grade 3.

Although typically diagnosed in older adults (median age 66 years), their occurrence in younger patients is rare and poorly characterized. title: P13.17.B HUMAN MENINGIOMA TUMOR MODELS REVEAL GRADE-SPECIFIC MICROENVIRONMENTAL INTERACTIONS
authors: A O Mohammed; K Joseph; D Depro; G Nishita; V Jariwala; A Boecke; M Al Shhab; I Vasilikos; J M Nakagawa; T Juratli; R Roelz; M Shah; J Beck; J Grauvogel; V M Ravi
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Meningiomas represent the most common primary intracranial tumors, accounting for approximately one-third of adult CNS tumors. Despite their frequency, model systems that accurately replicate the complex tumor-microenvironment interactions across meningioma grades remain underdeveloped, limiting translational progress. This study aimed to establish and characterize human meningioma tumor models to interrogate grade-specific cellular behaviors and microenvironmental dynamics
MATERIAL AND METHODS
Patient-derived meningioma cell lines were established through mechanical and enzymatic dissociation of surgically resected tumors, followed by expansion in specialized culture media. GFP transfection was performed to enable live-cell tracking. For ex vivo modeling, human neocortical slices — obtained from access tissue from non-meningioma surgeries, either 2 cm distal to the glioma core or from epilepsy surgeries under neuronavigation guidance — were injected with GFP-labeled meningioma cells. Tumor progression, cluster formation, and tissue integration were assessed over six days using longitudinal live imaging and immunofluorescence staining. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was employed to resolve cellular heterogeneity and tumor-microenvironmental interactions. Machine learning-based image segmentation combined with manual curation enabled precise quantification of tumor cell distribution and interaction patterns within the host tissue.
RESULTS
Grade 3 meningioma cells demonstrated significantly enhanced cluster formation, tissue invasion, and microenvironmental remodeling compared to lower-grade counterparts. Ex vivo models recapitulated patient tumor behaviors, with scRNA-seq revealing upregulation of genes associated with mesenchymal transition, extracellular matrix remodeling, and immune modulation in Grade 3 tumors. Microenvironmental analysis indicated that higher-grade tumors established more extensive cell-cell interaction networks and induced greater astrocytic and microglial activation relative to Grade 1 and 2 models. Furthermore, immune profiling revealed a more immunosuppressive environment, with myeloid-derived suppressor cells, reducing immune surveillance and facilitating tumor evasion. Additionally, there was increased activation of astrocytes and microglia, contributing to a supportive tumor microenvironment.
CONCLUSION
Our patient-derived meningioma models reveal grade-specific differences in tumor behavior and TME interactions. Grade 3 meningiomas show aggressive clustering and microenvironmental remodeling, offering insights into malignant progression. These models provide a high-fidelity platform for studying tumor biology and preclinical evaluation of therapies targeting tumor-stroma interactions

title: P13.18.A MENINGIOMAP: A SINGLE-CELL ATLAS OF MENINGIOMA ECOSYSTEMS AND MICROENVIRONMENTAL NETWORKS
authors: A Boecke; A O Mohammed; D Das; G Nishita; R Roelz; M Shah; T Juratli; J Beck; J Grauvogel; K Joseph; V M Ravi
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Meningiomas are the most common primary intracranial tumors, yet their cellular diversity, tumor-stroma interactions, and the relationship between neoplastic and normal meningeal cells remain incompletely understood. While recent studies have provided valuable single-cell insights into specific tumor contexts, a unified atlas encompassing both meningioma and healthy meningeal tissue across patients and studies is lacking.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
We constructed MeningioMap, a comprehensive single-cell atlas by harmonizing three publicly available datasets with in-house single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of surgically resected meningiomas and matched adjacent meningeal tissue. The dataset encompasses over 300,000 high-quality cells from 40+ patients, spanning diverse tumor grades, anatomical locations, histopathological subtypes, and genders. Standardized preprocessing, robust batch correction, and integrative clustering pipelines were employed. Preliminary spatial transcriptomic analyses further validated key tumor-stromal interactions predicted from scRNA-seq profile.
RESULTS
Meningioma delineates a high-resolution taxonomy of malignant and non-malignant cell states within the meningioma ecosystem. We identified distinct malignant subpopulations characterized by specific copy number alterations, transcriptional programs, and clinical associations with tumor grade. Comparative analysis with matched meninges uncovered conserved meningeal lineages and unveiled tumor-specific reprogramming events. Spatial transcriptomics confirmed localized immune remodeling and stromal activation signatures at the tumor-meninges interface. Notably, we identified a novel transitional malignant-stromal phenotype enriched in invasive tumor fronts, suggesting a potential driver of recurrence and therapeutic resistance.
CONCLUSION
MeningioMap represents the most extensive single-cell resource for meningioma and meningeal research to date. Beyond offering a foundational reference for tumor heterogeneity and cellular dynamics, it provides critical insights into tumor-microenvironment crosstalk, informing future strategies for precision diagnostics, risk stratification, and targeted therapeutic development. An interactive, publicly accessible portal will facilitate broad scientific and clinical utility.

title: P13.19.B PUSHING THE LIMITS: CARBON ION RE-IRRADIATION FOR RECURRENT MENINGIOMAS FOLLOWING PREVIOUS HIGH-DOSE PHOTON RADIOTHERAPY
authors: M Y Deng; J Debus; L König
abstract:
BACKGROUND
The management of recurrent meningiomas following prior high-dose photon radiotherapy remains a substantial clinical challenge due to limited treatment options and concerns regarding cumulative toxicity. Carbon ion radiotherapy, characterized by its steep dose gradient and superior relative biological effectiveness (RBE), offers a promising salvage modality in this context.
METHODS
We retrospectively analyzed 64 patients treated with carbon ion re-irradiation for recurrent intracranial meningiomas between 2011 and 2024. Treatment was administered in 13-17 fractions, with a per-fraction dose of 3 Gy (RBE), corresponding to an EQD2 range of 48.8-63.8 Gy (RBE). Dose prescription was individualized based on the time interval since prior radiotherapy and cumulative dose within the target volume. Tumor progression was assessed according to the Response Assessment in Neuro-Oncology (RANO) criteria.
RESULTS
The median follow-up was 18 months (range: 3-112 months). All patients had previously received high-dose photon radiotherapy, with a median dose of 54 Gy. The median interval between the initial and re-irradiation treatments was 68.5 months (range: 12-295 months). The majority of patients had WHO grade 2 meningiomas (n=41), followed by grade 1 (n=16) and grade 3 (n=7). The 2-year local control rate was 57.7%, and the 2-year overall survival rate was 93.6%. Radiation necrosis occurred in 17 patients (26.6%), all initially managed with corticosteroids; three required escalation to bevacizumab.
CONCLUSION
Carbon ion re-irradiation appears to be a feasible and effective salvage treatment for recurrent meningiomas following high-dose photon radiotherapy. Early results demonstrate promising local control with an acceptable toxicity profile. Ongoing analyses, including volumetric assessment and molecular profiling, aim to refine risk stratification and optimize patient selection.

title: P13.20.A SPATIAL HETEROGENEITY OF METHYLATION CLASSES IN MENINGIOMAS: IMPACT ON CLASSIFICATION ACCURACY AND CLINICAL PROGNOSIS
authors: F Zettl; A Shmatko; A Patel; F Keller; F E Hinz; S L Maas; L Schweizer; M Preusser; N Berghaus; A von Deimling; M Gerstung; I Bludau; F Sahm
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Meningiomas are the most frequent primary central nervous system tumors and are predominantly benign. Although the risk of tumor recurrence generally correlates with malignancy, some patients with histologically benign meningiomas also experience recurrence. Methylation classification promises to improve risk prediction in meningiomas. However, the relationship between methylation patterns and clinical behavior remains incompletely understood. We hypothesize that intra-tumoral heterogeneity may confound methylation classification and influence clinical outcomes.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
To investigate our hypotheses, we applied an attention-based multi-instance learning model named Hetairos previously validated to predict methylation classes, to infer methylation class distribution on hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) stained whole slide images. We validated the in-silico predictions by molecular analyses, including methylation classification on selectively sampled tissue and immunohistochemistry (IHC) staining. For quantification, we defined intra-tumoral heterogeneity as the presence and abundance of multiple predicted methylation classes within individual tumors. We correlated the extent of heterogeneity with clinical outcomes such as recurrence rates and progression-free survival in a cohort of over 200 meningioma patients across different centers with tumors of benign or intermediate methylation classification.
RESULTS
We successfully validated the predictions of Hetairos by confirming the presence of heterogeneous tumor regions through comparative molecular methylation profiling and IHC staining of cases displaying high intra-tumoral heterogeneity. By stratifying patients into purely benign versus heterogeneous benign/intermediate groups based on in-silico methylation prediction, we found that tumors with high intra-tumoral heterogeneity experienced significantly higher recurrence rates and shorter progression-free survival compared to homogeneous ones. These findings suggest that spatial heterogeneity in methylation classification has clinical significance and may explain recurrence in tumors initially classified as benign.
CONCLUSION
Our analyses confirm that some meningiomas show high intra-tumoral heterogeneity for methylation classes, here spatially illustrated with an attention-based image model, interfering with accurate methylation-based classification that can lead to a clinically relevant misdiagnosis towards a more benign tumor phenotype. Recognizing and quantifying heterogeneity could improve risk stratification and guide postoperative management. Further validation in larger cohorts is warranted to establish the assessment of presence and spatial latitude for multiple methylation classes as a prognostically relevant factor for meningioma patients.

title: P14.01.B HEMANGIOBLASTOMATOSIS ASSOCIATED WITH VON HIPPEL LINDAU SYNDROME, CASE SERIES
authors: L E SUSSMANN - ESTRADA; E JARAMILLO-JIMENEZ; M TORRES-BUSTAMANTE; J H MONTENEGRO-MUÑÓZ; C E RIVAS-CHARA; L POSADA-YEPES; J E RODRIGUEZ-DÁVILA
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Hemangioblastomas (HB) are benign, grade 1, highly vascularized tumors, representing 3% of primary neoplasms of the central nervous system (CNS) and 7-12% of posterior fossa lesions. Approximately 30% of cases are associated with Von Hippel Lindau syndrome (VHL), with 25% of patients presenting multiple and recurrent lesions. Hemangioblastomatosis is an extremely rare condition characterized by leptomeningeal dissemination of HB and a tendency for recurrence, resulting in severe neurological outcomes.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
A retrospective case series was conducted. We analyzed sociodemographic data, medical history, clinical manifestations, radiological findings, treatment approaches, and follow-up outcomes. Diagnosis of hemangioblastomatosis was established based on radiological evidence of multiple HB lesions with leptomeningeal involvement.
RESULTS
Eight cases were identified (6 women, 2 men), with an age range of 29-49 years. The predominant clinical manifestations at diagnosis were severe progressive headache and posterior fossa symptoms. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed cerebellar lesions in all cases, spinal cord involvement in 5 patients, and medulla oblongata lesions in 2 patients. VHL was confirmed in 4 cases through genetic testing showing pathogenic heterozygous variants, and in 3 additional cases through family history and multiple angiomatosis. Six patients underwent multiple surgical resections, one received endoscopic ventriculostomy, two underwent fractionated CyberKnife radiotherapy, and one received cervical radiotherapy. One patient was treated with bevacizumab. The median follow-up period was 8.5 years (range: 1-20 years), with varying degrees of lesion stability observed after interventions.
CONCLUSION
Hemangioblastomatosis represents a potentially aggressive progression of HB, characterized by recurrence and multifocal presentation. For VHL surveillance, long-term monitoring with periodic magnetic resonance imaging is recommended to increase early detection of recurrence of leptomeningeal lesion or involvement. This allows appropriate treatment strategies to be established, depending on factors such as the size of the lesion, the number of lesions and clinical manifestations, with the intention of reducing the morbidity and mortality of this disease.

title: P14.02.A OPTOCHEMOGENETIC MODELING OF NEURO-CANCER CROSSTALK IN VON HIPPEL-LINDAU DISEASE
authors: X Lu
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) disease leads to tumors in the nervous system, including cerebellar and spinal cord hemangioblastomas (CBHB, SCHB), and pheochromocytomas (PCC), involving significant neuro-cancer interactions. Understanding these bidirectional interactions is limited by the absence of accurate genetically engineered mouse (GEM) models. Traditional approaches for modeling localized gene recombination face issues such as off-target effects and systemic toxicity.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
We employed a novel optochemogenetic (OCG) switch technology, using photoactivatable caged 4-hydroxycyclofen (4-OHC) with localized UV illumination, to precisely induce genetic alterations in specific nervous system compartments (cerebellum, spinal cord) and peripheral nervous tissue (adrenal medulla). Using reporter mice (UBC-CreERT2 mTmGf/+), we optimized this UV-driven method to achieve targeted gene recombination. Subsequently, we created GEM models (UBC-CreERT2 Vhlf/f and UBC-CreERT2 Vhlf/f Ptenf/f) to investigate tumor initiation and progression driven by localized neuro-cancer interactions.
RESULTS
Preliminary findings validated effective localized gene recombination via the OCG switch, demonstrating specificity without systemic side effects. Conventional systemic induction methods caused rapid lethality, highlighting the necessity for spatially controlled gene recombination to study neural-tumor crosstalk accurately. Ongoing experiments focus on refining UV illumination conditions to effectively model the neural influences on cancer initiation and progression.
CONCLUSION
Our optochemogenetic approach uniquely enables precise investigation of neural influences on tumor formation and tumor-induced neural alterations specific to VHL disease. These GEM models are expected to uncover novel neural-cancer crosstalk mechanisms, advancing our understanding of cancer neuroscience and paving the way for targeted therapeutic strategies.

title: P14.03.B ADDITIONAL METRONOMIC CYCLOPHOSPHAMIDE SURMOUNTS VISMODEGIB RESISTANCE IN ADULT SHH-MUTATED MEDULLOBLASTOMA WITH BONE METASTASIS: A CASE REPORT
authors: F Bouille; E Jouglar; L Rozenblum; L Nichelli; B Mathon; L Morardet; F Bielle; P Leblond; F LAIGLE-DONADEY
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Only 20% of medulloblastomas occur in adults, a rarity that limits the availability of large-scale therapeutic trials in this population. Vismodegib has shown some signs of efficacy in patients with SHH-medulloblastoma, especially in those with bone metastases. However, its combination with metronomic treatments such as cyclophosphamide has not been reported yet. Material and methods: We report the case of a 40-year-old man diagnosed in 01/2022 with a desmoplastic SHH-activated medulloblastoma with SMO mutation. A T6 bone metastasis was identified at disease onset and histologically confirmed. Given the early progression of the bone lesion despite stable brain imaging, systemic chemotherapy — two cycles of carboplatin-etoposide (03-04/2022), followed by Temozolomide-Topotecan (06-07/2022) — was prioritized over immediate craniospinal irradiation. Then, the brain MRI showed a leptomeningeal infratentorial enhancement, and the patient was treated by radiation therapy (RT) on the craniospinal axis, including all adjacent bone metastases, followed by boosts to a large skull metastasis, and to the posterior fossa (54 Gy, terminated in 09/2022). Unfortunately, in 12/2022, despite the patient’s excellent general condition (KPS 90), the 18F-FDG-PET showed a bone progression outside of the field of RT (femur, hips...). A “compassionate” regimen with vismodegib (150 mg/d) was initiated in 01/2023. The patient achieved a complete metabolic cerebral response and a partial bone response in 04/2023, maintained until 11/2023. However, a slow progression of bone lesions was observed by the end of 2023. Given the unusual sustained response to vismodegib, our national board decided on 01/2024 to add a metronomic regimen of cyclophosphamide (50 mg/d) to vismodegib.
RESULTS
The clinical tolerance of the vismodegib + cyclophosphamide combination was excellent, only with grade 2 alopecia, grade 1 myalgia, and grade 3 lymphopenia. In 06/2024, a slow progression of three bone lesions was observed which were treated by hypofractionated RT (30 Gy in 10 fractions). A good metabolic response was noted on PET-scan in 08/2024. Due to perfect control of brain and bone lesions, it was decided to continue the association of vismodegib and cyclophosphamide. As local bone progression occurred on 02/2025, new targets were treated by focal radiotherapy. Twenty-seven months after the initiation of vismodegib, and seventeen months after the initiation of the combined therapy of vismodegib/cyclophosphamide, the patient maintained a KPS of 90%, with a good quality of life, and no bone pain.
CONCLUSION
We report the first case of vismodegib combined with cyclophosphamide for the treatment of bone metastatic SHH-medulloblastoma in an adult. The favorable therapeutic outcome in this patient supports the need for dedicated prospective trials to further evaluate the potential benefits of this strategy.

title: P14.04.A CHARACTERISTIC FEATURES OF PATIENTS WITH AUTOIMMUNE DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSES FOR PRIMARY CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM LYMPHOMA (PCNSL)

In imaging, PCNSL may resemble a number of differential diagnoses including autoimmune diseases like multiple sclerosis (MS). To identify aspects with which autoimmune differential diagnosis can be ruled out, we analyzed clinical and diagnostic features in PCNSL patients.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
Data of 107 patients who were hospitalized at University Hospital Regensburg and diagnosed with PCNSL between 2012 and 2022 were reviewed retrospectively. Patients were retrospectively classified according to the McDonald criteria of 2017, according to which MS is diagnosed. Descriptive statistics and correlation analyses, using Student’s T test, Chi-squared test and Fisher’s exact test, were performed.
RESULTS
Of 104 patients, to whom the McDonald criteria could be retrospectively applied, 6 (5.8%) patients with formally positive criteria were identified. Of these six patients, the majority (66.7% vs. 33.3%) had a relapsing symptomatology that could resemble MS (p < 0.001). Patients with positive McDonald criteria (n = 6) had significantly more often (50%) a history of an autoimmune disease (like Crohn’s disease or rheumatoid arthritis) compared to patients with negative McDonald criteria (4.1%) (p = 0.004). CSF-specific oligoclonal bands (OCBs) were detected in 60% (n = 3) of patients with positive McDonald criteria and in 8% (n = 4) of patients with negative criteria (p < 0.001). Patients with negative McDonald criteria had their main lesions more often in the white matter (54.1%, n = 53 vs. 16.7%, n = 1) and both supra- and infratentorial (21.4%, n = 21 vs. 16.7%, n = 1) (p = 0.021). title: P14.05.B CAR T-CELL THERAPY DOES NOT LEAD TO MEDIUM-TERM NEUROCOGNITIVE DETERIORATION IN PATIENTS WITH CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM LYMPHOMAS. A LOC NETWORK STUDY
authors: C Houillier; S Mersali; R Chapelle; M Ribeiro; N Weiss; D Psimaras; L Le Guennec; C Birzu; K Hoang-Xuan; I Boussen; M Baron; V Morel; M Uzunov; V Friser; S Choquet
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Several recent studies have shown promising efficacy of anti-CD19 chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy in central nervous system (CNS) lymphomas. Data regarding neurotoxicity were reassuring, with rates of severe acute neurotoxicity similar to those described in systemic lymphomas. However, recently published data from our group outlined the risk of prolonged neurologic deterioration in patients who experienced severe neurotoxicity, which is unusual in systemic lymphomas. The aim of this study was to evaluate mid-term neurocognitive outcomes in CNS lymphomas treated with CAR T-cells.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
Patients were retrospectively selected from the French LOC network database according to the following criteria: 1) CNS lymphoma treated with CAR T-cells at Pitié-Salpêtrière hospital; 2) Isolated CNS relapse at the time of leukapheresis; 3) Availability of neuropsychological follow-up. Neuropsychological assessment was performed as part of the usual care, before CAR T-cell infusion and, in the absence of tumoral progression, 6 weeks (W6), 6 months (M6) and 12 months (M12) after CAR T-cell therapy.
RESULTS
Of 38 CNS lymphomas who received CAR T-cells between May 2021 and March 2024, 30 patients (median age: 61 years (range: 30-82), 17 women, 14 primary, 16 secondary CNS lymphomas) benefited from repeated neuropsychological assessments. At the time of CAR T-cell infusion, 7 had stable or progressive disease, median Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) was 75 and median Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score was 23.5 (range: 11-29). Eleven patients received tisagenlecleucel, 17 axicabtagene ciloleucel and 2 brexucabtagene autoleucel. Nineteen patients experienced acute neurotoxicity, including 6 cases of grade 3-4 neurotoxicity. Twenty-two patients were assessed up to M12 (all other patients progressed). Clustering of these longitudinal data using a k-means approach revealed at W6 a subgroup of patients (n=22) with stable or improved cognitive functioning and a subgroup (n=8) with worsened cognitive functioning. Membership to these clusters was strongly associated with the occurrence and severity of an acute neurotoxicity (p=0.01). At M12, there was a statistically significant improvement of MoCA score (median 26 vs 23.5, p<0.001) compared to baseline. Scores addressing memory, executive functions, visuo-spatial functions and anxiety/depression also improved, although not significantly. Such improvements were already seen at M6, and applied both to the whole population and to the subgroup who experienced grade 3-4 neurotoxicity.
CONCLUSION
Mid-term neurocognition follow-up of patients with CNS lymphoma treated by CAR T-cells seems reassuring, with no significant cognitive worsening, even in patients who experienced severe acute neurotoxicity. These results should be confirmed with longer follow-up.

title: P14.06.A TREATMENT OUTCOME FOR INTRACRANIAL GERM CELL TUMOR (ICGCT): EXPERIENCE FROM A SINGLE TERTIARY CENTRE IN INDIA
authors: V Venkataramana; K Venkatesan; S Deshpande; B Misra; M Sankhe; K Desai; A Kapadia; S Almel
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Intracranial germ cell tumors are fairly rare tumors occurring mostly in children or young adults with a comparatively good prognosis. Historically, ICGCT were treated with cranio-spinal irradiation (CSI); however, the current standard of care for localised ICGCT, in particular germinomas, is more conformal treatment like whole ventricle radiation followed by tumor bed boost (WV+TB), without compromising the results. We report our experience of treatment outcome of patients treated consecutively.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
We report our experience in a consecutive series of 19 patients treated for ICGCT at our institution from 2001 to 2024. After surgery (biopsy / decompression) and chemotherapy (Cisplatin or Carboplatin + Etoposide +/- Ifosfamide), all patients received radiotherapy with a mean dose of 45Gy. Sixteen (84.2%) patients underwent WV+TB irradiation, while 3 (15.8%) received CSI.
RESULTS
Median age at diagnosis was 14 years (range: 5-30 years) and 15 (78.9%) patients were male. Median follow-up for the cohort was 97 months (10 months - 244 months). Sixteen patients had germinoma and 3 patients had non-germinomatous germ cell tumors (NGGCT). The primary disease sites were pineal gland (57.8%) and suprasellar region (26.3%). The 5/10-year overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) of the entire cohort were 94.4% / 87.2% and 88% / 88%. The 5/10-year OS of pure germinoma was 100% / 91.7%. Two (10.5%) patients progressed and died of their disease. 5 (26.3%) patients had endocrine deficiencies and 1(5.3%) developed progressive bilateral optic atrophy which was present prior to radiotherapy. Neither second malignancy nor neurocognitive dysfunction was reported in our series.
CONCLUSION
In our study, excellent 5-year overall survival were achieved with chemotherapy followed by reduced whole ventricular radiation. Although ICGCT have favourable cure rates, close attention to long term follow-up with assessment of neurocognitive function and subsequent malignancies is needed.

title: P14.07.B CAR T-CELL THERAPY IN PRIMARY CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM LYMPHOMAS: A MULTICENTER RETROSPECTIVE STUDY FROM THE LOC NETWORK
authors: F Bouille; M Baron; R Houot; R Ursu; I Boussen; C Soussain; A Waultier-Rascalou; B Guffroy; G Ahle; M Blonski; F Morschhauser; L Willems; T Gastinne; P Jerome; C Moluçon-Chabrot; A Schmitt; L Schenone; E Corvilain; E Gyan; F Jardin; V Morel; M Barrie; K Laribi; M Alcantara; A Campidelli; C Herbaux; K Hoang-Xuan; S Choquet; C Houillier
abstract:
BACKGROUND
The use of CAR T-cell therapy has been delayed in primary central nervous system lymphomas (PCNSL) due to the fear of unacceptable neurotoxicity. However, several recent small series (<30 patients) have shown promising results in heavily pretreated patients. The aim of this work was to confirm the interest of CAR T-cells in a larger cohort of PCNSL, with a longer follow-up.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
We retrospectively selected from the French LOC network database the patients with PCNSL treated with CAR T-cells and analyzed their characteristics and outcomes.
RESULTS
Sixty-seven patients with PCNSL (43 men, 24 women) from 24 centers received CAR T-cells between January 2020 and October 2024. Their median age was 66 years (range: 31-82). Their median ECOG score was 1. At the time of leukapheresis, brain involvement was present in 84% of patients, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) involvement in 25%, and ocular involvement in 12%. Patients had received a median of 2 prior lines of therapy (range: 1-6), including autologous stem cell transplantation in 30/67 cases. Sixty-five patients received bridging therapy before CAR T-cells. Thirty-eight patients (57%) received axicabtagene clioleucel, 20 (30%) tisagenlecleucel and 7 (10%) lisocabtagene maraleucel. Patients were followed for a median duration of 12 months (maximum: 47 months). During the follow-up, the best response was a complete response in 39 patients (58%) and a partial response in 14 patients (21%). Only 4 patients relapsed more than 12 months after the CAR T-cell infusion. Relapse-free survival was significantly better in patients in complete or partial response at CAR T-cell infusion (2-year RFS 55,6% vs 27,6%. P= 0,01). The 1-year and two-year progression-free survival rates were 50 % and 44%, respectively. The 1-year and two-year overall survival rates were 66% et 50%, respectively. Cytokine release syndrome (CRS) occurred in 95% of patients, with grade III-IV CRS in 4%. Immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS) was observed in 69% of patients, with 27% experiencing grade ≥ III events.
CONCLUSION
This work confirms the interest of CAR T-cells in PCNSL, in a larger cohort with a follow-up up to 4 years, with a high percentage of long-term remission and a reassuring tolerance profile in a population of heavily pre-treated patients. Future studies are warranted to clarify the exact positioning of this treatment within the therapeutic arsenal for the disease.

title: P14.08.A GLIOSARCOMA SPATIAL ARCHITECTURE IS DEFINED BY UNIQUE ECM AND IMMUNE REMODELING TRANSCRIPTIONAL PROFILES
authors: M Mühlbauer; N Neidert; J Beck; O Schnell; F Sahm; D Heiland
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Gliosarcoma (GS) is a rare, aggressive variant of Glioblastoma (GB), representing approximately 2% of all GB cases. It is characterized by its biphasic histological growth pattern with glial and sarcomatous areas. Little is known about GS pathogenesis or the underlying reasons for its distinct clinical features compared to GB, including higher rates of extracranial metastasis and skull invasion. Given the similarity in mutational profiles and chromosomal alterations between GS and GB, we hypothesize that GS arises from a unique interplay between tumor cells and the tumor microenvironment (TME), promoting a mesenchymal phenotype and the development of sarcomatous niches responsible for its clinical behavior.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
Spatial Transcriptomics (10x Genomics) und methylation profiling was applied to 15 GS samples from 13 patients. We used non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) and single cell deconvolution using large reference single cell RNA sequencing datasets to confidently identify conserved spatial features in our data. To identify the most discerning characteristics between GS and GB, we used a graph-based neural network approach.
RESULTS
Using a reference-based DNA methylation classifier, 12 of the 13 tumors (92%) were identified as belonging to the mesenchymal (MES) GB subgroup. While transcriptional profiles of GS samples were heterogeneous, NMF revealed four recurrent transcriptional metaprograms. In addition to hypoxia- and glial-associated programs, we identified an extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling program correlated with sarcomatous areas and enriched for vascular endothelial and smooth muscle cells. Lastly, an immune response program spatially associated with mesenchymal-like tumor cells and proliferating tumor-associated mononuclear cells. Subsequent cell-cell communication analysis uncovered potential signaling interactions and highlighted the importance of TGFβ- and MAPK-pathways for the formation of these distinct niches. A classifier based on the graph-based neural network successfully distinguished GB from GS subregions.
CONCLUSION
In this study, we performed the first in-depth spatial characterization of GS, identifying specific ECM remodeling and immune reactive spatial features unique for the TME of GS. Our findings provide insights into the transcriptional programs shaping GS tissue architecture, which could be crucial for understanding its biology and eventually aid the design of targeted therapies.

title: P14.09.B RISK FACTORS FOR CRANIOPHARYNGIOMA RECURRENCE: ANAYLSIS OF LONG-TERM FOLLOW-UP
authors: J Hwang; S Nam; M Kim; J Phi; C Park; S Kim; Y Kim
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Craniopharyngiomas are benign tumors that often exhibit aggressive clinical behavior. The aim of this study is to evaluate the long-term outcomes of surgery for primary and recurrent craniopharyngiomas, identify the risk factors for recurrence and assess the predictors of subtotal resection (STR).
MATERIAL AND METHODS
We retrospectively analyzed data from 279 craniopharyngioma surgeries performed at a single institution between 2010 and 2024. The median follow-up period was 64.0 (IQR 30.5-100.5) months. Preoperative characteristics, neuro-endocrinological results, recurrence patterns, and radiological features were evaluated. Statistical analyses included Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, Cox regression for recurrence factors, and logistic regression for predictors of the extent of resection.
RESULTS
The cohort included 185 primary and 94 recurrent tumors, and the endoscopic endonasal approach was used in 84.2% of cases. The overall 5-year recurrence rate was 29.2% (95% CI: 23.4-36.0%). Gross total resection (GTR) was achieved in 85.7% of cases. Multivariate analysis revealed that pediatric-onset (HR 1.98, 95% CI: 1.12-3.50) and subtotal resection (HR 3.40, 95% CI: 1.79-6.42) were significant risk factors for recurrence. Multiple recurrences showed progressive patterns of decreasing gross total resection rates and shorter recurrence intervals. Vascular encasement (OR 8.03, 95% CI 3.23-19.9) and recurrent tumor status (OR 5.10, 95% CI: 2.25-11.6) were significant predictors of STR.
CONCLUSION
Age at onset and extent of resection are critical factors influencing craniopharyngioma recurrence. Radiological features, particularly vascular encasement, are valuable predictors of the likelihood of subtotal resection. These findings offer important insights for planning the optimal treatment strategy for craniopharyngioma patients.

title: P14.10.A DISTINCT EPIGENETIC AND TRANSCRIPTIONAL PROFILES OF EPSTEIN-BARR VIRUS (EBV) POSITIVE AND NEGATIVE PRIMARY CNS LYMPHOMAS
authors: L Hai; D Friedel; F Hinz; D Hoffmann; S Doubrovinskaia; H Rohdjess; K Weidenauer; E Denisova; G Scheffler; T Kessler; A Kourtesakis; C Herold-Mende; O Henegariu; J M Baehring; J Dietrich; B Brors; W Wick; F Sahm; L D Kaulen
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)+ and EBV- primary CNS lymphomas (PCNSL) carry distinct mutational landscapes, but their transcriptional and epigenetic profiles have not been integrated and compared. This precludes further insights into pathobiology and molecular differences, relevant for classification and targeted therapy.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
23 EBV- and 15 EBV+ PCNSL, histologically classified as diffuse large B-cell lymphomas, were subjected to RNA-Sequencing and EPIC methylation arrays. Unsupervised clustering analyses were performed. title: P14.11.A AUTOGRAFT OLFACTORY STEM CELL TRANSPLANT FOR SPINAL CORD INJURY DEVELOPING INTO A PERSISTENT CERVICAL SPINAL MASS
authors: G H Stevens
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Spinal cord injury (SCI) often causes detrimental loss of motor, sensory, and autonomic function. The central nervous system has limited regenerative potential and neuronal damage caused by SCI can be severe and even irreversible. To date, there is no established treatment for SCI, but stem cell transplantation has been suggested and studied as a potential treatment option. The theory behind using stem cells to treat SCI is that pluripotent stem cells have the ability to differentiate and acquire characteristics of target tissues. The potential to self-renew however also carries the risk of uncontrolled cell growth and tumor formation.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
We report a case of olfactory mucosal stem cell transplantation for traumatic SCI at the level of C6-7. Three years after transplant, the patient developed new neurologic symptoms of arm weakness. MRI showed a multilobulated mass at the site of the stem cell transplant.
RESULTS
After sustaining a spinal cord injury, the patient underwent an Olfactory stem cell injection. 4 years later a cervical spine debulking showed olfactory cells. Two additional surgeries over the next 3 years also showed olfactory cells.
CONCLUSION
This case demonstrates a disastrous complication of stem cell transplantation and highlights the need for additional studies to validate its use for treatment.

authors: R Paterra; N Rosati; V Nazzi; M Moscatelli; I Vetrano; V Cojazzi; A Guarinoni; S Pellegatta; A Silvani; M Eoli
abstract:
BACKGROUND
phenotypes, are characterized by the development of multiple intracranial, spinal and peripheral schwannomas. Following the recent introduction of molecular diagnosis criteria for the subclassified of those conditions according a to the germline causing gene, we decided to investigate clinical and molecular characteristics of patients with a tumor burden suggestive of non NF2 related SWN.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
We selected 81 patients harbouring multiple schwannomas with at least one tumor with histological proven schwannoma diagnosis and, after a brain and a spine MRIs not fulfilling diagnostic criteria for NF2 related SWM following the Updated diagnostic criteria and nomenclature for neurofibromatosis type 2 and schwannomatosis”. All patients underwent NF2, SMARCB1 and LZTR1 mutational screening by NGS and MPLA analysis using blood DNA or the tissue of two different tumours when available (13 cases). The following clinical parameters were investigate age of first symptom, age at diagnosis, tumor burden Schwannoma location, presence of meningioma, presence of other neoplasms, presence of skin hyperpigmentation, presence of pain, hereditary.
RESULTS
Constitutive analysis showed LZTR1 gene germline pathogenic variants in 24 subjects (29.6%), SMARCB1 in 6 cases (7.4%), a LZTR1 VUS in 5 cases and no mutations in the known schwannomatosis driven genes in 45 (55.5%). title: P14.13.B TREATMENT OF RECURRENT ADAMANTINOMATOUS CRANIOPHARYNGIOMA WITH A COMBINATION OF BEVACIZUMAB AND TOCILIZUMAB: A CASE SERIES
authors: L M Webb; U Sener; T J Kaufmann; J A Trejo-Lopez; J J Van Gompel; M Peris Celda; J N Sarkaria; M W Ruff
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Adamantinomatous craniopharyngiomas (ACPs) are rare, partially cystic central nervous system tumors driven by the WNT/β-catenin pathway. As they grow, ACPs compress the surrounding pituitary gland, optic chiasm, and third ventricle. ACPs are highly morbid tumors with enormous quality of life impact on patients, often early in life. Thus, better treatments are needed. Current ACP treatment consists of maximally safe surgical resection with radiation for residual disease. Complete surgical resection is challenging, and recurrence is common. Targeted systemic chemotherapy is not routinely used for ACP treatment. Interleukin-6 (IL-6) levels are elevated within ACPs compared to normal brain tissue, making IL-6 an intriguing therapeutic target. Treatment response of ACP to tocilizumab alone or in combination with bevacizumab has been reported in children.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
We retrospectively reviewed the medical records of three adults with recurrent ACP who received combination treatment with bevacizumab and tocilizumab on a compassionate basis between June 2022 and April 2025 at Mayo Clinic in Rochester, MN. We collected demographic, clinical, treatment, radiologic, and outcome data.
RESULTS
All three patients were male and median age at initial ACP diagnosis was 38 years (range: 32-42 years). All patients underwent subtotal resection followed by radiation therapy. One patient had repeat surgical resection and two patients required interventions for hydrocephalus. At the time of ACP recurrence, all patients had visual impairment, endocrine dysfunction, and headaches. All patients received bevacizumab (7.5 mg/kg q3 weeks) and tocilizumab (8 mg/kg q3 weeks [n=2] or 4 mg/kg q4 weeks [n=1]). While receiving combination therapy, ACP tumor volume decreased on magnetic resonance imaging for all three patients (64%, 68%, and 29% reduction). None exhibited tumor growth since starting combination therapy. One patient had a small intraparenchymal hemorrhage, suspected secondary to radiation-induced cavernous malformation, so bevacizumab was discontinued, and he remains on tocilizumab alone. The other two patients continue combination therapy (for 344 and 351 days). Two patients experienced improvement in vision, and one had improvement in cognition. Possible adverse effects of treatment included sinus infections, fatigue, neutropenia, and hypertension.
CONCLUSION
Treatment with combination bevacizumab and tocilizumab was associated with shrinkage of ACP tumors and clinical improvements and obviated the need for further surgery or radiation in all three patients. This combination of medications may reprogram the tumor microenvironment, leading to ACP involution. This well-tolerated regimen provides a noninvasive option for treatment of recurrent ACP, and potentially initial ACP treatment, and may improve quality of life for patients.

title: P14.14.A 3D VOLUME GROWTH RATE OPENS NEW PERSPECTIVES FOR THE CLASSIFICATION OF AGGRESSIVE PITUITARY ADENOMAS
authors: T Graillon; E Tabouret; R Appay; P Romanet; A Barlier; A Mansourt; T Brue; D Figarella-Branger; F Castinetti; T Cuny; H Dufour
abstract:
BACKGROUND
WHO 2022 classification of neuroendocrine tumors states that there are currently no grading systems for pituitary adenomas (PitNET). Therefore, we aim to assess three-dimensional volume growth rate (3DVGR) in multiple PitNET and to correlate 3DVGR with tumor progression and neuropathology.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
Operated patients with growing or proliferative PitNET were retrospectively selected as 10 patients with pituitary metastasis and chordomas. Millimetric gadolinium 3DT1-weighted MRI was requested.
RESULTS
Totally, 103 3DVGR measurements were performed including 69 non-proliferative and 31 proliferative PitNETs with a median 3DVGR at respectively 21.6 %/year and 49.0 %/year (p<0.0001). Based on ROC analysis (AUC 0.993,p<0.001), we classified 3DVGR in three different classes: 3DVGR<50%/year; 50%/year≤3DVGR<80%/year; 3DVGR≥80%/year with a median PFS at respectively 91.0 months (95%CI: 84.8-107.2), 35.0 months (95%CI: 29.0-35.0) and 7.0 months (95%CI: 4.8-12.2). For 3DVGR<50%/year patients, no significant PFS difference was observed comparing proliferative vs. non-proliferative tumor status (p=0.381). For patients with proliferative status, PFS of patients with 3DVGR≥50%/year was significantly worse than PFS of patients with 3DVGR<50%/year (p<0.001). Finally, by multivariate analysis, only the 3DVGR (cutoff: 50%/year) was significantly associated with the risk of early progression (p<0.001), in contrast to the proliferative status. By combining either the 3DVGR ≥80% or the Ki67 ≥8%, we were able to identify the 12 most aggressive PitNETs, characterized by a dramatic decrease in the median PFS(8.5 months vs. 64 months for the other patients).
CONCLUSION
PitNET proliferation classification was proposed as follow: 3DVGR<10%: not or slowly progressive; 10%≤3DVGR<50%: slowly progressive; 50%≤3DVGR<80%: rapidly progressive; 80%≤3DVGR: aggressive. Therefore, 3DVGR could be a very interesting tool to assess PitNET proliferation in complement to histological analyses.

title: P14.15.B PURE CYSTIC LESIONS OF THE CONUS MEDULLARIS: A SINGLE CENTRE STUDY AND SYSTEMATIC REVIEW
authors: A Bashir; S Vankipuram; V M Russo
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Pure cystic lesions at the conus medullaris comprising ventriculus terminalis (VT), intramedullary arachnoid cyst (IMAC) and neurenteric cyst (NEC) are rare benign cysts. Compared to IMAC and NEC requiring often surgery, the VT is considered as a normal anatomic development phenomenon rarely needing more than MRI surveillance. However, the literature is limited and there exist no uniform guidelines. The aim was to present our experience from a cohort with these lesions and discuss management strategies as compared to the existing literature.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
A retrospective review was conducted identifying patients (>16 years) from our institutional archive from 2013 to 2024. Demographic factors, presenting symptoms using the established Classification by de Moura Batista et al., and therapeutic management were recorded. Previous history of spinal trauma or surgery, or radiological evidence of adjacent tumour tissue or malformations e.g. Chiari malformation, tethered cord or spinal dysraphism were excluded. A literature search was performed using PubMed/Medline, EMBASE and Cochrane until December 2024 to identify cases with pure cysts at the conus medullaris using same inclusion criteria. Non-parametric Fisher exact or Kruskal-Wallis tests were used.
RESULTS
Twenty-two patients (F/M ratio 2: 1; median age 42 years) were included. All patients but two presented with back pain with/without sciatica where six had sensorimotor disturbances and two with also urinary dysfunction. No association was found between the cyst size and the symptoms, p=0.572. Ten patients underwent microsurgical cyst fenestration via laminectomy while two had additional a cyst-subarachnoid shunt inserted. Histology was available for eight patients revealing VT in one case, IMAC in three and NEC in four while it was inconclusive in the rest. Complete recovery was observed in four patients while partial in three with no association with the cyst size, p=0.707. Patients with NEC showed a tendency of recurrence, p=0.465. Twelve patients underwent annual MRI surveillance and remained stable with a median follow-up of 49 months. The literature yielded case studies and small series of VT (n=99), IMAC (n=10) and NEC (n=6) whereas 77 patients (VT 77.8%, IMAC and NEC 100%) had undergone surgery, most commonly microsurgical cyst fenestration. Complete recovery was seen in 36.5% and partial in 37.4%.
CONCLUSION
Our results shows that the VT rarely requires surgery, compared to IMAC and NEC. However, the literature mainly reports surgical treated VT cases and may not be representative for all VT cases as conservatively managed and asymptomatic cases are less likely to be published. We believe that the VT is an expression of persistent malformation of 5th ventricle without necessary having a progressive evolution, and surgery should be avoided unless expansion of the cyst per se and exclusion of other causes.

title: P14.16.A REINFORCEMENT LEARNING IDENTIFIES TIM-3 BLOCKADE AS A PROMISING IMMUNOTHERAPEUTIC STRATEGY IN CHORDOMA
authors: J Kada Benotmane
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Chordoma, a rare notochord-derived bone malignancy, remains largely resistant to chemotherapy and radiation, making en-bloc surgical resection the therapeutic cornerstone. However, due to anatomically challenging locations at the skull base and sacrum, achieving complete (R0) resection is frequently impossible, resulting in local recurrence rates of 40-60% after incomplete (R1) resection. Effective systemic treatment strategies remain urgently needed.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
We performed comprehensive multimodal immune profiling on six newly diagnosed sacral chordomas, integrating CD45-enriched single-cell RNA sequencing (total of 85,921 cells: 39,938 from tumour tissue and 45,983 from matched peripheral blood), coupled with paired T/B-cell receptor sequencing. Spatial context was defined via 10X Visium spatial transcriptomics performed on four tumours (total 20,164 spatial spots, median 5,041 per tumour). To identify promising therapeutic targets, we employed a reinforcement-learning-driven, agent-based computational model (CellAgentChat) to simulate the effects of immune-checkpoint inhibitor perturbations.
RESULTS
All analysed chordomas consistently exhibited a distinct “nest-septa” architecture: physaliphorous tumour nests were largely devoid of immune cell infiltration, while surrounding fibrous septa were densely populated with immunosuppressive M2-like macrophages, DC2-type dendritic cells, and enriched in TGFB/IL-10 signalling. Despite this exclusionary environment, we identified T-cell receptor (TCR) clonotypes shared between peripheral blood and tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes. Convergent CDR3 sequence motifs suggested the presence of chordoma-specific antigens; notably, these T-cell clones adopted an exhausted phenotype (PD-1⁺TOX⁺) upon entering the tumour microenvironment. Reinforcement-learning simulations predicted the downstream transcriptional effects of immune-checkpoint inhibition, identifying TIM-3 blockade as the most promising strategy. In silico TIM-3 inhibition robustly enhanced antigen presentation, cytokine signalling, and immune-regulatory gene expression specifically within the immunosuppressive septal compartment.
CONCLUSION
This multimodal characterization of six sacral chordomas reveals a spatially structured immunosuppressive barrier, penetrated—but not overcome—by circulating tumour-reactive T cells. Although generalisability is constrained by cohort size and anatomical specificity, our reinforcement-learning models strongly support clinical evaluation of TIM-3 blockade, either as monotherapy or in combination with PD-1/CTLA-4 inhibitors, as a promising therapeutic avenue for sacral chordoma patients.

title: P14.17.B A REAL-WORLD SURVEY OF 1830 SURVIVING PATIENTS WITH ADAMANTINOMATOUS CRANIOPHARYNGIOMA IN CHINA
authors: Z Lin; Y Deng
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Adamantinomatous craniopharyngioma (ACP) is a rare benign tumor of the central nervous system. Real-world studies on surviving patients in China remain lacking. This study aimed to systematically analyze the demographic characteristics, treatment patterns, complications, recurrence rates, and factors influencing quality of life (QoL) and family economic burden among Chinese ACP survivors through an independent third-party survey.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
In July 2024, a third-party volunteer team conducted a questionnaire survey of 1,830 ACP survivors in Chinese communities. Chi-square tests and multivariate logistic regression analyses (SPSS 21.0) were used to evaluate influencing factors.
RESULTS
72.3% of patients underwent initial surgery at ages 0-10 years, with a male predominance (59.3% vs. 40.7% female). In the initial treatment, 98.6% of patients underwent surgery. Gross total resection (GTR) rates were comparable between transcranial approach (TCA) (84.37%) and endoscopic endonasal surgery (EES) (87.73%), but TCA had significantly higher recurrence rates (26.1% vs. 15.3%; P<0.001) compared to EES. In subtotal resection cases, regrowth rates were higher after TCA (65.26% vs. 40.74% EES; P=0.0001). Among 267 patients with residual tumors, only 108 were recommended radiotherapy (RT), and 56 ultimately received RT. RT recipients required no further treatment significantly more often than non-RT cases (36/56 vs. 77/211; P=0.0002). Among patients with residual tumors after the first operation, only 108 were recommended for RT by doctors, and 56 eventually received it. The proportion of patients who did not require further treatment after radiotherapy was significantly higher than those who did not receive it (36/56 vs. 77/211, P=0.0002). There were differences in the incidence of complications between TCA and EES. Specifically, for gross total resection, TCA associated with higher rates of sinusitis, dyslipidemia, hyperglycemia, flatfoot, and forehead incision suppuration. title: P14.18.A SCHWANNOMAS DISPLAY CONSERVED CELLULAR STATES AND PREFERENTIAL MHC CLASS II ANTIGEN PRESENTATION ACROSS DIFFERENT GENETIC BACKGROUNDS AND ANATOMIC LOCATIONS
authors: L Gonzalez Castro; A Gavish; L Bussema; C Mount; C Neftel; M Nomura; E Chiocca; W Bi; O Arnaout; F Barker; J Brown; J Jordan; T Batchelor; A Stemmer-Rachamimov; S Plotkin; I Tirosh; M L Suvà
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Despite being associated with molecular alterations in the NF2 gene, there is limited understanding of the gene expression programs that govern the behavior of schwannomas—both in sporadic cases and in patients with schwannoma predisposition syndromes—and how these programs relate to tumor anatomic location.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
We characterized the transcriptional heterogeneity of schwannomas across different genetic backgrounds and anatomic locations at single-cell resolution. Tumor samples from patients undergoing resection for symptomatic schwannoma were dissociated and processed for whole-transcriptome profiling using Smart-seq2. Our cohort included 22 schwannomas: 5 from schwannomatosis patients, 11 from neurofibromatosis type 2 (NF2) patients, and 6 sporadic tumors (3 post-radiation). Anatomically, 12 tumors were from cranial nerves (11 vestibular, 1 accessory), and 10 from spinal or peripheral nerves.
RESULTS
We profiled 11,373 cells, including 4,725 neoplastic cells and various non-neoplastic populations. Copy number alteration analysis revealed intratumoral polyclonality. Non-negative matrix factorization identified six conserved transcriptional metaprograms related to stress response, myelin production, antigen presentation, interferon signaling, glycolysis, and extracellular matrix remodeling. Notably, schwannomas exhibited a distinctive antigen presentation metaprogram, enriched for MHC class II genes (e.g., HLA-DRA, HLA-DRB1). Additionally, we observed a distinct interferon signaling program, which was conserved across most tumors but attenuated in vestibular schwannomas, indicating a potential mechanism of regional immune evasion. Comparison with pan-cancer data confirmed the relative uniqueness of these immune-related programs to schwannomas.
CONCLUSION
We provide a comprehensive single-cell transcriptomic analysis of schwannomas across genetic and anatomic contexts. Our findings reveal unique, conserved immune-related transcriptional programs, particularly involving antigen presentation and interferon signaling, which may contribute to tumor immune evasion and inform future immunotherapeutic strategies.

title: P14.19.B PRIMARY HISTIOCYTIC SARCOMA OF THE CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM: REPORT OF TWO CASES, INCLUDING A CASE WITH PROMINENT INTRAVENTRICULAR DISSEMINATION
authors: K Donev
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Primary Central Nervous System histiocytic sarcoma is rare aggressive malignant neoplasm with less that 50 cases reported in the literature. They usually harbor variable genetic alteration including MAPK and PI3K pathways as well as tumor suppressor genes TP53 and CDKN2A/B, among others. Herein, two additional two cases of Primary CNS histiocytic sarcoma are reported.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
N/A.
RESULTS
Case 1: 78-year-old man with past medical history significant for renal cell carcinoma (25 years ago), and chronic kidney disease, presented with gait instability and multiple falls. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and Positron Emission Tomography-Computed Tomography (PET/CT) scan revealed prominent intraventricular dissemination with multiple enhancing masses along the ventricular system and periventricular areas that were enlarging over time. In addition, there were multiple intramedullary, central canal and pial surface lesions in the cervical spine. Also left adreanal adenoma was seen and small indeterminate lesions in the liver and left kidney. Overall findings were suspicious for primary CNS malignancy. Biopsy revealed histiocytic sarcoma. Given the advanced stage of disease the patient opted for palliative therapy and eventually passed away 14 days after the diagnosis. Case 2: 56-year-old woman with medical history of breast carcinoma (2021) and hypertension presented with one year history of bilateral feet and calf paresthesia, followed by repeated falls and eventually becoming wheelchair-bound. She also developed hearing impairment, dysarthria, dysphagia and abnormal extraocular movements. Multiple brain MRIs revealed extensive extra-axial and leptomeningeal enhancement involving bilateral cavernous sinuses, optic chiasm and tracts, prepontine cistern and adjacent temporal regions. Nodular enhancement along cranial nerves and brainstem was also noted. Excisional biopsy revealed histiocytic sarcoma. Patient clinically deteriorated rapidly and passed away 10 days after the diagnosis. Pathology: Both cases revealed high-grade malignancy composed of sheets of large cells with ample cytoplasm. Significant nuclear pleomorphism and multinucleation was seen. Background chronic inflammation was present. Large neoplastic cell were positive for histiocytic markers, including CD68, CD163, CD4, PU.1 and S100, while all other lymphoma, epithelial, melanocytic and sarcoma markers were negative. MayoComplete Histiocytic Neoplasm panel was negative for all 8 mutations tested.
CONCLUSION
Primary CNS histiocytic sarcoma is a very rare entity. These two cases support the previously reported aggressive clinical course of primary CNS histiocytic sarcoma. Histiocytic sarcoma can involved any area of central nervous system, but prominent intraventricular dissemination as seen in case 1 has been previously reported in only case.

title: P14.20.A GAMMA KNIFE RADIOSURGERY FOR PAPILLARY CRANIOPHARYNGIOMA AFTER SURGERY: A SINGLE-CENTER STUDY ON TUMOR CONTROL AND PREDICTORS OF RECURRENCE
authors: Z Lin; Y Lin
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Papillary craniopharyngioma (PCP) is a distinct histopathological subtype of craniopharyngioma with unique clinical, radiological, and molecular characteristics compared to the adamantinomatous variant. While Gamma Knife radiosurgery (GKRS) is an established modality for residual or recurrent craniopharyngiomas, limited data are available regarding its efficacy specifically in PCP. This study aimed to assess tumor control after GKRS in surgically treated PCP patients and to identify prognostic factors for recurrence.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
A retrospective review was conducted of 32 patients with histologically confirmed PCP who underwent GKRS at Beijing Tiantan Hospital between August 2002 and March 2025 following surgical resection. Clinical and radiological data were analyzed. Tumor progression was defined radiographically. Progression-free survival (PFS) was calculated using the Kaplan-Meier method. Univariate and multivariate Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate potential predictors of recurrence.
RESULTS
The median clinical follow-up was 49.05 months (mean, 70.34 months; range, 1.48-272.68 months). Radiological follow-up (available in 28 patients) had a median duration of 33.80 months. Tumor recurrence occurred in 10 patients (31.25%) with a median time to recurrence of 22.5 months. One-, 3-, and 5-year PFS rates were 90.6%, 81.25%, and 71.9%, respectively. Univariate analysis identified tumor volume, number of isocenters, and post-GKRS visual change as significant predictors of recurrence (P < 0.05). On multivariate analysis, subjective visual deterioration after GKRS was an independent risk factor for recurrence (OR 25.15, 95% CI 1.45-5.41, P = 0.001), while visual improvement did not significantly differ from stable vision. Post-treatment visual outcomes included improvement in 6.25%, stability in 62.5%, and deterioration in 31.25% of patients. One death occurred in the recurrence group. Most recurrences were managed with repeat GKRS or surgery.
CONCLUSION
GKRS offers reasonable long-term tumor control for PCP following surgical resection. Post-radiosurgical subjective visual decline may indicate early tumor recurrence and warrants close follow-up.
