title: EP09.06 FIRST-IN-HUMAN USE OF ACCELERATOR-BASED BNCT WITH CONCURRENT P-BORONOPHENYLALANINE (NBB-001) AND SINGLE-DOSE BEVACIZUMAB FOR RECURRENT GLIOBLASTOMA
authors: M Harat; L Yuan-hao; M Blok; I Zarebska
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Recurrent glioblastoma remains one of the most therapeutically challenging malignancies, with rapid progression and limited salvage options. BNCT (Boron Neutron Capture Therapy) offers biologically targeted irradiation by delivering high-LET alpha particles selectively to tumor cells containing boron-10. This case represents the first-in-human clinical use of the NeuPex Block-I (Neuboron) system—a compact, hospital-integrated tandem accelerator delivering epithermal neutrons via a lithium target.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
A 52-year-old male patient with right frontal glioblastoma WHO grade 4 (IDH1/2 wild-type, 1p/19q non-codeleted, MGMT promoter methylated) underwent surgery on 20.12.2023. This was followed by standard radiochemotherapy per Stupp protocol (60 Gy with concurrent temozolomide), and adjuvant temozolomide. Multiparametric MRI and FET-PET uptake in dual acquisition confirmed recurrence showing rapid clinical deterioration shortly after radiological recurrence. The patient was treated with a single session of accelerator-based BNCT using p-boronophenylalanine (NBB-001) followed by a single infusion of Bevacizumab post-treatment. Neutron irradiation was performed using the NeuPex Block-I (Neuboron) system. Clinical monitoring, imaging, hematology, and quality-of-life evaluations were conducted at baseline and at regular intervals post-treatment.
RESULTS
BNCT dosimetry showed selective tumor targeting with favorable distribution of boron concentrations and corresponding compound biological effectiveness (CBE). The highest boron concentration was observed in the tumor (GTV: 66 µg/ml, CBE 3.8), while normal brain tissue showed significantly lower values (26.25 µg/ml, CBE 1.3). DVH analysis confirmed adequate dose coverage, with Dmax and Dmean for the GTV reaching 43.045 Gy-Eq and 22.276 Gy-Eq, respectively. title: EP10.01 CLINICAL EFFICACY/EFFECTIVENESS, SAFETY AND HEALTH-RELATED QUALITY OF LIFE ASSOCIATED WITH TREATMENTS FOR RELAPSED/REFRACTORY PAEDIATRIC LOW-GRADE GLIOMA: A SYSTEMATIC LITERATURE REVIEW
authors: O Witt; R Brandt; A Houchard; N Kelkouli; B Mayer; L Vinals; A Mastronuzzi; D Hargrave
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Patients with relapsed/refractory paediatric low-grade glioma (R/R pLGG) face considerable long-term morbidity. Most cases are driven by single-gene alterations in the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway for which several targeted agents are being evaluated. Systematic literature reviews (SLRs) were performed to deepen understanding of the efficacy/effectiveness, safety and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) evidence for therapies in R/R pLGG, and to inform Health Technology Assessment (HTA) submissions for tovorafenib, a type II pan-RAF inhibitor.
METHODS
MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, CDSR and DARE databases were searched up to 25 November 2024 with additional manual searches of key conferences, HTA reports, trial registries and regulatory documents in January 2025. Clinical trials and real-world (RW) studies of patients with R/R pLGG meeting predefined criteria were eligible (PROSPERO registration, CRD420250648339). Risk of bias was assessed. Findings were summarized narratively.
RESULTS
In total, 30 clinical trials (20 single-arm, 7 non-randomized, 3 randomized) and 14 RW studies (13 retrospective, 1 prospective) were included. Most clinical trials evaluated MAPK inhibitors (n = 15, including pan-RAF inhibitor tovorafenib [n = 2] and V-Raf murine sarcoma viral oncogene homolog B (BRAF) inhibitor dabrafenib [n = 2]) or chemotherapy-based regimens (n = 13; 12 regimens). Most RW studies evaluated chemotherapy-based regimens (n = 10; 18 regimens), one evaluated RAF/BRAF inhibitors. The majority of MAPK inhibitor studies reported the distribution of patients with BRAF alterations and often reported stratified outcomes. In contrast, only one clinical trial of a chemotherapy-based regimen reported BRAF alteration status; stratified outcomes were not reported. Between-study comparisons were complicated by limited patient characteristics and/or subgroup reporting, and where reported, by heterogeneity in populations and methodologies used for assessing outcomes. Specifically, in clinical trial BRAF-altered populations, overall response rates ranged from 15-69% and median progression-free survival from 14-37 months. Across drug classes, fatigue was a frequently reported adverse event of special interest. No HRQoL data were found. Functional outcomes of increasing clinical interest were out of scope of the SLRs.
CONCLUSION
The variety of therapies identified highlights a lack of standard of care for R/R pLGG and a need for specific, well-tolerated treatment options with proven efficacy/effectiveness that improve HRQoL/functional outcomes. Future studies that report molecular prognostic factors (e.g. BRAF alterations), employ consistent efficacy/effectiveness and safety assessments, and evaluate long-term treatment impact on HRQoL/functional outcomes are needed to guide treatment selection.

title: EP10.02 A DIABENZALACETONE-BASED COMPOUND MODULATES PROLIFERATION, MIGRATION, AND APOPTOSIS IN MEDULLOBLASTOMA CELLS
authors: L E Thomas; S Siddiqui; M Braoudaki
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Medulloblastoma (MB) is a leading cause of cancer-related deaths in children and young adults, accounting for over 20% of paediatric brain tumours. Despite advances in treatment, outcomes remain poor, underscoring the urgent need for novel biomarkers and therapeutic strategies. This study evaluates the therapeutic potential of Dibenzalacetone (DBA) in MB.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
The half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC₅₀) of DBA was determined in DAOY cell line using an MTT assay. To evaluate the DBA’s functional effects, cells were treated with DBA at the IC₅₀ concentration, a higher dose (+10 µM), a vehicle control (DMSO), and Cisplatin as a positive control. Cell viability and proliferation were assessed under each condition. Colony formation was quantified, normalised to the DMSO control, and expressed as a percentage relative to untreated controls. The impact of DBA on cell migration was evaluated using a scratch wound healing assay, with wound closure measured at 0, 24, and 48 hours and normalised to DMSO-treated cells. Nuclear morphology and apoptosis-related changes were assessed via DAPI staining, comparing treated and control cells.
RESULTS
The IC₅₀ of the DBA was determined to be 50 µg/mL. Vehicle control DMSO-treated DAOY cells demonstrated robust colony formation (100%), while DBA at IC₅₀ and the higher concentration reduced colony formation to 36.5% and 35.1%, respectively. The positive control reduced colony formation to 43.3%, indicating comparable efficacy. In wound healing assays, DMSO-treated cells achieved ~100% closure by 48 hours, whereas DBA-treated DAOY cells showed significantly impaired closure, including wound expansion and negative closure percentages at 48 hours. DAPI staining revealed nuclear fragmentation in DBA treated cells, indicating apoptosis, while DMSO-treated cells exhibited intact nuclei and mitotic activity.
CONCLUSION
The DBA was found to significantly inhibit proliferation, migration, and survival of MB cells, demonstrating strong potential as a therapeutic candidate. Further investigation is warranted to explore its mechanism of action and evaluate its efficacy in paediatric MB cell models.

title: EP10.03 ASSESSING INTEREST IN THE SIOPE BTG YOUNG INVESTIGATORS AND INNOVATORS (YII) GROUP: RESULTS FROM A EUROPEAN SURVEY
authors: C Satragno; J Apps; E Opocher; C Michi; K Green; C Dorfer; K Scheinemann; Y Lassen; C Faria
abstract:
BACKGROUND
To support the growing interest in structured collaboration among young researchers, the SIOPE BTG Young Investigators and Innovators (YII) Group initiated a new phase of development. To guide this process and assess community needs, we conducted a dedicated survey among potential young members across Europe.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
A web-based survey was distributed between November and December 2024 to early-career professionals involved in paediatric neuro-oncology, including both researchers and clinicians. The questionnaire collected information on group membership, expectations, clinical roles, specialization topics, willingness to engage in collaborative projects, and outreach activities. Data were analyzed descriptively.
RESULTS
A total of 61 participants responded. While only 11.5% (7/61) were current members of the YII group, 77.1% (47/61) expressed interest in joining. Nearly half (49.2%, 30/61) were already members of other SIOPE BTG or European trial working groups, highlighting a strong inclination toward structured collaboration. Most respondents (68.9%, 42/61) had completed specialization, and among these, 42.9% (18/42) had less than 6 years of professional experience. The main areas of expertise were high-grade glioma (48.1%, 29/61), low-grade glioma (44.2%, 27/61), and embryonal tumors (44.2%, 27/61). Key expectations included networking, educational events, collaborative research projects, and active involvement in broader SIOPE BTG group activities. Additionally, 69.2% (42/61) expressed willingness to contribute to social media and outreach initiatives, and 96.1% (59/61) were open to being contacted for participation in future projects.
CONCLUSION
This survey confirms strong interest among young investigators in actively contributing to the SIOPE BTG YII Group. Based on these insights, we plan to consolidate membership, strengthen links with the other SIOPE BTG working groups, and launch collaborative initiatives tailored to young researchers’ needs. Our goal is to build a dynamic and inclusive environment that empowers the next generation of paediatric neuro-oncology professionals across Europe.

title: EP11.01 PALLIATIVE MANAGEMENT OF BRAIN METASTASIS IN FOLLICULAR VARIANT PAPILLARY THYROID CARCINOMA: A CASE REPORT
authors: R D Kakde; A M Bhange
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Brain metastases from differentiated thyroid carcinomas are rare, with the follicular variant of papillary thyroid carcinoma (FVPTC) accounting for a minority of cases. Optimal management strategies remain individualized due to limited clinical experience.
CASE PRESENTATION
We report a case of 75 year-old female diagnosed with FVPTC who presented with right frontal region swelling. FDG PET CT was done which was suggestive of right frontal and temporal bone lesions infiltrating into the adjacent brain parenchyma and few nodules in both the lobes of thyroid gland. Biopsy from the right frontal lesion was positive for metastases from carcinoma of thyroid. The patient initially underwent total thyroidectomy followed by histopathological confirmation of FVPTC. The case was discussed in the internal tumor board of hospital, where decision was taken to treat the brain metastasis with palliative external beam radiotherapy (30Gray/10fractions) followed high-dose radioiodine (150 mci) therapy for systemic disease control. Pre-therapy scans demonstrated iodine avid metastatic brain lesions
DISCUSSION
This case highlights the rare occurrence of brain metastasis in FVPTC and emphasizes the importance of a multidisciplinary approach, including surgical, radiation, and nuclear medicine interventions. Palliative radiotherapy played a crucial role in symptom control and improving the patient’s performance status, allowing for subsequent high-dose radioiodine therapy, which is essential in achieving systemic disease management in iodine-avid metastases.
CONCLUSION
Early identification and multimodality management of brain metastases in FVPTC can provide meaningful palliation and may enhance the effectiveness of subsequent systemic radioiodine therapy. This case underscores the critical role of individualized, coordinated care in the management of advanced differentiated thyroid cancers. <!--EndFragment-->

title: EP11.02 CURRENT TREATMENTS AND RECENT ADVANCES FOR BRAIN METASTASES
authors: L He; Y Chen
abstract:
BACKGROUND
The incidence of brain metastases (BMs) has increased significantly in recent years, which can be attributed to prolonged survival due to advancements in systemic therapies and enhanced imaging technologies. Despite the availability of various treatment options, the prognosis for affected patients remains poor.
METHODS
This review summarizes the primary current treatment modalities for BMs and highlights recent advances in these treatment strategies.
RESULTS
For patients with solitary or limited brain metastases, surgical resection remains a key treatment modality. Innovations in intraoperative diagnostic tools, such as intraoperative fluorescence and handheld confocal microscopy, have improved the accuracy of tumor margin delineation. For patients with a high intracranial tumor burden, whole-brain radiotherapy (WBRT) remains a foundational treatment option; however, it is associated with notable adverse effects on cognitive function. Combining WBRT with memantine, an N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor antagonist, may alleviate these cognitive impairments. Stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) offers an effective alternative for both solitary and multiple brain metastases, particularly as an adjuvant therapy following surgical resection, and is associated with a reduced risk of cognitive decline compared to WBRT. The efficacy of many chemotherapeutic agents remains limited due to the presence of the blood-brain barrier. Targeted therapies, particularly those developed for tumors with specific genetic mutations such as non-small cell lung cancer and breast cancer, have demonstrated substantial therapeutic benefits. Immune checkpoint inhibitors, a major class of immunotherapies, have led to significant advancements in the treatment of various malignancies. Additionally, the combination of immunotherapy with other treatment modalities presents promising potential.
CONCLUSION
Clinical management should be tailored based on the type of primary tumor, molecular characteristics, number and location of brain metastases, the patient’s systemic condition, and estimated survival. With the ongoing technological innovation and growing understanding of tumor biology, treatment of BMs is anticipated to become increasingly precise and personalized, ultimately improving patients’ outcomes.

title: EP11.03 EMERGENCY STEREOTACTIC RADIOSURGERY FOR SOLITARY BRAINSTEM METASTASIS IN CERVICAL CANCER: A NOVEL APPLICATION OF GYROSCOPIC RADIOTHERAPY
authors: A Sopel; M Rucinska; S Nawrocki
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Metastases of cervical squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) to the brain are exceedingly rare, and those affecting the brainstem are even more exceptional. Their anatomical complexity limits surgical access and therapeutic options. The ZAP-X radiosurgery system, employing a self-shielded gyroscopic linear accelerator, offers high-precision stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) particularly suitable for treating lesions in eloquent brain areas.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
We report a case of a 49-year-old female patient with FIGO stage IIB HPV-associated cervical SCC, initially treated with definitive chemoradiotherapy and brachytherapy. Fifteen months after completion of treatment, she developed neurological symptoms indicative of central nervous system involvement. MRI revealed a solitary contrast-enhancing lesion in the dorsal pons. A multidisciplinary team indicated SRS with ZAP-X. The patient underwent single-fraction ZAP-X treatment to 18 Gy at the 50% isodose line.
RESULTS
The treatment was well tolerated with no acute complications. The patient experienced symptomatic improvement in balance and vision. Ophthalmologic follow-up confirmed resolution of a left abducens nerve palsy. Follow-up MRI at six weeks post-treatment demonstrated a reduction in lesion volume by approximately 35%, with decreased perilesional edema and no new CNS or systemic lesions.
CONCLUSION
This is one of the first reported cases of a solitary brainstem metastasis from cervical SCC treated using the ZAP-X system. The favorable clinical and radiological outcomes support its use as a safe and effective modality for managing intracranial metastases in anatomically sensitive regions. ZAP-X SRS may expand the therapeutic options available for rare and complex CNS metastases in gynecologic oncology.

title: EP12.01 CHALLENGES IN THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PROTOCOL FOR CARE AND TREATMENT OF PATIENTS WITH BRAIN TUMORS. THE CASE OF A HOSPITAL CENTER IN MEXICO
authors: V Vazquez Zamora; E D Razis
abstract:
BACKGROUND
In 2024, as part of the EANO Mentorship Program, the Protocol for the care and treatment of patients with brain tumors of the Department of Radiation Oncology in the Specialty Hospital of Mexico Social Security Institute (HE-IMSS) in Puebla, Mexico was developed, which seeks to standardize the approach to brain tumor patient care by the radiation oncologists of the Unit with a goal to improve practice. This document has been well received by medical staff and has been put into practice since November 2024. However, there are still areas that need improvement for its proper implementation.
OBJECTIVES
To analyze the challenges with the implementation of the Protocol for the care and treatment of patients with brain tumors of the Department of Radiation Oncology in the Specialty Hospital of Mexico Social Security Institute (HE-IMSS) in Puebla in daily practice.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
Once the Protocol for the care and treatment of patients with brain tumors of the Department of Radiation Oncology was established, observations regarding parameters that hinder the complete implementation of the protocol were recorded.
RESULTS
Most challenges were independent of the function of the Radiotherapy Department. Challenges detected are: 1) Lack of description of the surgery (extent of resection) performed by Neurosurgery, in at least 30% of the patients, 2) Magnetic resonance (MR) study generally performed pre-but not postoperatively, 3) Lack of medications, with only temozolomide available for concomitant-adjuvant use, and 4) Delayed pathology reporting times (20 business days after the surgical procedure)
RESULTS
Our plan is discussing the challenges with all involved parties to improve the implementation of the Protocol within a period of no more than 6 months from the implementation of the changes (March/2025), with the objective of: 1) achieving a reduction of files with inadequate surgery reports by at least 50%, 2) Increase in postoperative MRI by 20% and 3) Have pathology results in less than 3 weeks in at least 50% of all cases. Delivery of results by September 10, 2025Initially, it is critical have an adequate evaluation of the patient and necessary studies in a timely fashion, according to the protocol and for this it is imperative improve communication with Neurosurgery and Pathology Departments and the Radiology Service to explain the importance of a detailed evaluation of their procedures.
CONCLUSION
For a correct implementation of a care protocol for patients with brain tumors, a multidisciplinary approach is required to improve efficacy as reflected by anadequate response of the tumors and a better quality of life for patients. Therefore, ideally a tumor board will need to be set up. Despite limited resources such as access to medications, many patients can benefit from the care offered by the Unit.

title: EP12.02 LOW GRADE GLIOMAS. REVIEW IN OUR CENTER
authors: E Iza Rodriguez; E Bóveda Carro; P González Fernandez; L Zaldumbide Dueñas; E Iruarrizaga Ovejas; J Mañe Martinez; G Bermudez Villar; A González Lopez
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Low-grade gliomas (LGG) represent a significant challenge for clinicians due to their location in critical brain areas and the diagnosis at younger ages than other brain tumors. Over the past few decades our understanding of these tumors has advanced considerably, but a significant gap remains regarding prognostic factors and optimal therapeutic strategies. This retrospective analysis seeks to shed light on the clinical, radiological, and molecular patterns associated with these tumors, with the goal of identifying factors that may influence therapeutic decisions.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
This is a retrospective descriptive study of 58 patients with an histologic confirmed LGG treated in our center between 2018 and 2023. Primary endpoints were overall survival (OS) stratified by glioma type, grade and type of surgery, and disease-free survival (DFS) stratified by adjuvant treatment.
RESULTS
We treated 39 women and 19 men, median age at diagnosis was 43 years (min 21 - max 79). A 53.4% were astrocytomas and 46.6% were oligodendrogliomas. A 75.9% were grade 2 and a 24.1% were grade 3. IDH-mutation was found in 53 patients (98,1%). Fourty-three percent had a complete resection (CR), 50% had a subtotal resection (STR) and 6,9% had only a biopsy. Seven (28%) of the patients with CR received adjuvant treatment. Of the 29 with STR, 24 (82.8%) received adjuvant treatment. Adjuvant treatment was radiotheraphy in 33 patients and chemotherapy in 27. It was given concomitantly in 13 cases. With a median follow - up of 48,5 months (IQR 55), 23 patients (46%) had a local relapse and 10 (17,2%) died. OS was higher in oligodendrogliomas (mean 106,4 vs 192,1 months; p = 0.038) and in grade 2 tumors (mean 164,3 vs 51,0 months; p < 0,01). There were no diference in OS between CR and STR. DFS was higher with adjuvant treatment (median 61 vs 31 months; p = 0.039).
CONCLUSIONS
This retrospective analysis highlights the heterogeneity and complexity of low-grade gliomas. Our data confirm that oligodendrogliomas and WHO grade 2 tumors are associated with significantly better overall survival. Interestingly, the extent of resection did not significantly impact survival outcomes, emphasizing the importance of a tailored approach when balancing resection with neurological risk. Moreover, adjuvant treatment was associated with longer disease-free survival, particularly in patients with subtotal resection. These findings support the role of molecular profiling and individualized treatment strategies in optimizing outcomes for patients with LGG. <!--EndFragment-->

title: EP12.03 «THE USE OF 5-AMINOLEVULINIC ACID IN GLIAL BRAIN TUMORS AND THE ROLE OF COMBINATION THERAPY»
authors: D Berdibayeva; N Ryskeldiev; A Kabykenova; S Akshulakov
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Recently, 5-ALA-induced fluorescence has been widely used in glioma surgery. The use of 5-ALA in neurosurgery allows to minimize the tumor volume and reduce neurological deficit, which can lead to an increase in patient survival. Objective: To analyze the survival of patients with glial tumors after microsurgical tumor removal using the drug gliolan (5-ALA).
MATERIAL AND METHODS
The study included 91 patients with glial brain tumors who underwent microsurgical tumor removal using fluorescence navigation (5 ALA), who were inpatients at the National Center for Neurosurgery in Astana from January 2022 to September 2023. Of these, 43 patients were male, 48 patients were female. The average age was 49.2 years. The age category of patients was from 19 to 77 years. All patients underwent microsurgical removal of the tumor using 5-ALA.
RESULTS
Of the 91 patients, 1 patient had a glial brain tumor G1, two patients had G2, 14 patients had G3, and 74 patients had G4-74. Total removal of tumors using 5-ALA was achieved in 43 patients, which was 47.2%. Subtotal removal was achieved in 34 patients, 37.6%, and partial removal was achieved in 14 patients, i.e. 15.3% of patients. The overall survival of 91 patients was 35 patients, which is 38.4% up to 3 years after surgery. During the analysis, 53 patients out of 91 received a course of radiotherapy, of which 37 patients received combination therapy with chemotherapy. In the analysis of surviving patients, 27 of 35 received a full course of chemoradiotherapy and only 7 patients did not receive a full course of CRT.
CONCLUSION
Analysis of 91 patients with glial tumors shows that the use of 5-ALA fluorescence improves the possibility of maximal removal of the brain tumor volume. In addition, the role of complex therapy in the postoperative period plays an important role in the study of survival.

title: EP12.04 REAL-WORLD SURVIVAL OUTCOMES AFTER (CHEMO)RADIOTHERAPY FOR WHO 2021-CLASSIFIED GLIOMAS: A MULTICENTER ANALYSIS OF CLINICAL, TREATMENT-RELATED, DOSIMETRIC, AND HEMATOLOGIC PROGNOSTIC FACTORS
authors: M Bilski; G Noel; K Smółka; K Kuncewicz; W Kuznicki; L Feuvret; K Korab; M Peszyńska-Piorun; P Korona; I Baranowska; A Suleja; F Mastroleo; R Kotecha; J Jurkiewicz; J Fijuth; B A Jereczek-Fossa; K Krystkiewicz; & Kuncman
abstract:
BACKGROUND
The 2021 WHO classification of gliomas introduced molecular profiling into the diagnostic criteria, reshaping prognosis and therapeutic strategies. However, most existing outcomes data are based on previous classifications, creating a knowledge gap regarding survival outcomes for gliomas with contemporary molecular characterization. We aimed to provide new real-world evidence for survival outcomes in patients with WHO 2021-classified gliomas to evaluate the prognostic impact of radiation-induced leukopenia/lymphopenia (RIL) alongside clinical and dosimetric factors.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
Data from patients with intracranial WHO grade (G) 2-4 gliomas diagnosed according to the WHO 2021 criteria, treated with surgical resection followed by radio(chemo)therapy, were retrospectively collected across four centers in Poland and France. For patients diagnosed before the WHO 2021 classification, a molecular analysis of IDH1/2 and 1p19q codeletion was performed prospectively. Primary endpoints, overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS), were evaluated by clinical, treatment-related, dosimetric, and RIL parameters. Statistical analyses were performed using Python libraries scikit-learn and statsmodels.
RESULTS
A total of 179 patients (median age 53 years) were included. IDH1/2 mutations and 1p/19q codeletion were identified in 55.3% and 22.4% of cases, respectively. According to the WHO 2021 criteria, 45 tumors were G2, 51 G3, and 83 G4. Chemotherapy was administered in 74.9% of patients, and the median radiotherapy dose was 60 Gy (32.5-80 Gy). Patients with IDH1/2 mutations demonstrated significantly longer PFS (7.7 vs. 1.0 years; p<0.01) and OS (8.2 vs. 2.5 years; p<0.01). 1p/19q codeletion correlated with longer PFS (7.7 vs. 1.6 years; p<0.01) but not OS. In WHO G3 gliomas, the addition of chemotherapy significantly improved PFS (6.8 vs. 3.6 years; p<0.01) and OS (6.9 vs. 3.9 years; p<0.01). Lower grades of leukopenia (0-2) were associated with longer PFS (3.6 vs. 1.2 years; p=0.02) and OS (7.2 vs. 3.2 years; p=0.04) compared to severe leukopenia. Patients with an ALC ≤1×10³/mm³ had significantly inferior survival outcomes, with shorter OS (5.3 vs. 8.7 years; p=0.0043) and PFS (1.4 vs. 6.8 years; p<0.001). A clinical target volume (CTV) cut-off of 127 cm³ predicted OS in WHO G4 gliomas (1.7 vs. 3.2 years; p=0.012). Principal component analysis confirmed that glioma grade, molecular alterations, hematologic parameters, and steroid use were major factors associated with survival, while dosimetric parameters showed a moderate correlation with hematologic variables.
CONCLUSION
This multicenter study provides RWE that molecular, clinical, hematologic, and dosimetric factors significantly impact survival in WHO 2021-classified gliomas, emphasizing the need for their integration into personalized treatment strategies.

title: EP12.05 REAL WORLD EXPERIENCE OF PATIENTS WITH IDH-MUTANT GRADE 4 ASTROCYTOMA TREATED WITH CHEMORADIATION
authors: N Aggarwal; G Shyam; O Al-Salihi; K Chia; A Swampillai; L Brazil; J Glendenning; V Manik; S L Forner
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Since the 2021 WHO CNS tumour classification, IDH-mutant WHO grade 4 astrocytoma has been recognised as a distinct molecular entity, separate from IDH-wildtype glioblastoma. While the Stupp protocol (60 Gy in 30 fractions with concurrent and/or adjuvant temozolomide) is standard for glioblastomas (IDH-wildtype), no single standard exists for IDH-mutant tumours. Some institutions adopt Stupp by analogy; others favour CATNON-based regimens (59.4 Gy in 33 fractions with adjuvant temozolomide). The choice of regimen and number of cycles varies. Evidence to guide treatment remains limited.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
We retrospectively reviewed patients with IDH-mutant grade 4 astrocytoma treated with a chemo-radiation approach at two UK neuro-oncology centres from 2019-2024. All underwent maximal safe resection followed by radiotherapy (60 Gy in 30 fractions), with concurrent and, where possible, 6-12 cycles of adjuvant temozolomide. Demographic, molecular, treatment and outcome data were collected. MGMT promoter methylation was assessed quantitatively, with ≥10% considered methylated. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to estimate progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS), with censoring at last follow-up for those that had not progressed or died.
RESULTS
Nineteen patients were included (63% male, median age 37 years). Most underwent debulking or partial resection. MGMT promoter methylation was present in 68%. Median PFS was 20 months (range 6-59) and median OS was 28 months (range 8-68). When stratifying by MGMT status, median PFS for the methylated group was 21 months (6-53), OS 28 months (9-68). For the unmethylated group, PFS was 13.5 months (8-18) and OS 20.5 months (8-35). Fourteen patients (74%) completed at least six cycles of adjuvant temozolomide; others discontinued due to progression. Intention to treat analysis confirms when planned for 6 cycles (11 patients), the PFS is 17 (6-39) and OS is 21 (8-68). For 12 intended cycles (8 patients), the PFS is 23.5 (10-59) and OS is 33.5 (15-59). Results are presented as intention-to-treat; as-treated analysis yielded comparable outcomes. At the time of analysis, 37% had progressed and 21% had died.
CONCLUSION
This multi-centre retrospective study adds to the limited real-world evidence for IDH-mutant WHO grade 4 astrocytoma. Survival outcomes in our cohort were encouraging, particularly among patients with MGMT promoter methylation and those receiving extended adjuvant temozolomide. These findings reflect variability in practice and highlight the need for prospective data to define optimal management in this molecular subgroup.

title: EP12.06 EARLY CSF DISSEMINATION OF THALAMIC MALIGNANT GLIOMA IN ADULT: CASE SERIES OF 7 PATIENTS
authors: J Hwang; C Lee; K Park; S Park
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Thalamic gliomas constitutes 1-5% of intracranial tumors. They are common in children and high grade tumor is more frequently occurred in adult. The outcome of thalamic malignant gliomas (TMG) is dismal, reported overall survival is around 1 year. Early progression is a main factor of survival limitation of TMG and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) dissemination is occasionally found during the progression. Authors report the case series of early CSF dissemination in adult patients with TMG.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
The clinical and radiological data of 26 adult patients with histologically proven thalamic gliomas were reviewed retrospectively. All patients were performed either resection or stereotactic biopsy, and followed by radiotherapy and/or chemotherapy. Of those, the patients with distant CSF dissemination were included.
RESULTS
Seven (26.9%) patients revealed the radiological distant CSF dissemination with mean 16.5 months (range, 3.5-35) after operation. Five patients were male and mean age was 38.7 years (range, 25-47). Pathological diagnosis was astrocytoma, grade 3 in 5 and diffuse midline glioma, H3 K27M-mutant in 2. As the first treatment, open resection or stereotactic biopsy was performed in 4 and 3, respectively. Adjuvant treatment was Stupp regimen (CCRT followed by temozolomide chemotherapy) in 2 and radiation followed by chemotherapy in 4. The distant dissemination was ventricles in 5, 4th ventricle with posterior fossa in 1, and cranio-spinal in 1. Four patients did not showed primary site progression. Six patients received additional chemotherapy (temozolomide or bevacizumab). Median survival after CSF dissemination was 5.3 months.
CONCLUSION
Early CSF dissemination seems to be an important factor of survival limitation in patients with TMG and it occurs in both cases of open surgery and stereotactic biopsy. The mechanism of frequent CSF dissemination in TMG is uncertain and it needed further investigation. Authors suggest that distant CSF dissemination should be considered in the treatment of TMG in adult.

title: EP12.07 TTFIELDS: EXPERIENCES OF FAMILY MEMBERS
authors: M Karlsson; E Wahlberg; E Degsell; l Kastbom; A E Malmström
abstract:
BACKGROUND
TTFields is an established treatment for glioblastoma (GBM). In Sweden, TTFields often requires daily assistance of a family member to be offered to the patient, creating possible ethical problems. Little is known about family members’ own experiences of TTFields treatment.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
Semi-structured individual interviews were conducted with 21 family members of GBM patients who had been offered TTFields treatment. The interviews were analysed by qualitative content analysis.
RESULTS
The family members described that TTFields treatment created hope in an otherwise hopeless situation, even though some participants knew that hope was unrealistic in a long-term perspective. Their role in the practical daily assistance of device management was crucial and the patient depended on their help. This made the participants bound to the patients, limiting their own possibilities to travel and work. They also worried about personally falling ill, due to lack of backup alternatives assisting the patient with TTFields. Despite this, most expressed little caregiver burden, instead described that TTFields management created closeness, meaningfulness and strengthened the relationship with the patient. The family members described inadequate support from the healthcare, leaving them with unanswered questions, insufficient information and practical problems. Many felt abandoned by the healthcare, who were often described as uninterested. Staff from the private company providing the device were instead described as helpful and accessible.
CONCLUSION
Family members play an important role in TTFields treatment, which can be experienced as both burdensome and rewarding. Offering a backup solution for assistance with TTFields management if the family member is temporarily absent would be beneficial. Our study identified a need for better support and information from healthcare providers for family members assisting in TTFields treatment to create a secure situation.
SUPPORT
The Medical Research Council of Southeast Sweden (Dnr. FORSS-976715, 981775, 995108) and a grant from the Swedish Brain Tumor Association.

title: EP12.08 HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS’ EXPERIENCES OF TUMOR TREATING FIELDS (TTFIELDS) FOR GLIOBLASTOMA- A QUALITATIVE STUDY
authors: L Kastbom; M Zemmler; R Öberg; E Degsell; M Karlsson; A Malmström
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most common primary malignant brain tumor in adults and is associated with dismal prognosis. Standard treatment is maximal surgical resection followed by radiation with concomitant and adjuvant chemotherapy with temozolomide. TTFields is nowadays introduced into clinical practice in many countries, after showing that survival is prolonged with 5 months. TTFields allows the unique benefit of tumor treatment outside the hospital setting but also presents a number of specific challenges, where patients need support. In Sweden, TTFields is prescribed by physicians, while the service of equipment and control of its use is provided in the patient’s home by staff from the private company which supplies TTFields. This requires a close collaboration between healthcare providers, the private company and patients, thereby potentially creating conflicts of interest. This study explored healthcare providers’ experiences of TTFields, including views on challenges with the treatment, such as decision making and partnership with the private company providing the device.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
Healthcare providers involved in the care of patients with GBM were recruited. Semi-structured interviews were performed individually. The interviews were transcribed and analyzed using quantitative content analysis.
RESULTS
Interviews were completed with 17 physicians and 6 nurses with experience in working within neuro-oncology. The participants had varying opinions regarding the challenges and the magnitude of the practical and ethical problems. A benefit of TTFields is its limited toxicity compared to other treatment options. According to healthcare providers, more patients tolerate wearing the arrays than anticipated. Physically active patients may be more reluctant to using TTFields due to the device´s impact on daily life. Overall, the collaboration with the company providing TTFields is satisfactory, but raises ethical concerns, such as problems with confidentiality, high cost for the therapy and lack of documented agreement regarding collaboration between the company and healthcare providers. The current support system with visiting patients at home by staff from the private company is viewed as inappropriate. Instead, unaffiliated technicians or nurses are suggested for support, to avoid bias.
CONCLUSION
The introduction of TTFields as a treatment of patients with GBM constitutes a new concept of treating patients in close collaboration with industry. There is a need to search for new solutions for tackling practical and ethical issues. Support: The Medical Research Council of Southeast Sweden (Dnr. FORSS-976715, 981775, 995108) and a grant from the Swedish Brain Tumor Association.

This study explored healthcare providers’ experiences of TTFields, including views on challenges with the treatment, such as decision making and partnership with the private company providing the device.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
Healthcare providers involved in the care of patients with GBM were recruited. Semi-structured interviews were performed individually. The interviews were transcribed and analyzed using quantitative content analysis.
RESULTS
Interviews were completed with 17 physicians and 6 nurses with experience in working within neuro-oncology. The participants had varying opinions regarding the challenges and the magnitude of the practical and ethical problems. A benefit of TTFields is its limited toxicity compared to other treatment options. According to healthcare providers, more patients tolerate wearing the arrays than anticipated. Physically active patients may be more reluctant to using TTFields due to the device´s impact on daily life. Overall, the collaboration with the company providing TTFields is satisfactory, but raises ethical concerns, such as problems with confidentiality, high cost for the therapy and lack of documented agreement regarding collaboration between the company and healthcare providers. The current support system with visiting patients at home by staff from the private company is viewed as inappropriate. Instead, unaffiliated technicians or nurses are suggested for support, to avoid bias.
CONCLUSION
The introduction of TTFields as a treatment of patients with GBM constitutes a new concept of treating patients in close collaboration with industry. There is a need to search for new solutions for tackling practical and ethical issues. Support: The Medical Research Council of Southeast Sweden (Dnr. FORSS-976715, 981775, 995108) and a grant from the Swedish Brain Tumor Association.

title: EP12.09 EFFICACY AND SAFETY OF LOCOREGIONAL VS. INTRAVENOUS ADMINISTRATION OF CAR-T CELL THERAPY IN RECURRENT GLIOBLASTOMA: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND SINGLE-ARM META-ANALYSIS
authors: A Turpo Peqqueña; H Loza Chipa; F Martins Lamas; P Bermejo Rosado; C Núñez Basurco; D Medina; J Turpo Peqqueña; D Gamarra Chambi; M Zapana Espinoza; W Valencia Velasquez; L Puma Villanueva; G Huanca Quispe; J Murillo Gutierrez; R Hernández Mayor; A Torres Ortiz
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) is the most common and aggressive primary brain tumor in adults. Despite standard treatment—including surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy—recurrence is inevitable, and current options are limited. Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy has shown efficacy in hematologic malignancies and is being explored for GBM. The optimal route of administration has not been established, with locoregional routes (intraventricular, intracavitary, intratumoral) used to bypass the blood-brain barrier. This meta-analysis evaluates the efficacy and safety of locoregional CAR-T compared to intravenous delivery.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
A systematic review was conducted across six databases (PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, CENTRAL, and Google Scholar). Primary outcomes included partial and complete response rates, progression-free survival, and overall survival. Secondary outcomes included disease progression and stable disease. A random-effects meta-analysis was performed using R software, and the ROBINS-I tool assessed risk of bias.
RESULTS
Fourteen studies with 148 patients were included. The partial response rate was 10.89% (95% CI: 4.73-23.12%), and the complete response rate was 6.85% (95% CI: 3.43-13.21%). Disease progression occurred in 52.46% (95% CI: 38.60-65.95%) of patients, and 28.22% (95% CI: 17.83-41.60%) had stable disease. Higher partial response rates were observed with locoregional routes (intraventricular/intracavitary). Thirteen studies reported median overall survival (2.5-11.8 months), with intravenous therapy showing better initial survival and locoregional routes offering prolonged benefits. Progression-free survival (1.3-5.2 months) was more consistent with intravenous routes. All studies were phase 1 trials with high risk of bias.
CONCLUSION
Locoregional CAR-T may offer a partial response advantage for recurrent GBM compared to intravenous delivery. While intravenous therapy showed better early survival, intracranial delivery provided prolonged benefits. However, the lack of statistical significance and high heterogeneity limit these findings. Larger, well-controlled studies are needed to confirm CAR-T’s potential in GBM.

title: EP12.10 HEMIZYGOUS DELETION OF CDKN2A/B IN IDH-MUTATED GLIOMA LEADS TO WORSE PROGNOSIS
authors: A E Lipatnikova; F M Ippen; A Dénes; T Olsson Bontell; A Corell; S Ferreyra Vega; T Kling; A K Suwala; H Carén; A S Jakola
abstract:
BACKGROUND
The negative prognostic impact of CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion in IDH-mutated glioma is well established. However, the prognostic significance of a hemizygous deletion remains debated. This study aims to evaluate overall survival (OS) and clinical characteristics of IDH-mutated gliomas with a hemizygous deletion of CKDN2A/B, compared to patients with retained status.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
This retrospective study defined the following inclusion criteria; (i) Operated at Sahlgrenska university hospital between 2007-2023 (ii) 18 years or older (iii) diagnosed with either an IDH-mutated astrocytoma or oligodendroglioma grade 2-3 according to the 2021 WHO classification system. CDKN2A/B status was determined through visual assessment of copy-number plots generated from DNA methylation data. The level of the CDKN2A/B locus was compared to baseline, whole chromosomal losses and extensive segmental losses to determine gene status.
RESULTS
A total of 198 patients were included; 97 astrocytomas and 101 oligodendrogliomas. A hemizygous deletion of CDKN2A/B was identified in 21 cases. These patients had a significantly shorter OS compared to those with retained CDKN2A/B (8 years vs. 14 years, p = 0.02). This difference was significant in astrocytomas (n = 12, 6 years vs. 11 years, p = 0.03) but not in oligodendrogliomas (n = 9, 10 years vs. not reached, p = 0.27). Tumors with a hemizygous CDKN2A/B deletion presented more frequently with headache and motor deficits. However, in a sensitivity analysis, the distribution of debut symptom was only significant in oligodendrogliomas. There were no other significant differences regarding tumor volume, surgical approach or oncological treatment.
CONCLUSION
A CDKN2A/B hemizygous deletion is associated with worse survival in IDH-mutated astrocytomas.

title: EP12.11 SYNCHRONOUS WHO GRADE 3 OLIGODENDROGLIOMA AND GRADE 4 ASTROCYTOMA: A CASE REPORT
authors: W Yoon
abstract: Since the introduction of the fifth edition of the WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System, glioma diagnosis has become more standardized and heavily reliant on molecular characteristics. Consequently, the co-occurrence of distinct glioma subtypes within a single patient is exceedingly rare. We report the case of a 59-year-old patient who presented with seizures and was found to have two spatially distinct brain tumors: one in the right fronto-temporo-insular region and the other in the left frontal lobe. The maximum diameters of the right and left tumors were 8.9 cm and 4.6 cm, respectively. MRI of the left frontal lesion revealed heterogeneous contrast enhancement. Gross total resection of the left frontal tumor was performed first; the tumor involved the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, including the supplementary motor area, and contained xanthochromic fluid. Histopathological and molecular analysis yielded an integrated diagnosis of oligodendroglioma, IDH-mutant and 1p/19q-codeleted, CNS WHO grade 3. Subsequently, near-total resection of the right tumor was performed. This tumor involved the frontal pole, entorhinal cortex, frontal horn, caudate nucleus, corpus callosum, insula, internal capsule, and temporal pole, with necrosis observed near the internal capsule. Molecular profiling revealed absence of 1p/19q codeletion, leading to a diagnosis of astrocytoma, IDH-mutant, CNS WHO grade 4. Following both surgeries, the patient remained seizure-free and maintained a good performance status. Adjuvant radiotherapy (60 Gy in 30 fractions) and six cycles of PCV chemotherapy were administered. Although the pathogenesis of multicentric gliomas remains unclear, this case supports the hypothesis of a single-cell progenitor origin in gliomagenesis.

title: EP12.12 NEW GLIOBLASTOMA THERAPY INDUCES CELL DEATH AND INHIBITS TUMOUR MIGRATION VIA MODULATION OF APOPTOTIC GENES
authors: J H Charlton; S S Siddiqui; M Braoudaki
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Glioblastoma (GB) is a highly aggressive type of brain cancer with dismal survival rates, underlying the vital necessity for novel therapeutic strategies. In this study, the effects of two newly synthesized in-house dibenzalacetone derivative compounds, SHG-24 and SHG-31 were evaluated in two GB cell lines to explore potential therapeutic strategies for treating this aggressive malignancy.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
MTT assays were performed to assess cell viability upon treatment with both compounds,. A wound healing assay was used to monitor cell migration. The wound was created in A172 and U87MG cells, followed by treatment with the respective IC50 concentrations of SHG-24 and SHG-31. Images were taken at 0, 24, and 48 hours to observe wound closure. Colony formation assays were also completed to assess the effect on colonisation post treatment with the two compounds. Real-time quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) was performed to analyse the expression of apoptotic genes in SHG-31-treated A172 cells.
RESULTS
The viability assay revealed an IC50 of SHG-24 and SHG-31 as 15μM and 30μM, respectively in A172 cell line and 10μM for both compounds in U87MG cell line. Both SHG-24 and SHG-31 induced significant cell death at low concentrations in both cell lines. Both compounds also caused a notable delay in wound healing compared to untreated cells, with both exhibiting better effects than cisplatin. Cell proliferation and colony formation was completely inhibited post treatment with SHG-24 and SHG-31. Interestingly, RT-qPCR results showed that SHG-31 treatment led to increased expression of BAX and CASP3.
CONCLUSION
Overall, both compounds exhibited promising anti-cancer properties, with SHG-31 showing potential to induce apoptosis paving the way for new effective therapies against GB.

title: EP12.13 TARGETING THE INFILTRATIVE EDGE OF GLIOBLASTOMA: BIOMARKER INSIGHTS INTO EARLY TUMOR RECURRENCE
authors: M Barak; M Hendrych; J Brychta; T Kazda; P Pospíšil; M Hermanová; J Šána; R Jančálek
abstract: Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, WHO Grade 4 (GB), is the most common primary malignant brain tumor, accounting for approximately 50% of all gliomas. The current standard of care for GB consists of maximal safe surgical resection, with the aim of gross total or supramarginal resection whenever possible. Even when gross total resection (GTR) is achieved, a heterogeneous population of residual tumor cells typically persists along the infiltrative margins. These cells, characterized by distinct genetic, epigenetic, and microenvironmental profiles, serve as a reservoir for treatment-resistant subclones that can drive tumor recurrence. Although some studies have indicated that unresected residual cells in the peritumoral brain zone display distinct alterations compared to cells within the central tumor mass, only limited molecular analyses have been conducted. This study aims to analyze molecular profiles of distinct cell populations in the peritumoral infiltration zone using next-generation sequencing (NGS) to identify molecular features associated with early disease progression.

title: EP12.14 ASTROCYTOMA IDH-MUTANT WITH PRIMITIVE NEURONAL COMPONENT
authors: M Hendrych; P Pokorná; M Barak; R Jancalek; J Sana; R Jugas; O Slaby; T Kazda; P Pospisil; T Jirasek; J Soukup; D Hrabos; M Syrucek; P Delongova; M Svajdler; P Kasparova; M Koblizek; M Hermanova
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Astrocytoma, IDH-mutant, is the most common primary brain tumor in young adults, with peak incidence between 30 and 40 years of age. It is defined by mutations in the IDH1 or IDH2 genes and the absence of 1p/19q codeletion, and it frequently harbors alterations in ATRX and TP53. Rarely, astrocytoma, IDH-mutant, amay exhibit primitive neuronal differentiation, morphologically resembling “small round blue cell” tumors or large anaplastic embryonal-like cells.
METHODS
We analyzed 18 cases of astrocytoma, IDH-mutant, with primitive neuronal differentiation. In 11 cases where both the primitive neuronal and glial components were available, macrodissection was performed by a pathologist. Each component was subjected to separate genetic (next-generation sequencing) and epigenetic (DNA methylation profiling) analyses. Morphological and immunophenotypic features were also evaluated.
RESULTS
The primitive neuronal component was characterized by absent or markedly reduced GFAP expression, positivity for neuronal markers, a high Ki-67 proliferation index, and frequent TTF1 expression. This component also exhibited distinct epigenetic signatures and copy number alterations compared to the glial component. All tumors were high-grade, with extensive copy number variations, frequent MYCN amplification, and RB1 loss.
DISCUSSION
Astrocytoma, IDH-mutant, with a primitive neuronal component expands the morphological spectrum of IDH-mutant astrocytomas and presents a significant diagnostic challenge. Recognition of this rare subtype is critical due to its aggressive biological behavior. title: EP12.15 THE CORRELATION OF OBESITY AND INCIDENCE OF GLIOBLASTOMA WHO GRADE 4
authors: A Fjerza
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most common and aggressive primary brain neoplasia in adults. In recent years, a correlation of obesity and an incidence of tumors was shown for many solid cancers, including brain tumors. The present study aimed at determining the effects of lifestyle and dietary habits in the development of Glioblastoma WHO 4 and their effect in the overallsurvival after the operation.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
A retrospective review was performed for all patients with a histologically proven and first-diagnosed GBM between 2019 and 2023 in our department. Clinical and paraclinical parameters were acquired from patient documentation. Our study includes patients first diagnosed with primary GBM WHO Grade 4, IDH wildtype. Individuals with a secondary GBM or missing preoperative data were excluded. Data analysis of each patient included gender, age, BMI, Karnofsky performance score, tumor location and postoperative survival time.
RESULTS
In this study, 101 patients with a first diagnosed primary GBM were included (54 males, 47 females; mean age of 62.7 years, and range 33 to 82 years). All patients got a gross total resection. All of them received the standard adjuvant treatment according to Stupp et al. 52 Patients were overweight- Class I obesity, 18 patients had class II. Only 2 Patients were underweight and 29 patients had a normal weight. Ca. 69,3% of the patients with GBM were obese. Our study shows that there is an association between glioblastoma and overweight. Normal weight patients had a mean overall survival of 386.7, the obese patients had a mean OS of 463 days. 22 of the obese patients (from 70, ca. 31.4%) had an OS over mean OS (>463 days). This shows that the obesity does not impact the overallsurvival.
CONCLUSION
Our study finds an association of patient’s BMI with GBM’s incidence, but doesn’t show a relationship between BMI and OS.

title: EP12.16 NEXT-GENERATION SEQUENCING IN IDH-WILDTYPE GLIOBLASTOMA: A PATHWAY TO PRECISION THERAPEUTICS
authors: S DAS; S Ahlawat; S Nathany; R K Gupta; S Vaishya; R Patir
abstract:
BACKGROUND
IDH-wild-type glioblastomas are one of the most aggressive brain tumors in the adult population with a dismal prognosis. Despite radiation therapy and chemotherapy, the prognosis of this category remains grim with a 5-year survival rate remaining 5% and a median survival rate of 12-18 months. In the era of precision medicine, it is necessary to find molecular targeted genes for which targeted therapy is available
MATERIAL AND METHODS
Next-generation sequencing (NGS) was carried out in ten histologically and molecularly proven IDH-wild type glioblastomas.
RESULTS
Among the ten patients of glioblastoma, we have found out that five patients had mutations or fusions, against which targeted therapy is available. Two patients had PIK3CA mutation (targeted therapy Alpesilib), one patient has RET mutation (targeted therapy Selpercatinib & Pralsetinib), one patient had GOPC-ROS1 fusion (targeted therapy Crizotinib, Entrectinib & Repoctrectinib), one patient had PTPRZ1-MET fusion (targeted therapy Capmatinib & Tepotinib) and one patient had FGFR3-TACC3 fusion (targeted therapy Erdafitinib, Anlotinib, etc).
CONCLUSION
While the standard treatment for glioblastoma has remained unchanged for the last 15 years, targeted therapy holds promise. However, due to BBB (blood-brain barrier), tumor heterogeneity, and resistance mechanisms developed by glioma cells, the success rate of targeted therapy has not been promising. However ongoing research is going on to overcome BBB like using nanocarriers, combination with immunotherapy or chemotherapy, etc. Although we have limitation of cases, 50% of our cases have shown mutation or fusion, against which targeted therapy is available. This holds future promise for targeted therapy for IDH-wild type glioblastoma.

title: EP12.17 EMOTION RECOGNITION IN PATIENTS WITH INSULAR GLIOMAS
authors: A Olejnik; A Bala; T Dziedzic; P Kunert
abstract:
BACKGROUND
The insula, due to its numerous connections with other regions of the brain, has been shown to mediate the execution of a variety of cognitive processes, including executive functions, attention, visual-spatial functions, memory, language and also social cognition. Social cognition is a broad-ranging concept that encompasses a wide variety of functions, ranging from fundamental perceptual tasks such as facial emotion recognition to higher-order inferential processes concerning the mental states, intentions, and emotions of others. The objective of the present study was to evaluate the emotion recognition ability of patients with insular tumors, taking into account the influence of particular clinical and demographic variables such as laterality of the lesion, age, sex and education.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
A group of 51 patients (18 women, 33 men) with insular gliomas (28 left, 23 right; WHO G2: 24, G3 14, G4: 13) was examined during their hospitalization, one day before the surgery. A demographically matched control group (n = 43; 22 women, 21 men) of healthy subjects was also included in the study. The Reading the Mind in the Eyes Test (RMET) was used to assess the ability of emotion recognition.
RESULTS
In the emotion recognition task patients scored significantly lower than healthy subjects (M = 21.02 vs 25.58; t = -4.934; p < 0.001). Furthermore, patients with a tumor in the left hemisphere demonstrated significantly higher scores than those with a tumor in the right hemisphere (M = 22.70 vs M = 19.04; t = 2.478; p = 0.008), despite no significant differences in age, education or gender between the two groups. title: EP12.18 MULTIPLE HIGH GRADE GLIOMA IN YOUNG ADULT: A CASE REPORT FROM A DEVELOPING COUNTRY
authors: D D Prayanti; M Bustami; R R Keswani; K Niswati; H Mailani
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Multiple high-grade glioma is a rare case with poor prognosis. Based on communication between the lesions, it is differentiated into multifocal (MF) and multicentric (MC). The incidence of multiple HGG was 2-35% of central nervous system gliomas, prevalence rate was 19%. The prevalence rate of MC was 6%, while MF was 11%.
CASE PRESENTATION
18-year-old boy, admitted to ER with status epilepticus. He had focal generalized seizures 5 months before, controlled with valproic acid. Bilateral ptosis, bilateral abducens palsy, left motoric lateralization were also found. He complained of gait imbalance, dysphagia, and left tinnitus 1 month before. Head CT showed obstructive hydrocephalus, so we consulted to neurosurgeon to do VP shunt. After VP shunt, GCS improved, but there were left total ophthalmoplegia, right oculomotor, trochlear, trigeminal, and central type facial nerve palsy. EEG showed background slowing activity, bilateral general slowing on both hemispheres especially left side, no sign of NCSE nor status epilepticus. Brain MRI showed multiple lesions in posterior pons, left cerebellum, bilateral thalamus, and left amygdala, suggestive multiple glioma. 8 days after VP shunt, we performed suboccipital decompressive craniectomy and tumor biopsy on left cerebellar vermis. The biopsy result was high-grade glioma. After surgery, he was treated in ICU for a week. 13 days after surgery, the seizures relapsed and there was hyponatremia. 15 days after surgery, there was acute respiratory failure so we intubated him again and then performed tracheostomy. Pneumonia appeared as a complication of long-term care. Due to the instability of patient’s condition, we postponed the chemoradiation. We also still could not do some molecular examination to distinguish whether this was an adult-type or pediatric-type glioma because of some limitation of health coverage.
CONCLUSION
Diagnosing and treating multiple high-grade glioma could be challenging, especially in young-adult. It should be distinguished between adult-type or pediatric-type. Multiple high-grade glioma commonly has poor prognosis. Although facing some limitations in diagnostic modalities, supportive treatment must be provided to stabilize the patient. Multidisciplinary approach between neurooncologist, neurosurgeon, neurointensivist, radiologist, pathologist is important to provide optimal treatment.

title: EP13.01 ARE GLUCAGON RECEPTORS FOUND IN HUMAN MENINGIOMAS?
authors: S E Tollefsen; O Solheim; A Jarmund; R Meta; I Nordahl; P Mjønes; S H Torp
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Glucagon receptors are mostly expressed in adipocytes and hepatocytes. Both somatostatin receptors (SSTRs) and glucagon receptors are G-protein coupled receptors, that are essential for regulation of metabolism. SSTRs are used within theranostics and as a marker of meningioma in routine diagnostic pathology with high sensitivity. Although the expression of SSTRs in human meningioma is extensively studied, there are no studies on the immunoreactivity of glucagon receptors. The aim of our study was to explore if glucagon receptors are expressed in human meningiomas, with similar diagnostic sensitivity as SSTRs. Hence, we investigated the immunohistochemical expression of glucagon receptors in a large series of human meningiomas and related the findings to WHO grade.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
Our study included 162 patients operated for a primary, intracranial meningioma (WHO 2016 grade 1 or grade 2) in the period of 1991 to 2000 at St. Olavs Hospital, Trondheim University Hospital, Trondheim, Norway. Three tissue microarrays (TMAs) from each tumor specimen underwent standardized immunohistochemical procedures. Sections were incubated overnight at 4°C with a polyclonal glucagon receptor antibody (Invitrogen, PA5-33595, dilution 1: 100). Immunoreactivity was evaluated by two consultant pathologists using staining index (SI). Tumors with SI > 3 were considered positive.
RESULTS
Glucagon receptors were detected in 79% of the tumors specimens, demonstrating a moderate sensitivity for human meningiomas. WHO grade 2 meningiomas had a significantly higher expression of glucagon receptors (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION
Glucagon receptors are expressed in most human meningiomas, but to a less extent than SSTRs. The presence of glucagon receptors does not seem to hold potential as a diagnostic marker in meningiomas.

title: EP13.02 LEPTIN RECEPTORS (OB-R) EXPRESSION IN PATIENTS WITH MENINGIOMAS
authors: R Ardhini; N Priscilla Angga Kusuma; R Retnaningsih
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Meningiomas are the most common primary brain tumors arising from arachnoid cap cells. Account for approximately one-third of all primary central nervous system tumors. Several factors have been studied for a possible relationship to the development of meningiomas. Leptin, which primarily produced by adipose tissue, and its receptor widely expressed in brain tissue. They believed to have the role in brain tumor development including meningiomas. This study aim to analized factors influencing leptin receptors expression in meningioma patients.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
We performed a cross-sectional study on meningioma patients between March - September 2024 in Dr. Kariadi General Hospital, Indonesia. Data collected include demographic characteristic, body mass index (BMI), and Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus. Tumor volume measured by radiologist using Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), and tumor type based on histopathological analysis. Leptin receptors expression analyzed using immunohistochemistry methods.
RESULTS
There were 36 female subjects with WHO grade 1 meningioma involved in this study. The most common age were between 41-50 years (58%), most patients had normal BMI (63.9%), 86,1% did not have type 2 DM, 3-month contraceptive injection (progesterone) was the most widely used (74.9%). The most common subtype was meningothelial meningioma (61.1%). 19,4% patients had small tumor size and 80,6% had large tumor size. Leptin receptors were found in all patients, 2,8% patients had weak positive leptin receptor expression, 27,8% moderate positive expression, and 69,4% strong positive expression. There were no significant correlation between age, BMI, DM, hormonal contraception, meningioma subtype, tumor volume, and leptin receptor expression (p>0,01).
CONCLUSION
Our study showed that leptin receptors were found in all meningioma patients and most of them had strong positive expression. It showed that leptin and its receptor expression could be used for diagnostic biomarkers in meningiomas.

title: EP13.03 AN EVALUATION OF SHORT-TERM OUTCOMES AND FOLLOW-UP SCHEDULES AFTER MENINGIOMA SURGERY
authors: R Shah; T Tajsic; A Joannides
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Heterogeneity exists between neurosurgical centres and individual surgeons regarding schedules of clinic follow-up and imaging after meningioma surgery, driven in part by resource constraints. We aimed to evaluate short-term (1-2 year) post-surgical functional outcomes, focusing on the effects of surgical results, post-operative complications and follow-up.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
A retrospective cohort study of 146 patients (mean age 60.2 ± 15 years, 77% female) who underwent craniotomy for meningioma resection between April 2020 and March 2022 at a single tertiary centre was conducted. Operative records and patient charts were reviewed for demographics, tumour features, Simpson Grade, complications, functional outcomes and follow-up schedule. Multivariate regression was used to assess the relative importance of patient characteristics and provider factors in recovery.
RESULTS
Most patients were symptomatic preoperatively (92.5%), commonly with focal deficits (29.5%) and seizures (26.7%). The mean tumour diameter was 41.8±16.1mm, with 76.7% WHO Grade 1. Simpson Grade 1 or 2 resection was achieved in 84.2% of cases. Post-operative complications within 30 days occurred in 41.1%, including new or worsened focal deficits in 15.8%, seizures in 9.6% and infection in 3.4%. In 52.7% of cases, patients were discharged in ≤4 days. Functional status improved significantly, with mean mRS scores decreasing from 2.1 pre-surgery to 1.8 at one year and 1.4 at two years (p < 0.05). Considering follow-up, 47.3%, 84.9%, and 95.9% of patients were reviewed in clinic within one, three, and six months, respectively. The first surveillance MRI occurred at a mean of 4.7 months, with 66.4% completed within five months. Timely imaging and clinic review correlated with improved functional recovery in multivariate analyses (p = 0.006 and 0.037 respectively). Advanced age, multifocal tumours, and complications within 30 days were also significant predictors of adverse outcomes.
CONCLUSION
Meningioma surgery is associated with substantial functional improvement. Early and structured follow-up, including timely imaging, is a significant factor in uncomplicated recovery. A consistent set of outcome measures is helpful for understanding surgical outcomes across cohorts.

title: EP13.04 DEMOGRAPHIC, LOCATION, SIGN AND SYMPTOMS OF INTRACRANIAL MENINGIOMA AND ITS ASSOCIATION WITH TUMOR GRADE
authors: T Aninditha; J Odilo; D Tandian; I Savitri Madjid; H R Sofyan; R Andriani
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Epidemiologically, meningioma is the most common benign primary intracranial tumor. The tumor has been profoundly affect women compared to men. The majority of tumor located on cranial base. The symptoms of meningioma varied depends on the location of the tumor. Headache, seizure, and focal neurological deficits had variously reported before. Based on the WHO classification, there were benign meningioma (grade I) and non-benign meningioma (grade II-III). Although previous study suggest that benign meningioma has a predilection on the cranial base, the association between demographic, location, and sign and symptoms of meningioma with tumor grade remain uninvestigated. This study aims to investigate the association of demographic, location, sign and symptoms of meningioma with its tumor grade.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
This study is a cross sectional study of intracranial meningioma patients from 2013-2023 underwent surgery in Cipto Mangunkusumo General Hospital. Demographic, radiologic, and clinical data were retrieved from medical record. A chi-square analysis performed to determine the association of investigated variables with tumor grade.
RESULTS
There were 531 subjects acquired in this study of which the majority were female (92.1%). The median age of the subjects were 45(18-82) years old. Most of the subjects had tumor on cranial base (77.2%). Benign meningioma were found in the majority of subjects (89.6%). Gender (p=0.424), age (p=0.561), headache (p=0.176), sensory deficit (p=0.105), cranial nerve deficit (p=0.242), seizure (p=0.808), decreased consciousness (p=0.073) and hemianopia (p=0.377) were not associated with tumor grade. Meanwhile, convexity location (p=0.000) and motoric deficit (p=0.002) were associated with non-benign meningioma.
CONCLUSION
This study shows that convexity tumor is associated with non-benign meningioma. This finding is consistent with previous study findings. Motoric deficits also associated with non-benign meningioma. This could be explained by convexity tumor will affect motoric pathway more than on the cranial base. However, there are no association of gender and age with tumor grade found in this study although previous study showed otherwise. These findings remain to be investigated.

title: EP13.05 STEREOTACTIC RADIOSURGERY FOR MENINGIOMA - SINGLE CENTRE EXPERIENCE ON SAFETY AND SEIZURE
authors: J W Ho
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) is a treatment option for meningioma that are untreated or recurrent after surgery and fractionated radiotherapy. The local control rate after SRS is around around 95% at 5 years. The incidence of seizure after SRS is approximately 5-15%. The purpose of our study is to evaluate the risk of seizure after SRS at our centre.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
Patients treated within a 2-year period from March 2023 to March 2025 were analysed. SRS dose was 16Gy /1 fraction or 25Gy/5 daily fractions for larger meningiomas (e.g. >10cc) or in order to meet organ-at-risk dose constraints. MRI head with contrast is performed after 6 months to evaluate response.
RESULTS
56 patients with 60 meningiomas were treated. The median follow-up duration was 242 days. The median volume of meningioma was 4.7cc (range 0.21-17.7cc). 50 meningiomas were treated with 16Gy/1 fraction (median volume 4.69cc) and 10 with 25Gy/5 fractions (median volume 12.7cc). 34 patients had no prior treatment for meningioma while 22 patients had recurrence after surgery including 7 who also had adjuvant fractionated radiotherapy. Following SRS four patients developed seizure. 2 patients had no prior treatment, 1 had prior surgery and 1 had prior surgery and adjuvant radiotherapy. The mean time to seizure was 141 days (range 89 - 189 days). MRI head at the time of seizure showed that 3 patients had increased perilesional oedema and meningioma changes consistent with radionecrosis while 1 patient had no apparent radiological change. Seizures were managed with anti-epileptic medication. Independent samples t-test showed no statistical difference in meningioma volume, prescribed dose or brain dose (V12Gy, D50%) between patients who developed seizures compared to those who did not. The analysis was limited by the small number of patients who developed seizure.
CONCLUSION
SRS for meningioma is safe and associated with a low seizure risk of 7% at our centre. Further work, with a larger sample size and longer follow up period is needed to determine the risk factors of seizures after SRS for meningioma.

title: EP14.01 A RARE CNS PRIMARY COLLISION TUMOR IDH-WILDTYPE GLIOBLASTOMA WITH COEXISTENT EPENDYMOMA A CASE REPORT
authors: B Lazo Poveda; J Navarro Fernández; B Cacho Vega; A Rodríguez Camacho; E Caballé Pérez; C Caro Sánchez; D Vega Moreno; M Serrano Murillo; O Chávez Martínez; A González Vázquez; G Reyes Soto
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Gliomas arise from glial progenitor cells and constitute a heterogeneous group of tumors. They include mainly glioblastomas, astrocytomas, oligodendrogliomas and ependymomas. IDH-wildtype Glioblastoma are the most common primary CNS malignant tumors. Ependymomas arise from the lining cells of the ventricular system, and less common in the brain parenchyma. A collision tumor is a neoplastic lesion comprised of two or more distinct cell populations.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
A case report of 54-year-old woman harboring IDH-wildtype glioblastoma with concomitant grade 3 ependymoma with 19q deletion.
RESULTS
A 54-year-old woman presented with a 2-week history of headache and progressive left hemiparesis. Brain MRI showed an intra-axial lesion in the right frontal lobe with contrast enhancement and calcifications in SWI. She underwent craniotomy with gross total resection (EOR 95%). Histopathological examination identified two distinct tumor components: one with features of a high-grade glioma: extensive necrosis and microvascular proliferation, positive immunoreactivity for GFAP and S100 protein. The other component exhibited ependymal differentiation characterized by perivascular pseudorosettes, morphologically corresponding to ependymoma. Immunohistochemistry, PCR and FISH analysis, revealed that the high-grade glioma component was IDH-wildtype and lacked 1p/19q codeletion, consistent with the diagnosis of IDH-wildtype Glioblastoma WHO grade 4. The ependymoma component was WHO grade 3 with 19q deletion only. ZFTA fusion and YAP1 fusion were not performed. No co-deletion was found in any component The pathologically calculated proportion in the sample was 60% ependymoma and 40% glioblastoma. Neuroaxis MRI and CSF analysis showed no evidence of distal tumor activity. Stupp protocol was given to treat the most aggressive component. Currently she has 1 year progression-free survival, with complete response by RANO criteria; functionally KPS 100% and ECOG 0.
CONCLUSION
This is an extraordinarily rare case of a CNS collision tumor that represents a challenge in diagnosis and management. These tumors are scantily described with only two cases reported.

CONCLUSION

title: EP14.02 CLIVAL DIFFUSE LARGE B-CELL LYMPHOMA AS AN UNCOMMON INITIAL PRESENTATION: A DIAGNOSTIC CHALLENGE AT THE SKULL BASE
authors: Y J Garcilazo Reyes; J O Navarro-Fernández; N Zapata-Canto; D Magos-Rodríguez; E Gómez-Apo; M Ramos-Ramírez; D Gasca-Saldaña; R Hernández-Ramírez; A Montenegro-Rosales
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Clival involvement by primary or secondary diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is extremely rare and may mimic other skull base tumors such as chordomas or metastases. Due to its anatomical location, lesions in this area may initially present with cranial neuropathies, often delaying diagnosis and treatment.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
We report the case of a 43-year-old woman with no prior medical history who presented with binocular diplopia due to right sixth cranial nerve palsy, in the absence of systemic symptoms. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed a right-predominant clival infiltrative lesion extending ventrally and caudally into the petrous apex and Meckel’s cave, with mild T2 hyperintensity, heterogeneous enhancement, absent bone remodeling, and involvement of cranial nerves V, VI, IX, X, and XI. Although chordoma was initially suspected, the atypical imaging features prompted further evaluation. FDG-PET revealed multifocal hypermetabolic lesions in the pancreas, spleen, pelvic lymph nodes, iliac/gluteal muscles, and subcutaneous tissue, with lytic bone involvement in the iliac crest and clivus. Laboratory tests showed mild leukopenia, elevated LDH (1270 U/L), and negative tumor markers (CA 19-9, CEA, β-hCG, CA-125). Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis and flow cytometry were negative for malignancy. A trans-sphenoidal biopsy was performed following tumor board discussion. Histopathological analysis confirmed DLBCL of non-germinal center phenotype
RESULTS
The disease was staged as Ann Arbor IV-A, with high-risk International Prognosis Index (IPI). Despite no CSF involvement, craniospinal radiotherapy, systemic chemotherapy (polatuzumab vedotin, rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin) and intrathecal chemotherapy (cytarabine/methotrexate) were administered. At six months, the patient is clinically stable with neurologic improvement and complete metabolic response.
CONCLUSION
Secondary clival lymphoma is rare and may mimic other skull base tumors. Distinctive imaging features should raise suspicion. A multidisciplinary management is essential for timely diagnosis and treatment.

title: EP14.03 RAPID RECURRENCE OF A ASTROBLASTOMA IN A YOUNG ADULT.
authors: A Fjerza
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Astroblastoma is a rare neuroepithelial brain tumor of uncertain origin, primarily affecting children and young adults. It accounts for 0.45-2.8% of all neuroglial tumors. Diagnosing astroblastoma is challenging due to its resemblance to other glial neoplasms in both histopathology and imaging. These tumors are typically large, peripheral, and located in the frontoparietal hemispheres, though they can also appear in the cerebellum, brainstem, or hypothalamus. Symptoms include headache, vomiting, nausea, seizures, and altered consciousness.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
The 33-year-old patient had a progressive dizziness of two weeks. She had no history of trauma, serious medical problems or family history of brain tumors. Physical examinations showed normal vital signs and no focal neurologic deficits. Her brain- MRI revealed a large contrast medium uptake/ lesion parietooccipital at the left side. Due to the clinical and imaging findings, we opted for the tumorresection. The histology showed an astroblastoma. The patient had no neurological deficits. She got a postoperative radiochemotherapy according to Stupp, 8 weeks after the operation. The MRI-Control showed a progress of the resttumor. We followed up at 3 and 6 months. The last MRI showed a stable disease.
RESULTS
Astroblastoma is an extremely rare tumor that was previously referred to as “neuroepithelial tumors of uncertain origin”. Currently, the WHO classification of CNS tumors categorizes astroblastomas as “other neuroepithelial tumors”. A bimodal age distribution is commonly observed, with most reported cases presenting between the ages of 10 and 30.
CONCLUSION
Due to the rarity of astroblastoma and the difficulties in diagnosing it at an early stage, there is no established standard treatment. High-grade astroblastomas typically have a poor prognosis, characterized by invasion of surrounding brain regions, high recurrence rates, and rapid progression. In such cases, aggressive treatment and ongoing monitoring are crucial.
