title: EP14.04 ERDHEIM-CHESTER DISEASE WITH CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM INVOLVEMENT: A RARE CASE REPORT
authors: D Rahmawati; D P Retnani; F A Putri
abstract:
OBJECTIVE
Erdheim Chester disease (ECD) is a rare form of non-Langerhans cell histiocytosis. ECD is characterized by the infiltration of various organs by foamy CD68+ and CD1a- histiocytes. Although ECD primarily affects the skeletal system, it may involve multiple organs, with central nervous system (CNS). The most common neurological symptoms are cognitive difficulty, cerebellar ataxia, cranial neuropathy, pyramidal tract involvement, and seizures. Therapeutic options for ECD include BRAF inhibitors, MEK inhibitors, and interferon-α. Glucocorticoids and localized radiotherapy may be used as adjunctive therapies to manage acute central nervous system (CNS) symptoms. This paper review on the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges associated with the treatment of Erdheim Chester disease (ECD)
CASE
We present the case of a 71-year-old man with chronic progressive cephalalgia on the left side, gradual right-sided weakness, acute anomic aphasia, and cognitive decline over the same period. A head magnetic resonance imaging revealed findings suggestive of glioblastoma. Patient had maximal tumor resection and histopathological examination showed anaplastic cell proliferation with round to oval pleomorphic nuclei, coarse chromatin, and vacuolated cytoplasm, along with vascular proliferation, lymphocytic infiltration, and a high mitotic index (10/10 HPF). These features were suggestive of anaplastic astrocytoma. Immunohistochemical staining revealed GFAP positivity in glial cells; CD68 positivity in histiocytes; CD45, CD3, and CD20 expression in lymphocytes and a Ki-67 proliferation index of 5%. CD1a was negative. Patient was diagnosed Erdheim-Chester Disease.
CONCLUSION
The patient was initially diagnosed with glioblastoma, based on both radiological imaging and histopathological examination. However, subsequent histochemical analysis revealed GFAP positivity in glial cells, CD68 positivity in histiocytes, and CD45, CD3, and CD20 expression in lymphocytes, findings that were more consistent with a diagnosis of Erdheim-Chester Disease. This case underscores the need for thorough diagnostic workup in atypical CNS lesions to avoid misdiagnosis and ensure proper treatment selection. Keywords: Erdheim-Chester Disease, Central Nervous System, Histiocytosis, Clinician Evaluation

title: EP14.05 LYMPH NODE METASTASIS IN MYXOPAPILLARY EPENDYMOMA WITHOUT CNS INVOLVEMENT: A RARE CASE REPORT AND THERAPEUTIC RESPONSE
authors: A González-Vázquez; B Cacho-Díaz; A O Chávez-Martínez; E Caballe-Pérez; G Reyes-Soto; B E Lazo-Poveda; C O Lara-Torres; A M Cano Valdez; A Rodríguez-Camacho; O Arrieta; M Serrano-Murillo; D A Vega-Moreno
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Myxopapillary ependymomas are rare neoplastic tumors originating from ependymal glial cells of the spinal cord. They rarely metastasize but may exhibit malignant behavior characterized by distant neural dissemination and spinal drop metastases.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
This is a retrospective case report of an adult patient with extra-neural metastatic myxopapillary ependymoma, including his diagnosis, treatment, and clinical outcomes.
RESULTS
We report the case of a 44-year-old male who presented with non-specific lower back pain for over 20 years, associated with gradual tumor growth. A near-total sacral resection was performed, and one year later, local recurrence was identified, without cerebrospinal fluid infiltration but with extra-neural metastases involving bilateral inguinal, pelvic, and retroperitoneal lymph nodes. Biopsy of an inguinal lymph node confirmed metastatic myxopapillary ependymoma. The patient underwent radiotherapy with a total dose of 36 Gy to the primary site and involved lymph nodes, followed by a sequential boost to 54 Gy to areas of gross disease, delivered with concurrent cisplatin. Adjuvant chemotherapy with cisplatin and etoposide (CDDP/VP-16) was administered. A PET-CT performed one year after treatment showed a partial response, with no further dissemination and good control of both neural and extra-neural disease. The patient remains under multidisciplinary follow-up and continues physiotherapy.
CONCLUSION
This case highlights a rare presentation of myxopapillary ependymoma with lymphatic metastasis in the absence of CNS dissemination. It underscores the potential efficacy of combined modality treatment, including systemic therapy, in controlling aggressive variants of this tumor.

title: EP15.01 ASSOCIATION BETWEEN SOCIOECONOMIC STATUS AND DEPRESSION IN PATIENTS WITH BRAIN TUMORS - FIRST RESULTS OF THE DIVERSO TRIAL
authors: S Agkatsev; A Gude; M Lückemeyer; L Lazaridis; S Seidel; C Schaub; S Bingöl; E Dülberg; S Lici; L Brandt; P Roser; A Reinacher-Schick; N Thon; M von Lilienfeld-Toal; D Miller; C Seliger
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Depression has been shown to affect many patients diagnosed with malignant brain tumors, impacting their quality of life and overall survival. While a variety of factors can affect the development of depressive symptoms, to date it remains unclear which socioeconomic factors may play a role. The investigation of this research question is part of the DiVersO trial (Digitale Versorgung in der Onkologie), a prospective non-interventional study. The primary goal is to elucidate if patients prefer to complete surveys using electronic or paper questionnaires. In addition, the trial contains questionnaires, which will allow us to explore the association between demographic factors, socioeconomic status and depression.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
In the DiVersO trial patients with brain tumors including primary central nervous system lymphomas (PCNSL) receiving treatment at our institution fill in a range of questionnaires to assess their psychological and physiological burden. To analyze if there is a link between specific factors and depressive symptoms self-reported by the patients, the results of the Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ)-9 and the adapted Diversity Minimal Item Set (DiMIS)-DiVersO were used. Patient recruitment for this study is planned until Q4 2027, and the follow-up is expected to be completed in Q4 2029. The DiVersO study is registered in the German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS00034347).
RESULTS
Since trial initiation in Dec 2024, 51 patients have been enrolled (n=11 PCNSLs, n=22 gliomas, n=18 patients with brain metastases). Of these, 41% were female (n=21), 59% male (n=30), ranging from 28 to 86 years of age (median age 65). 69% filled in the questionnaires on paper (n=35) vs. 31% on a tablet (n=16). PHQ-9 was completed by n=42 patients, 57% male (n=24) and 43% female (n=18). A multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed on results of the PHQ-9, demographic factors, and socioeconomic factors derived from the DiMIS-DiVersO questionnaire. Preliminary analyses demonstrated a significant association between the general state of patients’ health and depression (OR 0.13, 95% CI 0.018-0.67, p=0.02), showing that “very good” or “good” self-rated health is associated with 87% lower odds of depression, relative to poor self-rated health. The factors sex, age, previous mental problems and financial worries, however, did not seem to be significantly associated with self-reported depressive symptoms.
CONCLUSION
The preliminary analysis showed an association between a patient’s general state of health and their depressive symptoms. While these findings need to be validated in a larger cohort, patients who experience “moderate”, “moderately severe” and “severe” depression need to be particularly closely monitored. As the recruitment is still ongoing, further results will be presented at the conference.

title: EP15.02 PATIENTS WITH OLIGODENDROGLIOMAS CNS WHO GRADE 2 AND 3 - PROGRESSION PATTERNS AND FUNCTIONAL OUTCOME IN LONG-TERM FOLLOW-UP
authors: S Josef; A Fischl; M Lenglinger; K Rosengarth; N O Schmidt; M Proescholdt; M J Riemenschneider; R Linker; E Bumes; P Hau
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Oligodendrogliomas are brain tumors typically associated with longer life expectancy and a more favorable prognosis than other gliomas. According to the current WHO classification, molecular testing for co-deletions of chromosomes 1p and 19q is essential to identify patients with CNS WHO grade 2 and 3 oligodendrogliomas who are more likely to benefit from radio-chemotherapy. However, given the relatively young age of these patients, the risk of impairment in somatic and neurocognitive function, quality of life, and social and occupational reintegration is significant, due both to the tumor and multimodal treatments.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
Clinical data of patients with a histologically confirmed diagnosis of oligodendroglioma, IDH mutant (CNS WHO grade 2 and 3), who were diagnosed and treated at the University Hospital of Regensburg until July 2023, were collected using a non-interventional, mixed retrospective-prospective study approach. Data include demographics (age, gender), prognostic factors (KPS at initial diagnosis, extent of resection), treatment modalities, as well as outcome data (PFS, OS). In addition, data on symptoms (NANO), cognition (NeuroCoq Fx), quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30 and BN20), and social and occupational reintegration (specific questionnaire) were collected in a cross-sectional approach at elective scheduled follow-up appointments. Key endpoints are treatment patterns, symptoms, cognition, quality of life, social and occupational reintegration and outcomes in a real-world setting. In addition, correlations of treatment patterns and outcomes with symptoms, cognition, quality of life, and social and occupational reintegration will be investigated. A total of 105 patients were identified through the local clinical cancer registry. Of these, 4 could not be assigned to a local patient ID, 7 had a histology other than oligodendroglioma, and 15 were excluded due to missing data. Therefore, 79 patients were included, of whom 48 are still in follow up. Of these, 46 patients completed quality of life questionnaires, and 44 of them underwent neuropsychological testing during their follow-up appointments.
RESULTS
The data collection phase has been completed in March 2025. We started with data analysis, that will be completed by the time of the EANO meeting. After a descriptive analysis, significant factors identified in univariable analyses will be further evaluated by correlation analyses and multivariable analyses.
CONCLUSION
Our study will provide unprecedented data on long-term follow-ups in a homogenous cohort of patients with oligodendroglioma, IDH mutant (CNS WHO grade 2 and 3), with a specific focus on long-term quality-of-life, cognitive and social outcomes. It will therefore provide a starting point for the development of prospective supportive measures for this specific patient population.

title: EP15.03 PAEDIATRIC FOURTH VENTRICULAR TUMORS -CLINICO-PATHOLOGICAL STUDY WITH ASSESSMENT OF QUALITY OF LIFE OF CAREGIVERS: PERSPECTIVE FROM INDIA
authors: S JAISWAL
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Fourth ventricular tumors are one of the common tumors visiting Neurosurgery OPD in India. Multimodality approach involves a dedicated and often a long-term patient care and rehabilitation. Diagnosis and management of the brain tumors requires multiple hospital visits and brings about unique challenges to the caregiver. Quality of life of the caregiver is invariably affected in these circumstances. A drastic change in the quality of life of the caregiver may lead to poor compliance to the treatment and inferior outcome. Most of the literature available on quality-of-life assessment is from developed countries and cannot be extrapolated in Indian scenario. Studying the clinical profile of paediatric fourth ventricle tumors and its effect on the quality of life of the caregiver provided us a valuable data which can be further utilized to make positive changes in the institutional policies in India.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
This prospective study was conducted at Neurosurgery department King George’s Medical University, India over a period 6 months from January 2024 to June 2024. Detailed clinical & radiological profile and histopathology was documented. Surgical procedures, intraoperative events, duration of hospital stay, mortality, morbidity and follow up details were also noted. Details of caregiver were noted and Quality of life of caregiver was evaluated based on World Health Organization Quality of Life- BREF (WHOQOL- BREF) questionnaire at time of admission and at 3 month follow up. The domains in above questionnaire were physical health, psychological, social relationships and environment. Change in above scores was assessed in four categories-children with clinical deterioration trend, improving trend, constant trend and expired after discharge.
RESULTS
30 patients were part of the study with age ranging from 6 months to 12 years. Medulloblastoma was the most common pathological entity. In hospital mortality of 13.3% was recorded. All those children who had deteriorated in their morbidity status (5), their caregivers showed decline in their WHO- TOTAL QOL index and WHO-Environment domain. There was a statistically significant decline in the total score of QOL of caregiver of children with deteriorated trend and those who expired after discharge. The improvement in the total score of QOL of caregivers of children who had an improved clinical trend was not statistically significant.
CONCLUSION
The changes that occur in the quality of life of the caregiver during the treatment journey of these paediatric tumour’s patients were profound especially in the resource crunch settings in India. On understanding the observation of the study, it can be widely suggested that a neurosurgeon role in India expands beyond surgical intervention and it must encompass a constant introspection of outcomes and holistic approach towards patient caregiver unit.

title: EP15.04 DEVELOPING A CONTEXT-BASED SUPPORTIVE CARE INTERVENTION FOR INFORMAL CAREGIVERS AND PATIENTS WITH ADULT-TYPE DIFFUSE GLIOMA GRADE 4
authors: T Gómez Vecchio; I Henoch; A Ozanne
abstract:
BACKGROUND
There is a high prevalence of unmet needs affecting both informal caregivers and patients with adult-type diffuse glioma grade 4. Recognizing the impact of unmodifiable demographic and clinical factors affecting patients’ health-related quality of life, this study aims to develop a supportive care intervention for patients and informal caregivers tailored to local care system specifics.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
A qualitative approach utilizing focus group interviews was employed, involving healthcare professionals (HCPs) from diverse stakeholders in Region Västra Götaland, Sweden. The interviews, conducted physically and digitally from November 2024 to March 2025, utilized semi-structured guides designed to last up to two hours, ensuring participants could engage during their working hours. Based on local clinical workflows, we approached the chief staff at 12 healthcare units and 6 municipal and community services (including healthcare organizations within county and municipal jurisdiction). Participants were recruited by email. The inclusion criteria were HCPs with direct experience in caring for patients with glioma grade 4 or those who are in regular contact with informal caregivers. Data analysis is ongoing, using manifest content analysis.
RESULTS
Twelve chief staff granted us access to their HCPs. A total of 12 focus groups were conducted including 44 HCPs. The sample included 35 (79%) participants from four hospitals under county jurisdiction, and 9 (21%) participants from units under municipal jurisdiction. In our sample eleven (25%) HCPs had up to five years’ experience, 18 (41%) had between 5 to 10 years of work experience, and 15 (34%) had more than ten years of experience in caring for patients with glioma grade 4 or their informal caregivers. The sample included 18 (41%) nurses, 10 (23%) social workers, six (14%) physicians, three (7%) physiotherapists, three (7%) occupational therapists, two (4%) psychologists, one (2%) speech therapist, and one (2%) nutritionist. Additionally, five (11%) of the HPCs had executive or leading responsibilities. Emergent themes were (i) the role of contact nurses within and between care units and sections; (ii) the value of multidisciplinary teamwork; and (iii) extending service overlap across different units and sections.
CONCLUSION
Although conclusions are pending further analysis, the findings underscore the need for improved alignment between HCPs’ intentions and patients’ expectations across various healthcare settings. Additionally, there appears to be a lack of alignment among HCPs’ intentions between different units and sections. An advisory board comprising researchers, healthcare professionals, patients, and informal caregivers will review our findings before publication.

title: EP15.05 AN EVIDENCE-BASED AND PERSON-CENTERED CARE PLAN FOR PATIENTS WITH PRIMARY MALIGNANT BRAIN TUMOR- A PHD PROJECT PROTOCOL
authors: M Mathiasen; H Pappot; K Piil; A D Nørøxe; F W Boele
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Patients with high-grade gliomas (HGG) experience significant physical, psychological, and cognitive symptoms, which can impact their ability to communicate and reduce their quality of life. Additionally, informal caregivers face substantial challenges impacting family dynamics. The high burden and unpredictable course of the disease, combined with the complexity of symptom clusters, make it essential to offer patients with HGG and their families a well-defined care plan (CP). A CP facilitates involvement in shared clinical decision-making processes, and may help inform and empower patients, ultimately improving quality of life and reducing hospital visits. Although effective symptom management is a crucial and integral part of CP, systematic symptom identification followed by information and support are often suboptimal in clinical practice, which may negatively impact patient symptom experience and treatment adherence. To address these challenges, this PhD project plans to develop a person-centered and evidence-based neuro-oncological CP: ‘My NeuroPath,’ tailored to HGG patients and their caregivers’ unique needs.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
The PhD study (2025-2028) is a three-phase, multi-method, sequential cohort study with the following objectives: 1) A systematic review 2) Establish a NeuroPath Panel of HGG patients and caregivers, 3) Design of the intervention My NeuroPath through an iterative participatory process, 4) Develop a Neuro-Care educational program for health care professionals, and 5) Examine the feasibility and safety of ‘My NeuroPath’ using a multi-methods design, and its potential impact on patients’ quality of life.
RESULTS
Although yet unavailable, at the EANO meeting, we will share findings related to objectives 1 and 2. Specifically, we will share the systematic review findings, which will be used to support the overall research rationale and the establishment of NeuroPath Panel.
CONCLUSION
By developing and testing a tailored neuro-oncological CP, we anticipate improving the collaboration between patients, caregivers, and healthcare professionals, thereby ensuring person-centered care with the potential to maintain or improve patients’ quality of life. Furthermore, we envision that the Neuro Care educational program will be useful guidance for healthcare professionals.

title: EP15.06 TESTING COMMERCIALLY AVAILABLE TOPICAL SKIN CARE PRODUCTS FOR THEIR EFFECT ON TUMOR TREATING FIELDS (TTFIELDS) THERAPY ARRAY ADHESIVENESS AND ELECTRIC CURRENTS DELIVERY
authors: M Sadovnik; S Zbidat; M Sellevoll; S Edelstein; G Lavy-Shahaf; R Blatt; I Tzchori; A Klein-Goldberg; A Haber; M Giladi; U Weinberg; Y Palti
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Tumor Treating Fields (TTFields) therapy is an approved treatment for glioblastoma (for newly diagnosed and recurrent), pleural mesothelioma, and metastatic non-small cell lung carcinoma. TTFields therapy is delivered to patients continuously via skin-adherent arrays, creating an inherent risk of skin irritation. To maintain patient quality-of-life and increase treatment effectiveness by preserving device usage time, proactive measures should be taken for management of skin adverse events (AEs). The goal of this study was to identify which commercially available topical skin care products may be used to alleviate device-related skin irritation without compromising treatment effectiveness.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
We tested the effect of topical skin care products on array adhesiveness (by measuring the force needed to peel off the array) and on electric current delivery. We selected for examination products that are recommended for preserving good skin health or are customary for the treatment of skin AEs, including skin barriers, topical corticosteroids, anti-itching products, wound healing agents, topical antimicrobials, and moisturizers. We performed a wide screen in animal models on 34 compounds, and then validated the results in healthy humans for 8 of the compounds.
RESULTS
The preclinical tests identified 24 compounds that did not interfere with array adhesiveness or electric current delivery, coming from the various medical use groups. The products that were determined to potentially interfere with TTFields delivery contained an electrical insulator/lipid component as the major ingredient. The human study corroborated the preclinical results.
CONCLUSION
To properly manage skin AEs in patients treated with TTFields therapy, topical skin care products should be selected that do not compromise TTFields delivery. This study provides a selection of such commercially available products.

title: EP17.01 LAMBERT-EATON MYASTHENIC SYNDROME ASSOCIATED WITH ANTI-HU AND ANTI-SOX1 ANTIBODIES IN SMALL-CELL LUNG CANCER: A CHALLENGING NEUROIMMUNO-ONCOLOGICAL MANAGEMENT
authors: A Gonzalez-Martinez; B Hernández Marín; A Alfranca; C Luque Cárdenas; C Albalat; S Trillo; Á Ximénez-Carrillo; J Alonso; F Sánchez-Madrid; J Vivancos
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome (LEMS) is a rare paraneoplastic autoimmune disorder affecting neuromuscular transmission, most commonly associated with small-cell lung cancer (SCLC). Although anti-voltage-gated calcium channel (VGCC) antibodies are present in the majority of cases, their absence does not rule out the diagnosis. The presence of anti-Hu and anti-SOX1 antibodies supports a paraneoplastic origin and may indicate broader neurological involvement. However, whether follow-up antibody titers correlate with clinical evolution remains unclear.
METHODS
We present a case report of a patient with suspected LEMS, detailing the clinical presentation, complementary tests and serial measurements of onconeuronal antibody titers.
RESULTS
A 76-year-old man presented with one month of progressive general deterioration, including proximal muscle weakness impairing both ambulation and upper limb elevation, dysarthria, dysphagia for solids, dysphonia, resting dyspnea, severe asthenia, cognitive impairment, weight loss, imbalance-type dizziness. Electromyography showed severe neuromuscular transmission dysfunction in the right periorbital muscles and a greater than 10% decrement in low-frequency repetitive stimulation of distal muscles. Onconeuronal antibodies revealed positive anti-Hu (+++) and anti-SOX1(+++). Thoracic imaging identified a right hilar mass, confirmed as stage IV SCLC. A diagnosis of probable LEMS was established and the patient was treated with pyridostigmine, high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone, and five sessions of plasmapheresis, followed by systemic chemotherapy using carboplatin (AUC 3) and gemcitabine (1000 mg/m² biweekly) resulting in mild clinical improvement with a decrease in SOX-1 and Hu antibody levels. Within the subsequent six months, the patient suffered a left proximal segment middle cerebral artery ischemic stroke, successfully treated with mechanical thrombectomy, complicated by early seizures and a right lower limb hemorrhage, leading to the withdrawal of anticoagulation. At present, the patient continues in partial response, and persistent imbalance-type dizziness and fatigue.
CONCLUSIONS
This case highlights the co-occurrence of anti-Hu and anti-SOX1 antibodies in a patient with paraneoplastic LEMS associated with SCLC with a notable correlation between decreasing antibody titers and partial neurological improvement following immunomodulatory therapy and chemotherapy with succesfully treated systemic complications achieving oncological partial response at six months. These findings underscore the importance of early recognition of paraneoplastic syndromes, comprehensive antibody profiling with longitudinal follow-up, and a multidisciplinary approach to optimize outcomes.

title: EP17.02 EFFECT OF RADIOTERAPY ON PSYCHOPATHOLOGY IN BRAIN TUMORS: PRELIMINARY REPORTS.
authors: C Calderoni; L Dinapoli; A Simonetti; A Restaino; F Bardi; A Gambacorta; D Chieffo; G Sani
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Radiotherapy might trigger mood, anxiety, and psychotic disorders, on the other hand,radiotherapy-related factors can confer resilience against psychopathology. Nevertheless, the behavioral consequences of radiotherapy in brain tumors are poorly investigated. Aims: To investigate the characteristics of subjects with brain tumors and compared them to those related tosubjects who already terminated radiotherapy.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
Twenty subjects with brain tumors who were undergoing radiotherapy (RAD+) and 20 subjects that concluded radiotherapy (RAD-) underwent a comprehensive psychiatric evaluation including depressive, anxious and manic symptoms, suicidal ideation, agitation, impulsivity, resilience, pain perception. Comparisons between RAD+ and RAD- included socio-demographical and clinical characteristics and psychiatric ratingscales. Chi square tests and Mann-Whitney tests were used for comparisons.
RESULTS
Subjects did not differ in gender, age, education, type and severity of brain tumor, type of psychiatric diagnosis and number of medications assumed. RAD+ and RAD- did not differ in term of depressive symptoms. RAD+ showed lower levels of anxiety, agitation, impulsivity and suicidal ideation than RAD-. Limitations: The small sample size and the heterogeneity of brain tumors investigated hampered the generalizability of the results Conclusion: Radiotherapy might represent a protective factor against development of psychopathology insubjects with brain tumors. Such protective factor might surge for the effect of chemotherapy-related setting perse or be a direct consequence of possible direct effect of the treatment.

title: EP17.03 LONGITUDINAL OBSERVATION AND SURGICAL OUTCOME OF SELLAR PARAGANGLIOMA
authors: C YANG
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Paraganglioma in the sellar region is an extremely rare entity, with a limited number of cases reported in the literature. Due to the paucity of clinical evidence, the diagnosis and treatment of paragangliomas in the sellar region remain challenging.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
Herein, we reported a case of sellar paraganglioma with parasellar and suprasellar extension. Particularly, the dynamic evolution of this benign tumor within a 7-year longitudinal observation was presented. Additionally, the relevant literature regarding sellar paraganglioma was comprehensively reviewed.
RESULTS
A 70-year-old woman presented with progressive visual deterioration and headache. Brain magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a mass in the sellar region with parasellar and suprasellar extension. The patient refused surgical treatment. Seven years later, brain magnetic resonance imaging showed the lesion significantly progressed. Neurological examination revealed bilateral tubular contraction of visual fields. Laboratory examinations showed endocrine hormone levels were normal. Surgical decompression was performed via a subfrontal approach, and subtotal resection was achieved. Histopathological examination confirmed a diagnosis of paraganglioma. Postoperatively, she developed hydrocephalus, and ventriculoperitoneal shunting was performed. Eight months later, cranial CT showed no recurrence of the residual tumor, and the hydrocephalus had been relieved.
CONCLUSION
Paraganglioma occurring in the sellar region is rare, and the preoperative differential diagnosis is difficult. Owing to the infiltration to the cavernous sinus and internal carotid, complete surgical resection is usually impracticable. There has been no consensus regarding postoperative adjuvant radiochemotherapy for the tumor residue. In-situ recurrence and metastasis have been reported in the literature, and close follow-up is warranted.

title: EP17.04 SURGICAL REMOVAL OF THORACIC EPIDURAL EWING SARCOMA WITH DOUBLE DOOR LAMINOPLASTY
authors: A Fjerza
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Intraspinal Ewing’s sarcoma lesions are rare occurrences. Limited clinical research exists regarding the surgical treatment options and prognosis of these tumors. We report a case of thoracic extradural Ewing’s sarcoma in a 14-year-old-girl, where we performed the double door laminoplasty technique for the removal of the tumor.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
The 14-year-old patient had a progressive neck and shoulder pain of a duration of one month. Her body examination showed a rapidly progressive severe paraparesis and hypoesthesia from Th6 in both legs. Her MRI revealed a sizable paravertebral mass located at the Th3 level on the right side, displaying extension along the rib and into the spinal canal through the neuroforamen. The portion from Th2 to Th4 (intraspinal extradural) exhibited a conspicuous space-occupying effect, leading to substantial compression of the spinal cord and signaling myelopathy. Due to the clinical and imaging findings, we opted for an immediate spinal decompression and tumor resection. To maintain the stability after operation, we performed a double door laminoplasty from Th2 to Th4. The block comprising the three laminae was gradually separated from the underlying tumor and extracted en bloc. Residual tumor fragments from the extracted laminae were carefully removed with the intention of reinsertion. Since the three removed laminae did not exhibit osseous infiltration or destruction, we reinserted them. The diagnosis was confirmed histologically. The patient had a significant reduction of the pain and improvement in her neurological deficits. The adjuvant therapy was started 3 weeks after the operation.
RESULTS
The open door laminoplasty technique has been previously used to treat cervical spondylotic myelopathy. We adapted it successfully for this thoracic case. Neither spinal malalignment nor displacement of bone flap (laminoplasty flap) were observed on postoperative examinations. No complications were encountered.
CONCLUSION
Ewing’s sarcoma typically affects children and young adults. However, the exact prevalence of extradural thoracic Ewing sarcoma remains unknown due to its rarity. It is impossible to definitively conclude which surgical modality is the best for these cases, but our case shows that a tumor resection with double door laminoplasty can be an optimal mode of treatment.

title: EP17.05 CAPECITABINE-INDUCED ACUTE NEUROTOXICITY IN CHARCOT-MARIE-TOOTH DISEASE: CASE REPORT AND MINI-SYSTEMATIC REVIEW
authors: V Prasad; M Ebrahim; R Malek Abdelsayed
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT) is a hereditary neuropathy with variable severity, commonly affecting motor and sensory peripheral nerves. In oncology, chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) presents a significant challenge in CMT patients, especially when treated with neurotoxic agents such as oxaliplatin. However, the safety of fluoropyrimidines, particularly capecitabine, in this population is not well characterised. We present a case of early-onset severe neurotoxicity in a CMT patient treated with capecitabine, followed by a mini-systematic literature review.
MATERIALS AND METHODS
A 51-year-old woman with genetically confirmed CMT1A (PMP22 duplication) and stage III colon adenocarcinoma underwent right hemicolectomy. Due to neuropathy concerns, oxaliplatin was omitted, and she was started on single-agent capecitabine at a 30% dose reduction (875 mg/m²). Within 72 hours of initiation, she developed profound motor weakness. Capecitabine was immediately discontinued, and symptoms rapidly resolved. A mini-systematic review was conducted to evaluate reported capecitabine neurotoxicity in CMT.
RESULTS
The patient’s rapid-onset quadriparesis reversed within 48 hours of stopping capecitabine. Neurological examination showed no permanent sequelae. She later tolerated 11 cycles of 5-FU/leucovorin and 8 cycles of FOLFIRI without recurrent neurotoxicity. A targeted review of the literature identified around 40 published cases documenting severe neurotoxicity in CMT patients treated with agents such as vincristine, paclitaxel, and cisplatin. Schneider et al. (2017) and Beutler et al. (2014) associated rare variants in CMT-related genes (e.g., SBF2, PRX) with increased susceptibility to taxane-induced neuropathy, even in the absence of overt CMT. Yerushalmi et al. (2007) described irreversible cisplatin-induced neuropathy in a CMT1A patient, whereas Cowie & Barrett (2001) reported safe use in another, highlighting inter-individual variability. Ibañez-Juliá et al. (2018) emphasised the importance of early detection and proposed the SUN-CMT checklist for clinical screening. No prior reports have documented acute, reversible motor neuropathy due to capecitabine in a genetically confirmed CMT patient.
CONCLUSION
Capecitabine may cause acute and reversible neurotoxicity in patients with Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, even at reduced doses. Thorough neurological assessment, individualised chemotherapy planning, and multidisciplinary management are essential for minimising treatment-related harm in this population. The absence of specific guidelines for oncological treatment in hereditary neuropathies calls for further prospective studies. Incorporating tools such as the EORTC QLQ-CIPN20 into routine practice may facilitate early detection and intervention for neurotoxicity in high-risk patients.

Within 72 hours of initiation, she developed profound motor weakness. Capecitabine was immediately discontinued, and symptoms rapidly resolved. A mini-systematic review was conducted to evaluate reported capecitabine neurotoxicity in CMT.
RESULTS
The patient’s rapid-onset quadriparesis reversed within 48 hours of stopping capecitabine. Neurological examination showed no permanent sequelae. She later tolerated 11 cycles of 5-FU/leucovorin and 8 cycles of FOLFIRI without recurrent neurotoxicity. A targeted review of the literature identified around 40 published cases documenting severe neurotoxicity in CMT patients treated with agents such as vincristine, paclitaxel, and cisplatin. Schneider et al. (2017) and Beutler et al. (2014) associated rare variants in CMT-related genes (e.g., SBF2, PRX) with increased susceptibility to taxane-induced neuropathy, even in the absence of overt CMT. Yerushalmi et al. (2007) described irreversible cisplatin-induced neuropathy in a CMT1A patient, whereas Cowie & Barrett (2001) reported safe use in another, highlighting inter-individual variability. Ibañez-Juliá et al. (2018) emphasised the importance of early detection and proposed the SUN-CMT checklist for clinical screening. No prior reports have documented acute, reversible motor neuropathy due to capecitabine in a genetically confirmed CMT patient.
CONCLUSION
Capecitabine may cause acute and reversible neurotoxicity in patients with Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, even at reduced doses. Thorough neurological assessment, individualised chemotherapy planning, and multidisciplinary management are essential for minimising treatment-related harm in this population. The absence of specific guidelines for oncological treatment in hereditary neuropathies calls for further prospective studies. Incorporating tools such as the EORTC QLQ-CIPN20 into routine practice may facilitate early detection and intervention for neurotoxicity in high-risk patients.

title: EP18.01 GLOBAL COLLABORATION TO SUPPORT THE TRANSLATION OF BRAIN TUMOUR THERAPIES: EARLY IMPACT AND LEARNINGS FROM A NOVEL THERAPEUTICS ACCELERATOR.
authors: C K Aitken; K Bushby; C Goetz; N Huskens; D Kobayashi; R K Mathew; K Noble; R Plummer; R Rahman; A Romero
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Researchers developing novel therapies for brain tumours must navigate numerous challenges, including selection of suitable preclinical studies, safety, clinical trial design, evolving regulatory landscapes, and securing sustained funding. To address these barriers and accelerate progress, the Brain Tumour Research Novel Therapeutics Accelerator (BTR-NTA) was launched in 2023. The BTR-NTA is an international therapeutics accelerator offering structured, independent, multidisciplinary input to support and de-risk the development of novel therapies for brain tumours. The BTR-NTA Committee comprises experts spanning discovery science, preclinical and clinical development, regulatory, manufacturing, and patient involvement. Supported by Brain Tumour Research, participation in BTR-NTA is free for academic groups.
MATERIAL AND METHODS
Industry and academic researchers at any stage of therapeutic development may submit their therapy for a BTR-NTA review. The Committee select eight therapies each year to receive up to 240 hours of expert input, including detailed assessment of the therapies’ strengths, identification of potential risks, and guidance on next steps. Central to the process is an in-person meeting with each research group and the BTR-NTA Committee, during which the proposed therapy is constructively discussed in a collaborative setting. This supportive model aims to strengthen therapies’ translational potential and clinical readiness.
RESULTS
Since its inception, the accelerator has received 29 requests for support from international groups developing new brain tumour therapies. Eleven therapies have been progressed to full review, and 37 multidisciplinary experts have provided input and guidance. One hundred percent of participants reported intentions to refine their research and development strategy based on BTR-NTA input, and 86% gained new insights or ideas previously unconsidered. Early indicators of BTR-NTA’s downstream impact include successful follow-on funding, strategic redesign of therapeutic approaches, and the formation of new patient involvement partnerships. In addition, the programme has identified recurring challenges across translational programmes that are now being synthesised to inform and benefit the broader neuro-oncology community.
CONCLUSION
The BTR-NTA provides a novel, structured approach to support researchers developing brain tumour therapies. Early results highlight the value of multidisciplinary input in strengthening translational strategies and accelerating progress toward clinical impact in neuro-oncology.
